chapters.title: Chapter 351: The Young Pendragon II
paragraphs: With the second strike, the enemy’s blade shook again with even more force and even cracked.
Only one more strike and this Cindari’s blade would definitely break! But before the third strike, the Cindari Mage sent another wave.
Seris was forced to retreat, and for a moment she only breathed.
Fifteen seconds.
Maybe less, and that was all she had, then she heard a rough sound from behind.
She thought one of the other Undead had appeared behind her, she turned around and what she saw surprised her.
One.
It had attacked two of the Cindari!
It raised the front half of its body, one of its legs was not working properly and its stomach was losing more blood with every movement.
Lian had told it to stay alive, not fight, just stay alive, but apparently One also had a very strange understanding of simple orders, just like its owner.
’This creature is stupid just like its owner.’ Seris said in her mind.
At the moment she was distracted, the Cindari that could control the Roots suddenly separated from the Formation and moved directly toward the Cocoon.
Seris moved, but the Swordmaster appeared in front of her.
The blades collided and she was trapped.
The Cindari moved a few more meters forward and then a heavy impact was heard, One slammed directly into the Undead’s body.
Its speed was nothing compared to before, its strength had also decreased, but it was enough to change the Undead’s path and both of them were dragged several meters across the ground.
Seris was truly surprised for a moment, then the Ancient Swordmaster brought its Blade down again.
The young Pendragon blocked, kicked with her healthy leg, created some distance and then her eyes stayed on One for a moment.
"Hey, don’t die." She herself had never thought she would say something like this to an ant.
One made a short, rough sound and weakly moved its antennae.
Seris turned back and held her Blade in front of the Swordmaster.
"He’s going to kill me if we both die." She whispered, but one second later she realized what she had said and that it made no sense at all.
"No."
[King’s Breaker.]
Her sword struck the enemy’s defense.
"The first ones to die will be us."
The second strike and then the third strike broke the Swordmaster’s temporary Barrier.
One charged again, this time the Undead with the largest body blocked its path.
The two huge bodies crashed into each other.
Seris jumped over One’s broken armor, her boot touched her Companion’s back for a moment.
One moved its body and threw her higher, and she spun in the air, her target was the Cindari Mage.
[King’s Execution.]
The blade moved toward the Undead’s neck with terrible speed.
The Mage pulled its head back, but it was too late, the Blade cut from the side of its neck down to its shoulder.
A deep cut appeared, the dry flesh opened but there was almost no blood, only a few very dark drops came out.
Seris landed and the Mage raised its hand at the same moment.
It was as if the deep Slash on its neck did not exist at all.
"Really? You don’t even die?" The young Pendragon looked at it in disbelief.
They did not fight like living creatures, bleeding did not matter, they did not feel pain.
They did not go into Shock, to stop them, she had to destroy their bodies in a way that made them unable to move anymore.
And doing that against Levels 34 to 38, in Seris’s current condition, was impossible, the only reason she was still alive and had been able to last this long was because of her Holy Rank Skill.
Otherwise, how could an Awakener like her, who had already been injured almost to death before this battle, fight five Level 35 creatures?
Did that even make sense?
But there was still one person who had almost not entered the battle, Cindar Vael and at that moment the Founder slowly started to come down.
Not toward Seris but toward the Cocoon and the young girl immediately blocked his path.
[Moonless Severance.]
The Attack Line appeared.
But Cindar did not even have a sword, he only moved his head a few centimeters to the side, the Slash passed beside his dry face.
A thin line appeared on his cheek and for the first time Seris managed to get his attention.
Cindar took his eyes away from the Cocoon, his golden eyes fixed directly on the girl.
There was no emotion, no surprise, no anger in them and only a cold evaluation.
Then he raised his hand, he did not seem to plan to use any Skill but all of Seris’s senses screamed at her to move.
She threw her body to the right, one moment later the place where she had been standing sank.
The ground and stones in an area of several meters were suddenly pressed several meters down, as if an invisible hand from the sky had crushed that place.
She looked at the hole with one eye and then at Cindar.
"So you are the real trouble."
Cindar moved his hand again, Seris immediately gathered all the strength she had.
But suddenly her Mana Channels burned like hot strings inside her body, and terrible pain spread through her body.
And the System gave a warning.
[Safe Duration Exceeded.]
[Muscle Fiber Damage Increasing.]
[Mana Channel Stress: Severe.]
Seris closed it, she did not have time to read the warning, if she retreated because of the pain, all of them would die.
She took two steps and jumped, then the invisible pressure behind her crushed the ground.
She landed on a huge Root, but suddenly the Swordmaster came from above and the girl blocked.
The next moment another Cindari appeared from below and she was forced to kick it away and create distance.
[Thousand Petal Swordstorm.]
Dozens of Slashes cleared the path, but her body was no longer responding like before, the muscles of her right leg had started shaking and her left hand hurt when holding the hilt.
Her one-eyed vision had also made her Depth Perception worse.
And finally, for the first time, she miscalculated one of the Swordmaster’s Slashes.
The edge of the Blade struck her shoulder, a new wound opened and blood ran down her arm.
Seris stepped back and almost fell, her only Holy Skill was still active but because its safe usage time had ended, it had itself become a problem.
She felt heavy physical and mental pressure and could collapse at any moment, but at the same time she could not turn the Skill off or she would be slaughtered immediately.
Then her healthy eye fell on the Cocoon.
Lian was there, she did not know exactly what he was doing, she did not know if his plan would work or not, but this was the last thing that mattered.
If she surrendered now, all their efforts would become meaningless.
She took a black, sphere-like object out of her Storage Space.
[Sovereign’s Last Stand.]
[Rank: S]
This was her 18th birthday gift, one of the most powerful Artifacts of her family, and her biggest trump card.
It was not a one-time-use item but each time she used it, its energy had to be filled again and filling its energy could require the cores of at least ten thousand Monsters.
Then she activated it.
The power did not enter her body like an explosion, and no huge aura appeared, instead only a very thin line of silver and golden light appeared around her body.
But Seris felt the difference immediately, the World became slower, not really, but she had become faster.
The power returned to the muscles that had been falling apart only a few seconds ago.
Her mind became sharper, the pain moved back, as if she could no longer feel the pain and all her focus was placed on the battle, it was working like a drug.
The Ancient Swordmaster attacked.
This time Seris saw the Blade, not only did she see it, she also guessed its next path!
Block.
The metals collided and she slid her Blade along it, the Counter strike hit the Undead’s face and a line opened from its forehead to its cheek.
Another Cindari came from the left and Seris moved one step aside, the fist passed beside her and her sword went under its arm.
Slash.
Another one of them sent a Root Spear from behind and the young Pendragon turned her body without looking and the spear passed beside her.
[King’s Breaker.]
The Barrier of the Cindari that had sent the spear broke.
On the other side, the Mage prepared a Fire Spell to send at her but—
[Moonless Severance.]
The Attack Line appeared directly on its arm, the Undead’s arm was cut off from the elbow.

chapters.title: Chapter 352: The Young Pendragon III
paragraphs: For a few seconds, Seris was truly moving between the five enemies, not at a level where she could defeat them.
But at a level where they could no longer freely pass by her, she was fighting five Undead between Levels 35 and 38 all by herself!
If the World knew about something like this, a huge wave of shock would shake the World! Fighting creatures like this at her Level was a great achievement, something almost without equal.
It was almost a picture of what she would become after Evolution, her potential was monstrously endless.
But could she really pass the First Evolution? Seris was not sure
and for a moment her mind returned to the day she reached Level 20.
When she received the Quest, for the first time she truly thought the System was joking with her.
That was why she had not told Lian, not because she did not trust him, at least that was what she had told herself, but because her Quest was insane and impossible.
The Swordmaster attacked again and she answered as well.
But between all those movements, an annoying question entered her mind, why was she really still here?
Main Quest? Of course.
If Black Silence reached Earth, their entire World would be in danger.
Selina? Yes.
She was a Human and Seris had no intention of allowing the Cindari to turn her body into a Vessel.
But if she was completely honest, there was another reason too.
Lian.
And accepting this part bothered her more than the pain of her wounds, she did not like caring too much about other people.
Caring made decisions weaker, it forced a person to take risks for things that did not make sense.
Lian had entered her life almost without permission, argued with her, made her angry several times, ignored her orders.
He had made decisions that Seris thought were stupid.
He had saved her, trusted her and worse, he had made Seris trust him too.
She had always thought trust meant willingly putting a weakness into someone else’s hands.
Now she understood that something worse also existed.
Trusting someone so much that even without knowing what their plan was, you were willing to stand against five Undead just because he had said,
"I won’t take long."
Seris became so angry at this thought that her next strike was much stronger than it needed to be.
The Swordmaster was pushed back several meters.
"When we’re done here...you’ll explain this." Seris said under her breath.
She slammed King’s Breaker into the nearest Undead.
She did not want to consider another possibility, that maybe they would really die today, because that possibility was useless right now.
The sound of One caught her attention, the ant slipped across the ground, its stomach had opened again but it still tried to stand.
The Undead that could control the Roots raised its hand, a very thick Root Spear came out of the ground.
Seris saw its path, directly toward her, she moved her healthy leg back and prepared to dodge.
But at the same moment, the Mage covered the right side with fire.
The Swordmaster was on the left, and Cindar was behind her! They surrounded her from every direction to make sure this attack would succeed!
She was trapped for a fraction of a second and the Root Spear was fired, she had no way to retreat unless she used force.
But the Cindari had also blocked her way with force!
However, before the spear hit her, something appeared in front of Seris.
One.
"No—" Her only eye widened.
The Root Spear went directly into One’s side, passed through its broken armor, went through its body, and came out from the other side.
This time One’s sound was not even a roar... just a short, muffled sound, its huge body stayed on the Spear for a moment.
Then the Root was pulled back and the ant fell to the ground.
"One!" Seris immediately looked at it.
There was no answer, its antennae were still, its legs were still and dark blood quickly gathered under its body.
For one second, there was no movement... the young Pendragon truly felt something drop inside her chest.
"One!"
Again, nothing.
Then...one of its legs moved very weakly, its right antenna shook, once...it was alive but barely, in a very thin space between life and death.
Seris did not know why seeing this scene made her angrier than losing her own eye.
Maybe because One was not her own creature, it was Lian’s Companion and when Lian came out, he was supposed to see this.
"I’ll kill all of you!" She tightened her grip on her sword, her anger became stronger, today was one of the worst days of her life.
And every moment it was getting worse and worse and she was becoming more and more angry.
She pulled up all the Mana she had left.
[Thousand Petal Swordstorm.]
This time the Skill was not beautiful, it was not controlled either, it was violent., hundreds of Sword Aura burst out from around Seris like a real storm.
The ground under her feet was covered with cuts, the Roots were torn into pieces.
The biggest Cindari had to raise its arms in front of its body, the Swordmaster took several steps back and the Mage was directly in the main path.
The first Slash cut one of its legs, the second passed through its shoulder and the third cut off its remaining arm.
The fourth opened a large part of its side, the Undead fell to the ground but still moved, without one arm, with its shoulder split open and without any reaction to pain.
"Damn..." Seris said with hate, her breathing became heavy.
"They don’t even die." Even the fact that she had managed to come this far was already beyond what she had expected.
The light of Swordheart Overdrive went out at that moment.
[Swordheart Overdrive Terminated.]
[Severe Muscular Damage Detected.]
[Multiple Mana Channel Tears Detected.]
Seris lost her balance, and this was exactly the moment the Swordmaster had been waiting for.
The Blade moved.
The girl barely pulled herself back but the blade passed through her side, creating a deep wound on her body.
Blood sprayed and she moved several more steps back.
Another Cindari sent a thin strand out of the ground and cut her healthy leg, Seris fell onto one knee.
The half-destroyed Mage made a Spell with its remaining hand, fire hit her back and the smell of burning armor and skin rose into the air.
And before she could stand up, Cindar raised his hand, pressure came down and the young Pendragon was slammed into the ground with her whole body.
She heard one of her ribs crack...then a second one and blood spilled from her mouth onto the ground, everything became blurry for a few seconds.
Only her healthy eye had become blurry, she took a hard breath, Sovereign’s Last Stand was still active.
But her Life Force was being consumed, her body could no longer handle the output.
Seris put her hand on the ground and stood up, not because she did not feel pain, she did.
Every breath, every movement, every muscle contraction, but there was still a distance between the five Undead and the Cocoon.
So it was not over yet.

chapters.title: Chapter 353: Seris’ Evolution Quest!
paragraphs: The Swordmaster came forward and she raised her sword, but Cindar passed by her and went directly toward the Cocoon.
The other four Undead saw Seris as an enemy.
Cindar did not, in his eyes Seris was not even an enemy, just an obstacle, something that needed to be removed from his path.
She pushed herself off the ground, no matter what it took, she would not let this bastard reach the Cocoon!
[Moonless Severance.]
Cindar turned his head slightly and at that moment the Slash landed on his cheek.
A deeper line appeared than before, he stopped and for the second time his eyes looked directly at the Human girl.
"You’re not going anywhere." Seris said coldly and very directly.
The Founder raised his hand, the invisible pressure was much stronger this time and the young Pendragon held her sword with both hands in front of her body.
The force came down on the Blade, the ground under her feet cracked and her knees bent.
Her injured thigh almost gave out, her other leg was also shaking but she did not move back, not even one centimeter.
"Hold on!" There was only one sentence in her mind.
The pressure became stronger and fresh blood came down from Seris’s nose, the muscles in her arms were almost torn apart.
"Not even one step, I won’t let you go toward the Cocoon!" The veins in her hands tore one after another and her muscles were crushed.
She could feel the terrible pain caused by the pressure crushing her bones.
And at that exact moment, the ground shook, at first she thought it was another Skill from Cindar, but the pressure suddenly stopped.
Cindar lowered his hand.
Seris looked in surprise, the other four Undead had also stopped at the same time.
The Swordmaster had lowered its Blade, the other one had stopped the Roots, the Mage had left its Spell unfinished.
They were all looking in the same direction.
The Cocoon.
Then the second shake came and this time the entire Forgotten Tree shook, the huge branches hundreds of meters above made loud sounds.
The ground around the Roots cracked open, the fog from the lower Dead Zone was pushed away.
The young Pendragon looked at the Cocoon, the surface of the Cocoon was now completely closed, there was no sign left of the opening Lian had entered through.
Selina was lying unconscious several meters away.

Golden.
Black.
Then the black became stronger.
THUMP.
The vibration moved from the Cocoon into the ground.

The Mana in the environment started to change direction, not only the Mana around the Forgotten Tree, something from far away was also being pulled in.
As if the Realm itself was feeding the Cocoon.
The five Undead slowly changed their positions, not to attack but to stand in a half-circle in front of the Cocoon.
None of them knelt, but their Formation looked like something similar to a Guard of Honor.
Seris looked at them for several seconds.
Then she understood, they had not come to kill Lian, at least not at this moment, they had not come to stop something either.
The opposite.
They had come to protect the Birth, to welcome it and that was what caused the worry and fear.
Because of what Lian had done inside it.
Selina was outside, which meant the first part of his plan had succeeded, but Lian himself had entered, and now the entire Forgotten Tree was shaking.
Mana from a World was being pulled toward that point.
And five creatures that should have been dead for centuries were standing in front of the Cocoon like ancient guards.
"Lian..." She said his name very quietly in her mind.
This time there was no sarcasm with it, no fake anger, only worry.
"What the hell did you do?" A few seconds later, she frowned.
The ground was shaking so hard that it was clear there was a power capable of shaking the entire World.
God knew what exactly was happening inside that Cocoon that was causing such terrible earthquakes.
Were these just normal effects of the Calamity’s Birth? Or were they the effects of something else? Like a battle between Lian’s consciousness and the Calamity?
She did not know, she was not sure, but she trusted that crazy Vorhelm, whatever was happening... it was definitely not a bad sign, right?
[Warning.]
[Calamity Is Manifesting.]
[Host Replacement Confirmed.]
[Gestation Reconstruction In Progress.]
Seris’s expression changed and a number appeared.
[Gestation Reconstruction: 97.4%]
That meant Lian had really become the Vessel and worse, the Birth had not stopped.
She held her sword tighter, her mind went to the worst possibility for a moment.
What if Lian had failed? What if he had not been able to control Black Silence? What if the Calamity was doing the same thing to him that it was supposed to do to Selina?
What if when the Cocoon opened, what came out was no longer Lian?
Seris stopped the thought immediately, not because it was impossible, but because thinking about it now would not help.
"Stay alive first." She said under her breath and it was unclear whether she was talking to herself or Lian.
"But if you really turn into a Calamity, what should I do?" She had no idea, she did not know how she was supposed to complete that damn Quest in this situation.
The same Evolution Quest, the same thing that when she had first seen it, she had thought the System was really making fun of her.
If even that man became the Vessel of the Calamity...would she still have to do it? But if she did not do it...she would never be able to go beyond the First Evolution.
[Calamity Entity Detected.]
[Quest Target Is Within Range.]
Seris’s eyes slowly moved from the panel back to the Cocoon, for the first time the meaning of the Quest truly felt heavy.
Black Silence was inside the Cocoon, but it was not only Black Silence, Lian was inside it too.
If the Birth was completed, the Calamity would be born from Lian’s body.
"What a damn joke...
The Undead continued to stand in silence.
One was lying on the ground behind Seris, with no clear movement, only its antenna shook once every few seconds.
Selina was still unconscious.
Aren was lying on the ground farther away.
And her? Almost her entire body was covered in blood, but she was still standing, at least for now she had no other choice.
Seris slowly breathed out.
THUMP.
The entire Dead Zone shook.
More Mana was pulled toward the Cocoon, the branches of the Forgotten Tree above them made loud sounds.
Why had the Quest hidden itself from Lian? Because it was strange? Because it did not want to worry him?
Maybe.
She had not told him at that time because it looked insane.
But now she had another thought.
Some Quests only become truly scary when the Target is no longer a meaningless name.
Seris locked her only healthy eye on the Cocoon, black light leaked through the Roots and the ground under her feet shook with every pulse.
THUMP.
Her heart seemed to match that same beat for a moment.
No.
She could not make a decision that she did not need to make yet.
Lian was supposed to come out, the same Lian as always.
Then Seris could blame him for this stupid plan until he regretted coming out of the Cocoon!
She did not want to do that... if he really came out himself... she could not force herself to actually complete her Evolution Quest...
But if, if something else came out...if Black Silence had taken his body...if there was no Lian left behind those eyes...
"If something other than you comes out of there..." Seris’s hand tightened around the sword hilt and her voice was so low that only she could hear it.
She raised the blood-covered blade a few centimeters.
"I’ll kill it myself."
The System showed its final message at that exact moment.
[Warning.]
[Calamity Birth Imminent.]
And directly below it, her Quest, which no longer looked funny at all, but instead looked like something she might have no choice but to complete...
[Evolution Quest: Kill The Calamity: Black Silence.]

chapters.title: Chapter 354: Memories Of A Calamity I
paragraphs: The last thing Lian remembered was a series of System messages that appeared one after another in front of his eyes in the darkness inside the Cocoon.
[Calamity Vessel Replacement Process Started.]
[New Vessel: Lian Vorhelm.]
[Gestation Process Is Being Reconstructed...]
Then everything went black.
He expected to feel the next pain.
He expected the energy of Black Silence to enter his veins, tear apart his Mana Channels, or at least for the pressure of that huge entity to cause his body to break apart from the inside.
But when he felt something again, he realized there was no pain.

Not because the pain had stopped, but because he could no longer feel his body, his fingers did not exist, he could not feel his legs, there was no chest moving up and down, there was no pulse, and he could not even feel the flow of Mana inside him.
For a moment, the only thing that remained was his consciousness, a consciousness floating in endless darkness, and a short thought passed through his mind.
"Am I dead?" He received no answer, and he doubted that was true, after all, he had an extra life, so even if he died, he should be able to return to life.
But at that exact moment, he felt something.
Hunger.
At first, Lian thought his own hunger instinct had reacted.
But this was different, very different.
The hunger he felt was not for meat, it was not for power, it was not for any of the things he knew.
An unwanted image formed in his mind.
An ocean.
Then a forest.
Mountains.
A plain.
Cities.
Billions of living creatures breathing inside a complete World.
Mana flowing through the land.
Souls.
Life.
Death.
All of them had only one meaning to whatever Lian was feeling... food.
"This hunger isn’t mine." He felt danger.
At that moment, something moved in the darkness and a System message appeared, but the edges of the words shook like a broken image.
[Foreign Memory Flow Detected.]
[Source: Black Silence.]
[Vessel’s Consciousness Has Been Pulled Into The Calamity’s Memory.]
Lian stared at the message for a moment, then the darkness in front of him broke and another World appeared.
There was no sky, or maybe there was and he could not understand it.
There was no clear ground under his feet, although he did not have feet to stand on anything either, everything was floating inside a colorless and endless space.
And in the distance, something was standing, Lian tried to look more closely, it had the shape of a creature.
Maybe.
But the more he tried to put it into a clear shape, the more the image broke apart.
He could not guess its height, it had no face, and no gender that he could recognize.
Even its body had no fixed shape, sometimes it looked like a very tall human, the next moment, it seemed as large as the sky.

And when he focused more, he even thought that maybe what he was seeing was not the creature’s real form at all, maybe his own mind had been forced to create an image for something that could not be understood.
But he could feel two things with certainty.
The first was its age.
Not the age of a thousand-year-old or ten-thousand-year-old creature.
Something much older.
So old that even the Worlds themselves seemed young compared to it.
And the second...
Hunger.
Before this, he had thought the hunger of Black Silence was huge, but now that he was facing this presence, that endless hunger even seemed small.
Around the dark presence, five other things were floating, they were not bodies, at least Lian could not call them bodies.
Five presences, five forms of existence, each with a different shape and feeling.
And he recognized one of them, the one from whose point of view he was seeing everything.
Black Silence.
And if his guess was correct, all of them should be Calamities, so there were five Calamities and that great figure should be the Father.
"So Caelus wasn’t completely crazy." Lian thought inside the darkness.
He had said the children of the Eternal Father would live forever, he had said Black Silence was one of his children.
Until then, Lian did not know whether that sentence was a religious metaphor or a real fact, now he at least had part of the answer.
Black Silence really was one of the five children of that being, that great being whose true nature was not clear at all.
But what those five Calamities were was still unknown.
Children? Creations? Pieces separated from its existence? Or something else?
The memory did not allow him to investigate further, the image broke and the World changed.
Sunlight hit Lian’s imaginary eyes, but this was not the World he had seen during the past few weeks.
There was no Dead Zone, no dead trees could be seen, the ground was not black and cracked, and the Black Silence veins were not coming out from under the ground.
The World was alive, golden plains stretched to the horizon.
Rivers of bright blue flowed between them and Mana could even be seen inside the water.
There were forests and huge cities built on cliffs, there were cities underground.
Different races moved through the streets.
Some were almost human-like, some had horns, some had skin with unusual colors, and some had wings.
Civilizations lived beside each other that made the modern Cindari look like little more than small remains compared to them.
But even all of this was small compared to what stood at the center of the World.
Primordial Root.
The tree was so huge that Lian could not see its highest branch, its branches covered a large part of the sky.
Its roots stretched thousands of kilometers through the ground.
Mana flowed through them into the entire World, underground water moved through its network of roots.
Clouds formed around its crown, forests stayed alive because of the flow of Mana that came out of it.
Without needing an explanation, he understood, this tree was not only a living creature, it was part of the structure of the World, maybe even the main reason life still existed in it.
And among all this greatness and beauty, there was also war, a bloody war that had started between several small civilizations.
Cities were burning and innocent creatures were being killed.
And in the middle of it, a lone man was kneeling beside the ruins of a burned house.
Lian recognized him.
Cindar Vael.
But he looked nothing like the legendary Founder of the Cindari.
He was younger, weaker, and his clothes were torn, his dark hair was covered with blood and dirt... his hands went under the rubble and moved the pieces of stone aside.
One.
Second.
Third.
Then he found something, a motionless hand and Cindar moved the rubble faster.
The body of a middle-aged woman was under the house, her eyes were closed, her chest was crushed... dead.
Cindar did not move for several moments, then he pulled his mother out from under the stones, but before he could see more, the memory suddenly broke.
Another image replaced it.
Graves.
Three graves beside each other.
Mother.
Father.
Younger brother.
Then the next image came, Cindar was standing beside a woman, the last person who was still beside him.
His lover.
Lian did not hear her name, or maybe Black Silence did not remember it.
But Cindar’s feelings for her were so strong that even Lian, who was only watching a memory, could feel their weight.
The woman was holding Cindar’s hand, they were running away from a city at war, screams came from behind them, the light of magic lit up the sky.
Cindar pulled her, only a few more meters, just a few more meters and they could escape.
But a wave of energy passed through the buildings behind them, he was thrown forward and when he turned around... half of a building had fallen onto the woman.
She was still alive, at least for a few seconds.
Cindar moved the stones with his blood-covered hands, the woman said something.
Lian could not hear her voice, then her eyes closed.
Cindar stopped moving, something inside him broke there, not at that exact moment, but the first crack had appeared.
The memories became faster.
Months.
Maybe years.
Cindar went from city to city, became stronger, fought, but everything he saw brought back a memory.
A mother holding her child in a market.
Their smiles.
His own mother’s face.
A couple sitting together in an inn, the woman’s hand on the man’s hand.
Seeing that scene reminded him of his lover.
Then heroes who were celebrated in the city square because they had won wars.
And the same question kept coming from Cindar, when his city was burning, where were these heroes?
And his hatred slowly took shape.
"They are all guilty." This thought passed through his mind for the first time and then became stronger.
"The ones who started the war."
"The ones who could have helped but didn’t."
"The ones who watched."
And then—
"The ones who are still alive." This last part no longer made sense, Cindar himself probably knew that.
But it did not matter.
Seeing the happiness of others reminded him of what he had lost.
And sadness became jealousy, jealousy became anger and anger became hatred!
This was hatred toward all living creatures, hatred that wanted to burn the entire World and burn everything!
But hatred without power was worthless... he had no power to take revenge...
One night, he fell asleep on the ruins of an abandoned temple.
And he dreamed.
The same colorless space, the same presence... the Father!
Cindar first tried to raise his head, but he could not, the pressure of that being’s existence forced him to his knees, not with power but simply with its presence.
No voice was heard, but the words formed directly inside his mind.
"What do you want?"
"Power." Cindar hesitated, was he dreaming? A stupid dream? But in any case, he answered.
"No." The answer came immediately.
"What? I am sure I know what I want, and that is power!"
"That is not what you want." The presence paused and then slowly said.

And the same question kept coming from Cindar, when his city was burning, where were these heroes?
And his hatred slowly took shape.
"They are all guilty." This thought passed through his mind for the first time and then became stronger.
"The ones who started the war."
"The ones who could have helped but didn’t."
"The ones who watched."
And then—
"The ones who are still alive." This last part no longer made sense, Cindar himself probably knew that.
But it did not matter.
Seeing the happiness of others reminded him of what he had lost.
And sadness became jealousy, jealousy became anger and anger became hatred!
This was hatred toward all living creatures, hatred that wanted to burn the entire World and burn everything!
But hatred without power was worthless... he had no power to take revenge...
One night, he fell asleep on the ruins of an abandoned temple.
And he dreamed.
The same colorless space, the same presence... the Father!
Cindar first tried to raise his head, but he could not, the pressure of that being’s existence forced him to his knees, not with power but simply with its presence.
No voice was heard, but the words formed directly inside his mind.
"What do you want?"
"Power." Cindar hesitated, was he dreaming?
A stupid dream?
But in any case, he answered.
"No." The answer came immediately.
"What?
I am sure I know what I want, and that is power!"
"That is not what you want." The presence paused and then slowly said.

chapters.title: Chapter 355: Memories Of A Calamity II
paragraphs: Cindar did not understand what this higher being meant for a few moments, but suddenly images appeared in front of him.
His mother.
His father.
His brother.
His lover.
"I want them back." His hands became fists, and this time his voice was lower.
The pressure in the space changed.
"Death is a small law," Father said calmly.
For a moment, Cindar even forgot to breathe, and the sentence continued.
"Small laws can be broken with enough power."
"Can you bring them back?"
"You can, if you are willing to pay the price for that power." The answer from that being was not what he expected.
"What do you want?" Cindar did not even ask if there was a price he would not be willing to pay.
The colorless space changed for a moment, and an image of the world appeared beneath him.
Oceans.
Forests.
Cities.
The Primordial Root and billions of living beings.
"The world you hate, offer it to me."
Even Lian, who was only watching the memory, expected Cindar to hesitate for longer, this was sacrificing an entire world! It was insane!
But he did not, and only asked.
"How?"
Five presences appeared around Father.
"One of my five children will enter your world."
One of the shadows moved forward ... Black Silence.
"You will open the door, you will be the anchor."
"And in return?" Cindar did not take his eyes away from the black presence.
"Every death it causes will make you stronger." An image of living beings appeared, one after another going silent.
"Every life that is devoured." Cities went dark.
"Every soul." An entire world became dark.
"Every world that falls apart." Then the image of Cindar’s family appeared again.
"Until the day your power is enough to break the law of death."
"I accept." Cindar stared for a long time and then only said that, he did not know if he was dreaming or not, but even if it was a dream, he did not want to lose such an opportunity.
"Good. Now show me how you became the anchor." Lian immediately focused all his attention on the memory.
He was a little surprised that everything had started from hatred, revenge, and power to bring his family back, but perhaps it made sense.
And now there was something more important to see, how did this man become the anchor!
Cindar reached his hand forward, and Father also sent something toward him, but right at the moment when the main event was about to happen—
The image broke.
The voices mixed together, the memory jumped forward several hours or maybe several days, and suddenly Cindar was in a bedroom in an inn.
What needed to be done had been done.
"Damn it, did you skip the important part?" Lian almost shouted into the darkness, but no one answered.

However, the scene changed and returned to the Primordial Root, under the tree, a black and evil-looking line that gave off the smell of destruction suddenly took root, thin and almost impossible to see.
Then a second line.
A third, and then more and more...deep inside the tree, something hungry opened its eyes ...Black Silence had entered the world!
At first, no one understood anything, there was nothing to see or understand.
A small animal drank water that one of the infected roots passed under.
A few days later, the animal attacked another of its kind.
Without a reason, with unusual violence, its eyes had turned black, its teeth had become larger, its muscles had changed.
Then the hunters became infected, then the herds, then the creatures that could use Mana, and finally ... intelligent beings.
But the infection in them was different, Black Silence was not creating something new.
It took what already existed and twisted it in the worst possible way.
In an animal, hunger became a desire to kill, fear became constant terror, and the instinct to survive became blind violence.
In intelligent beings, doubt, hatred, jealousy, anger, fear, everything became stronger.
A city that had traded with its neighboring city for centuries suddenly became convinced that its neighbors were planning to attack.
A commander killed his own soldier for a betrayal he had never committed.
A mother, in her madness, saw her own child as an enemy.
Mages used their spells on civilians.
Allied rulers accused each other.
Small wars started burning ... then they became bigger, and then the world started eating itself.
Plants were not safe either, trees twisted, roots hunted living creatures.
Mana beasts turned into monsters that later generations did not even know had once been normal animals.

Lian now understood, Black Silence was not a disease, it was not a curse, at least not in the normal sense, it was something that found the inner decay of every living being and grew it until it consumed their entire existence.
And while the world became weaker, Cindar became stronger.
Lian could feel it in the memory, every time a creature affected by Black Silence died, something was added to the Calamity.
And a very small part of that power returned to Cindar through the Anchor Link.
First, his body changed, becoming faster, stronger, and more resistant, then his Mana capacity grew, after that his lifespan, and then he gained abilities that he could not even imagine before.
A man who was once only a defeated warrior slowly became one of the most powerful beings in the world.
But the more disgusting part was something else, people loved him.
Cindar appeared to be fighting against the infection, he killed infected monsters, saved cities, and rescued caravans from being surrounded.
The more the infection spread, the stronger he became, and as a result, he performed even greater feats.
People shouted his name.
"Cindar saved us!"
Statues of him were built, children wished to become like him.
A man who had lost everything and, despite his painful past, had become one of the greatest heroes in the world.
He became a symbol and an example of hope for the world, and none of them knew that the same man had opened the door for the Calamity.
"Bastard..." Lian thought with disgust.
But not everyone had been fooled.
Aurelia stood in front of a huge map.
Lian recognized her immediately, the same woman he had seen in the memory crystal, but this Aurelia was younger and the world had not completely fallen yet.
Several black points were marked on the map, and the woman followed their paths with her finger.
This was a meeting between the most powerful beings in the world to find a way to save the world.
"These are not random."
"The infection has appeared everywhere." Another leader said.
"No, every infected area is close to one of the veins connected to the Primordial Root." Aurelia showed the Mana vein paths on the map.
There was silence.
Cindar was also standing in the same room, calm, respected, one of the most trusted heroes there.
"We need to go to the Primordial Root, maybe we can find the answer we are looking for there." The woman added at the end.
Lian could almost feel Cindar’s tension, but no one suspected him.
Even Aurelia, why would she? Cindar was one of the most loved heroes in the world, a man who had fought against the infection more than most people.
A man whose painful past had caused millions of people to see him as a sign of will and hope.
Even that woman trusted him, and that trust was what later killed almost all of them.
The investigation continued.
Until the main truth was discovered, the Primordial Root had been infected.
The decision the leaders of the world made was not simple, destroying that tree might damage the world forever.
The water cycle, the flow of Mana, the weather, part of life, everything was connected to it, but if the tree remained, Black Silence would continue to grow.
So they made their choice, the Primordial Root had to be destroyed.
The battle that happened for this was something Lian had never seen before.
Seven powerful leaders of the world stood around the Primordial Root, Aurelia in the center.
And behind the tree was its Guardian, Titan, who had not been infected at that time, a huge being that had been created to protect the Primordial Root and the flow of life in the world.
Even it took part in destroying the thing it had been created to protect, because it understood that if the Root remained, there would be no world left to protect.
Light covered the entire sky, the branches of the Primordial Root fell one after another.
The roots were cut, the Mana flows shook, and finally the heart of the tree was broken.
At that moment, Black Silence lost its Vessel, for a moment the Calamity was left in the world without a Vessel.
The leaders of the world recognized the Calamity without hesitation and, without giving it a chance, trapped it inside Titan’s body, this was a plan they had prepared beforehand.
Lian saw black material come out from thousands of broken roots, and something happened that they had not expected, Titan’s huge eyes slowly turned black.
The Guardian of the Primordial Root became the Calamity’s new prison, and then the prison started to go mad.
At first, Titan was still himself, he worked with the leaders and told them to move back.
He asked them to stop him if he lost control, but Black Silence ate away at his mind from the inside.
It changed his memories, twisted his instincts, increased his anger, and turned his pain into madness.
Until nothing remained of the old Guardian, the Infected Titan was born, and the final battle began.
The leaders of the world were actually winning, with great difficulty, with serious wounds, with losses ... but Aurelia had prepared a plan to seal the Calamity.
However, something happened that none of them expected ... Betrayal!

chapters.title: Chapter 356: Memories Of A Calamity III
paragraphs: Titan fell to one knee, the first chains were starting to form.
At first glance, it seemed that everything was finally coming to an end, Titan would be sealed, the Calamity would be imprisoned, and the world would be saved.
But right at the moment when everything could have ended—
Cindar pushed his sword through the back of one of the seven leaders, the man did not even understand what had happened.
"Why?" The blade came out of his chest and blood fell onto the ground.
"...Cindar?" Aurelia turned around, real disbelief could be seen on her face.
"I’m sorry." Cindar pulled the sword out of the leader’s body, his voice was calm, but there was no real regret in it, it was clear that he did not really care about what he was saying.
He had never planned to let the Calamity be sealed, if Black Silence was imprisoned, he would never reach his wish.
"It was you." Aurelia only looked at him for a few moments, and then it was as if the final piece of the puzzle fell into place in her mind.
"You allowed that thing to enter our world."
"I only took back something this world stole from me."
"And to take it back, you sold all of us?" Aurelia’s eyes changed for a few seconds, not only with anger but also with something like sadness.

She had known all this time that someone had betrayed them, she knew the source of this infection was beyond their world ... but she truly did not expect the traitor to be one of the world’s greatest hopes.
"If I have to, I will do anything to bring back what was taken from me." Cindar raised his sword.
His betrayal broke the balance of the battle, one of the leaders was dead, and two others were seriously injured.
Titan stood up again, and Black Silence inside him exploded with even greater force.
Aurelia understood that they could no longer kill Titan, so there was only one other way left.
She had already prepared a backup plan, she knew that any variable could happen in this decisive battle, so she was prepared.
Seven people had entered the battle, one had fallen by Cindar’s hand, but even the soul of the dead leader still answered the final seal.
Aurelia began the ritual.

This time it was not with Mana but with life, with the soul, and the first person burned himself, his body turned into light, his soul was pulled out, and a huge chain of light wrapped around Titan’s arm.
The second leader sacrificed himself too, and a chain formed around Titan’s left leg.
The third leader ... the fourth, and one after another, every chain had the price of one life, one soul, one hero.
Cindar understood what they were doing, he attacked them, but it was too late.
Aurelia was the last one remaining, her body was full of wounds, blood ran from the corner of her mouth.
But before activating the final seal, she looked at Cindar, not with hatred, and perhaps that was worse.
"You did not lose everything, Cindar, you gained the love of the world and you threw everything away yourself." Then her body turned into light and the final chain was formed.
BOOOOOOM!
Titan was slammed into the ground, seven glowing chains pinned his body deep into the Giant’s Graveyard.
Black Silence roared, not with a sound but with hunger and anger, but it could no longer move.
The Calamity was finally suppressed and Cindar was alone ... again.
For years, he tried.

With a sword, with magic, with ancient Artifacts, with forbidden rituals, with blood, with sacrifice, but the chains were not normal, they were not made with Mana, each one was a continuation of the soul of one of the leaders.
No matter how strong he became, he could not break them, and worse, Black Silence was no longer devouring anything.
So no power was reaching Cindar either, his growth stopped.
Lian now completely understood Cindar’s true motivation, he did not worship Father, Black Silence was not a goddess or a sacred being to him, all of them were tools to him.
Tools for one goal, his family, his lover, and bringing them back from death.
"So you wanted billions of beings to die just to bring back a few people." Lian whispered quietly.
Sacrificing an entire world to bring back the people he loved ... Was it worth it? He could not answer that, because he did not know what he would do in such a situation.
But sacrificing an entire world was not a joke either, especially because through this method the Calamity could reach more worlds and the number of victims could reach trillions.
Trillions of children, women, and men ... billions of families and living, intelligent beings that could love, hate, build, and destroy... they would be sacrificed just to bring back a few people?
"But is it even possible to reverse life and death and bring the dead back from death?" He did not know the answer to this question, that higher being had said it was possible.
But had it really told the truth? Or was it only a lie to control Cindar’s feelings?
He had no idea ... but one thing he was sure of, the final winners would be Father and the Black Calamity, who would achieve their goal of destroying forms of life and worlds.
And thinking about it made the hair on his body stand up and gave him a very bad and dark feeling.
One person! That being who was called Father was bringing almost an entire world to an end just by manipulating one person’s feelings ... what kind of power was that?

"Is it possible that something exactly like this happened to our world too?" He then whispered to himself, it was possible that such a scenario had also been carried out in their world and that the Calamity they had faced was one of the five Calamities.
If that was true, then it was possible that someone in their world had also betrayed them and allowed the Calamity to enter ... but who?
He looked at Cindari ... if his reasoning was correct, the traitor in their world was also one of the humans who stood at the top of the world.

"Ah, but this makes everything more complicated, then what exactly is the System? Why were we given the power to resist while the other worlds were not? And what are the real conditions for choosing an anchor?" He still had many unanswered questions.
He decided to watch the rest of the memories, maybe he could get more answers.
And the first thing he saw was Cindar’s anger and worry, Black Silence being imprisoned was not good news for him.
Every life Black Silence devoured made the Calamity stronger, every world it destroyed made its existence grow.
And part of all this growth reached Cindar through the Anchor Link.
One world.
Two worlds.
Ten worlds.
If Black Silence ate enough, Cindar really might one day reach a level where life and death were nothing more than laws he could break.
At least that was what he believed, and he tried many times to contact Father again.
In dreams... beside the remains of the Primordial Root, which had now become the Forgotten Tree.
But no answer came and years passed, and Father remained silent, but Cindar did not give up.
After decades of research, he found another way, he could not break Titan’s seven chains, but he did not need to release the Calamity all at once.
The Primordial Root had not completely disappeared, part of it had survived.
A piece that later became something the Cindari called the Forgotten Tree.
Its root network was still connected to the world, and through that network, a very weak connection to Titan also remained.
Cindar found a way.
Little by little, year by year, a very small amount of Black Silence was transferred from Titan to the tree.
So little that the chains would not react immediately, the tree became a temporary Vessel, but there was one problem.
Black Silence was hungry, even in that weak state, and to stay alive inside the tree, it started eating the tree itself.
Mana, life force, water, roots, almost everything was slowly being consumed.
And Lian finally understood the real reason why the Forgotten Tree had dried up.
"So that was it..." The tree was not dying simply because of the passage of time.
It was being eaten, and Cindar knew it, the main plan was simple, Black Silence would be transferred from Titan to the tree over centuries.
When enough of the Calamity had gathered, Cindar would awaken and become the new Vessel himself!
That was right, he planned to become the new Vessel himself, he was already the Calamity’s Anchor and had very high compatibility.
He even believed that if he was both the Anchor and the Vessel, he would gain even more power.
Then Black Silence would be released again, it would devour more worlds, Cindar would grow, until he could bring back his dead.
But such a plan could take hundreds of years, and he could not stay awake for all that time.
So he created a race.
With the help of a piece of the Primordial Root, his own blood, he caused the surviving intelligent beings of the world who were the same species as himself to undergo a kind of mutation.
Which eventually caused a new generation to be born, smarter, stronger, faster, and easier to control and manipulate.
The Cindari.
Their name came from him.

So no power was reaching Cindar either, his growth stopped.
Lian now completely understood Cindar’s true motivation, he did not worship Father, Black Silence was not a goddess or a sacred being to him, all of them were tools to him.
Tools for one goal, his family, his lover, and bringing them back from death.
"So you wanted billions of beings to die just to bring back a few people." Lian whispered quietly.
Sacrificing an entire world to bring back the people he loved ...
Was it worth it?
He could not answer that, because he did not know what he would do in such a situation.
But sacrificing an entire world was not a joke either, especially because through this method the Calamity could reach more worlds and the number of victims could reach trillions.
Trillions of children, women, and men ... billions of families and living, intelligent beings that could love, hate, build, and destroy... they would be sacrificed just to bring back a few people?
"But is it even possible to reverse life and death and bring the dead back from death?" He did not know the answer to this question, that higher being had said it was possible.
But had it really told the truth?
Or was it only a lie to control Cindar’s feelings?
He had no idea ... but one thing he was sure of, the final winners would be Father and the Black Calamity, who would achieve their goal of destroying forms of life and worlds.
And thinking about it made the hair on his body stand up and gave him a very bad and dark feeling.
One person!
That being who was called Father was bringing almost an entire world to an end just by manipulating one person’s feelings ... what kind of power was that?

"Is it possible that something exactly like this happened to our world too?" He then whispered to himself, it was possible that such a scenario had also been carried out in their world and that the Calamity they had faced was one of the five Calamities.
If that was true, then it was possible that someone in their world had also betrayed them and allowed the Calamity to enter ... but who?
He looked at Cindari ... if his reasoning was correct, the traitor in their world was also one of the humans who stood at the top of the world.
"Ah, but this makes everything more complicated, then what exactly is the System?
Why were we given the power to resist while the other worlds were not?
And what are the real conditions for choosing an anchor?" He still had many unanswered questions.
He decided to watch the rest of the memories, maybe he could get more answers.
And the first thing he saw was Cindar’s anger and worry, Black Silence being imprisoned was not good news for him.
Every life Black Silence devoured made the Calamity stronger, every world it destroyed made its existence grow.
And part of all this growth reached Cindar through the Anchor Link.
One world.
Two worlds.
Ten worlds.
If Black Silence ate enough, Cindar really might one day reach a level where life and death were nothing more than laws he could break.
At least that was what he believed, and he tried many times to contact Father again.
In dreams... beside the remains of the Primordial Root, which had now become the Forgotten Tree.
But no answer came and years passed, and Father remained silent, but Cindar did not give up.
After decades of research, he found another way, he could not break Titan’s seven chains, but he did not need to release the Calamity all at once.
The Primordial Root had not completely disappeared, part of it had survived.
A piece that later became something the Cindari called the Forgotten Tree.
Its root network was still connected to the world, and through that network, a very weak connection to Titan also remained.
Cindar found a way.
Little by little, year by year, a very small amount of Black Silence was transferred from Titan to the tree.
So little that the chains would not react immediately, the tree became a temporary Vessel, but there was one problem.
Black Silence was hungry, even in that weak state, and to stay alive inside the tree, it started eating the tree itself.
Mana, life force, water, roots, almost everything was slowly being consumed.
And Lian finally understood the real reason why the Forgotten Tree had dried up.
"So that was it..." The tree was not dying simply because of the passage of time.
It was being eaten, and Cindar knew it, the main plan was simple, Black Silence would be transferred from Titan to the tree over centuries.
When enough of the Calamity had gathered, Cindar would awaken and become the new Vessel himself!
That was right, he planned to become the new Vessel himself, he was already the Calamity’s Anchor and had very high compatibility.
He even believed that if he was both the Anchor and the Vessel, he would gain even more power.
Then Black Silence would be released again, it would devour more worlds, Cindar would grow, until he could bring back his dead.
But such a plan could take hundreds of years, and he could not stay awake for all that time.
So he created a race.
With the help of a piece of the Primordial Root, his own blood, he caused the surviving intelligent beings of the world who were the same species as himself to undergo a kind of mutation.
Which eventually caused a new generation to be born, smarter, stronger, faster, and easier to control and manipulate.
The Cindari.
Their name came from him.

chapters.title: Chapter 357: Memories Of A Calamity IV
paragraphs: The Cindari.
Their name was taken from his own name.
The children of a new civilization that was supposed to live on the ruins of the previous world, but they did not know the whole truth.
Only the leaders knew a kind of twisted truth, a hidden line of people whose duty was to pass the truth from one generation to the next.
He taught them about Father, what kind of higher being he was and that he had to be worshiped, and their final goal, which was to free Father’s child, Black Silence.
Their duty was also simple, protect the Forgotten Tree, watch over the transfer, and hide the truth.
And when the appointed day came, awaken the Founder.
Cindar then entered the coffin, his body was placed between life and death, his biological activity dropped almost to zero, and time almost stopped for him.
Now Lian understood what that coffin under Rootcrown had been, it was not a tomb but actually a waiting room.
Centuries passed, everything was calm until something unexpected suddenly happened and then Cindar woke up earlier than planned.
One of the Cindari leaders was kneeling in front of the coffin.
Their Founder opened his eyes, his body was still dry and pale, but his consciousness had returned.
"Why did you wake me?"
"Some beings entered the world that do not belong here."
Cindar was silent for a moment, then images appeared inside a memory crystal.
Humans, but not Humans from Earth, they were natives of the Tenth Ruined Realm, a group that Aren had once been part of.
Cindar looked at their faces for the first time, he truly did not know them.
"What are these?"
"We don’t know."
"They appeared from a crack that did not exist before."
"From outside this world?" Cindar narrowed his eyes.
"Yes."
At that moment, something changed inside Cindar’s mind, another world, which meant Black Silence did not have to eat only this Realm.
If a being from that world became a Vessel, it could become the Anchor of its own world.
The Calamity had found a path to a new world and a new world meant more life, more death, and more power!
Cindar thought for a long time, his original plan was ready, he could become the Vessel at the right time.

But now a new opportunity was in front of him, another world, just another world, if Black Silence devoured that place first and then transferred to Cindar, perhaps his final power would become several times greater.
And as a result, reaching the power needed to reverse death would become easier.
Greed won.
"Capture one alive."
The leader raised his head.
"Why?"
"I want a healthy body." That was all, and he gave no further explanation.
But the Humans were not weak, their groups spread throughout the forests.
They resisted, stole from the Cindari, took Artifacts, stole maps, killed Cindari, and the Cindari killed them too.
Hatred slowly formed on both sides.
As generations passed, the original order, "Capture one alive," was almost forgotten among ordinary people.
What remained was simpler, Humans are enemies and they must be killed.
But the leaders still needed a living body, so another story was created.
A story that was so close to the truth that it was easy to believe.
The Forgotten Tree was dying, this was true.
With its death, the water and Mana of the three forests would be destroyed, this was also mostly true.
The Cindari world might one day become impossible to live in, and again, this was true.
And then came the main lie:
"Our only hope is to find a way to another world."
"The Humans came from another world."
"So we must capture one alive so we can find a way out."
It was a great goal, easy to understand, saving an entire race, and the people believed it, and instead of killing the Humans, several Humans were captured alive.
One after another, they were brought to the Forgotten Tree.
Lian saw the scenes, one was a young man, the roots wrapped around his body.
The process began, but a few moments later his body started to have seizures.
[Insufficient Compatibility.]
[Vessel Stability Rejected.]
The roots pulled back and the man did not survive, when the news reached Cindar, he showed no special reaction, it seemed like he expected such a result to happen.
And then he ordered them to use other Humans, until one of them was finally chosen.
The second was a woman, but her Soul did not match the structure of the Calamity, she was rejected and died again.
The third, another failure.
The fourth also met the same fate, death.
Some did not even last a few minutes, Black Silence did not accept any Human body, in fact, it accepted none of them and almost no Humans remained.
All the Humans who had appeared from the crack and were spread across the three forests were soon either killed by monsters or captured by the Cindari.
Except for one, Aren, who was still on the run, the last living option and because of that they chased him, and capturing him was one of the hardest things for them.
He was a Human who could use the Earth Element, he could hide anywhere there was soil, and the forests were like his home.
It took years until they were finally able to capture him and when they finally captured him, they did not kill him.
Aren was the last hope of Cindar’s plan.
But before the Cindari could start the process on him, the world changed again.
A new crack opened and Humans returned, but this time they were different.
Cindar understood with only one look.
These Humans did not belong to the same world as Aren, the source of their Mana was different, their Souls had been formed by different laws.
And this made him smile with greed, if there was another world, then how many other worlds were there?
Ten?
A hundred?
A thousand?
And each one could become food, so could he become infinitely strong this way?
That same day, one of the new Humans appeared near the Forgotten Tree.
Selina.
The roots reacted almost immediately, not because she was the most special Human alive.
Not because of an unmatched Talent, not because of a strange Bloodline, Black Silence first sensed something else.
Something behind Selina, the world she came from, Earth.
The Calamity’s hunger became stronger for a moment, then it examined the girl’s body.
She was not the best possible Vessel but she was enough for it to endure her for some time, enough for it to enter their world after devouring this world and find a better one.
[Suitable Vessel Detected.]
[Vessel Compatibility: Acceptable.]
[Gestation Process Started.]
The roots grabbed Selina.
And Lian finally understood everything.
"So you never wanted Selina."
The feeling of Black Silence’s hunger was still flowing through the memory.
"You sensed the smell of Earth from her."
"But why? Why did you choose someone from Earth but not from the Ruined Realm?" He frowned deeply, this was something he could not understand.
Why had the Calamity not chosen an Anchor and Vessel from the Tenth Ruined Realm, but immediately chose the first option from Earth without hesitation?
What was the difference? What was the reason behind it?
He himself had two theories, but both had flaws and unclear points.

The first was that the Tenth Ruined Realm was already being taken over by a Calamity, and since a Calamity could see the memories of its Vessels, it probably knew about this and most likely could not enter a world that was already being attacked by another Calamity.

The second theory was that the Tenth Ruined Realm had already reached the point of destruction and there was not much left of it, and Black Silence needed destruction, killing, and chaos to become stronger.
So clearly a world that was already almost destroyed had little value to it.
"Of course, there could also be a third theory, a combination of both theories." Lian whispered.

He himself felt that perhaps the second theory was more correct, because if we assume that a Calamity cannot enter a world that is already being attacked by another Calamity, then Black Silence should not be able to enter Earth either.
He was sure that his own world was also being attacked by one of the Calamities, although he did not know which one, after all, he only knew one of the five Calamities.
But even so, Black Silence had also accepted an Anchor and Vessel from Earth, which meant it could enter a world that was already being attacked by a Calamity.
Although Earth had one difference from the Tenth Ruined Realm, Earth was still healthy and was neither destroyed nor close to destruction.
They had not only been able to resist, but had also been able to push the Calamity back.
And because of that, Earth was more attractive to Black Silence, a world that still had life, and because of that it wanted to enter their world.
But these were only a few possible theories and he could not be completely sure, not to mention that he was still not sure whether the selection of Anchors was random or had important conditions.
Because he was sure that there were no special conditions for being a Vessel, the Vessel only had to be able to carry the existence of Black Silence.
But he was not sure about being an Anchor, his instincts told him that there were more important conditions, but he had no idea what those conditions could be.

Unfortunately, the memories showed him nothing, he only understood that Anchor and Vessel were two different things, one person could be both a Vessel and an Anchor, but it was also possible for the Anchor and Vessel to be two different beings.
Right now it seemed that he was becoming a Vessel, the System notifications confirmed this.
