chapters.title: Chapter 358: Memories Of A Calamity ( Final )
paragraphs: But he did not know whether he would also become an Anchor or not, but if he did not, how was the Calamity supposed to enter their world? Because it was clear that it needed an Anchor to enter their world and allow the Calamity to enter.
"Ah, damn it, this is too confusing, why do I even have to get involved in this stuff?" He sighed from exhaustion.
He was only an eighteen-year-old young man who had not even been an Awakened for very long, so why did he have to get involved in such huge cosmic plots?
"At least my other questions have been answered."
The other questions were answered one after another.
Why Selina? Because she was from Earth and had at least the required compatibility.
Why did Aren survive? Because he was the last remaining Anchor connected to another world.
Why did the Cindari want Humans alive? Not to escape, but to open a path for the Calamity.
Why was the Forgotten Tree dying? Because it was holding Black Silence inside itself and the Calamity was feeding on its life force.
Why was the Titan still considered the main Vessel while a new embryo was growing inside Selina?
Because the Titan was the prison and the old Vessel, while the Tree was slowly pulling the Calamity out to create a new Vessel.
Why did failing the Main Quest mean that Black Silence would gain access to Earth?
Because Selina and now Lian were Vessels from Earth.
Why had Cindar placed himself between life and death? Because he was waiting for the day he could become the final Vessel.
Why did Caelus talk about Father, Salvation, and the children? Because Cindar’s truth had turned into a religion over the generations.
Lian did not know what he felt for a long time, part of him understood the young Cindar, a man who had lost everything.
His family, his home, his lover, his loneliness was real, his pain was real.
Even his first anger was understandable, but none of it justified anything.
He looked at an image of Cindar standing beside the Forgotten Tree and waiting for the Calamity to be transferred.
"You lost your family." Then images of cities destroyed because of Black Silence appeared.
"And because of that, you decided to destroy everyone else’s families."
"You were a victim."
An image of young Cindar, his bloody hands under the ruins, then an image of Cindar the hero, the smiles of the people and ...then betrayal.
"Then you became the worst thing you hated."
But at that moment, Lian noticed another point, some of the memories he had seen should not have belonged to Black Silence.
Cindar’s private conversation with Father, his memories of his family, his feelings toward his lover.
Thoughts that no one had heard, why did Black Silence know them? And the answer slowly became clear.
The Anchor bond was not one-sided, just as Cindar received a share of the Calamity’s power, the Calamity had also taken a part of him.
Memories, feelings, perhaps even pieces of his Soul, every Anchor left a trace of themselves inside Black Silence.
"The relationship between a Calamity and an Anchor is complicated, it is a two-way relationship, both benefit from each other, both depend on each other."
"But the relationship between a Calamity and a Vessel is not like this, the Calamity forcibly takes over the Vessel and makes all of its consciousness, personality, and existence its own."
Lian suddenly became silent.
"Wait...then if I am its new Vessel right now..."
The memory reacted, all the images shook, for the first time, he felt something inside Black Silence looking at him.
Not at his body but at his memories, he tried to pull his mind back, but it was too late and the images began to break.
Cindar.
Aurelia.
Primordial Root.
Titan.
Father.
Everything fell over one another.
The System appeared.
[Gestation Reconstruction: 99.7%]
[Gestation Reconstruction: 99.8%]
Lian tried to pull himself out of the flow of memories but nothing happened, he was no longer only feeling the past.
Black Silence’s hunger was returning to the present.
And with it he felt something else ...Earth.
Lian could not see Earth, but he could feel it, like a familiar smell behind a very thick wall.
The Mana of his world, its Souls, its life, and to Black Silence a very delicious food.
"Damn it, damn it, damn it!" He suddenly felt all of his consciousness being destroyed, as if something was forcibly erasing everything.
Lian tried to stop it but it was useless.
He tried again and it was useless again.
Something like worry formed in his mind, if this continued, besides himself, both worlds would be doomed!
The space around him became dark again, the memories were gone, everything became dark again but this time the darkness was not empty.
Something was eating Lian, eating him, first his sense of time disappeared, he did not know whether one second or one hour had passed.
Then the sounds disappeared, then his recent memories started to slip away.
The face of a girl appeared in his mind for a moment.
Hair.
One eye.
A sword.
But her name—
What was her name?
Lian grabbed it in fear.
"Seris."
The image became stable and then the giant ant with natural armor.
Its name disappeared for a moment.
"One."
Aren.
Selina.
Earth.
He had to keep every name in his mind, as if he let go of it, Black Silence would eat it.
Then it was his turn.
Who was he? A blurry image appeared in front of him and even the System in front of him started to break.
[Calamity Bir—]
The message failed.
[Vessel Conscio—]
The words shook.
[Error.]
Then the final number appeared.
[Gestation Reconstruction: 100.0%]
[Calamity Birth Started.]
Black Silence’s hunger rose from deep inside him with several times more force, now it was no longer guessing about a distant world and for a moment Earth appeared in front of him.
A complete world was behind Lian’s existence, billions of lives.
Oceans, cities, forests, Souls, Mana and all of them had only one meaning in the eyes of the Calamity.
Food.
And he finally understood something about Black Silence that was worse than all of Cindar’s truth.
One world would never be enough for it, even ten worlds might not be enough, this being was made to be hungry.
To devour worlds and the thing that called itself Father had five damned children like it.
Now Lian knew everything.
He knew why Black Silence had come to this world, he knew why Cindar had betrayed them, he knew why the Forgotten Tree was dying.
He knew what the Cindari leaders were really looking for and he finally knew why Selina had been chosen.
But none of these answers were comforting, the truth was much worse than what he had imagined.
Cindar had sold his own world for power, Black Silence wanted worlds to feed its hunger.
And Father still existed somewhere out there, a being with power that was even hard to imagine.
And what was even worse than all of this? There was probably a damn bastard like Cindar in their world too.
A bastard who, for whatever reason, had sold their world and allowed a Calamity to enter their world and was still alive somewhere on Earth.
"Wait..." A very terrifying guess suddenly appeared in his mind.

A crazy guess came to his mind about why Black Silence was not looking for an Anchor to enter Earth, perhaps it wanted to use the same bastard who was already the Anchor of a Calamity in their world as an Anchor?
Could one Human be the Anchor of two Calamities...?
At the same time, another message appeared in the darkness.
[Calamity Birth Is Nearing Completion.]
Lian tried to hold on to the last parts of his consciousness.
His own name, and this was more important than anything else, if he lost it, what would remain?
If he lost his name, then there would be no trace of his existence left.
His name was like a chain to his existence. If it were forgotten, his personality and existence would also be forgotten.
"Lian Vorhelm."
The name remained bright for a moment and then the darkness began to eat it from the edges.
"Lian... Vorhelm."
The mental letters disappeared one after another.
Seris.
One.
Earth.
Himself.
They all moved farther away and Black Silence covered the last part of his consciousness.
He frowned, he still had a backup plan, and he wasn’t going to give up so easily.
And just before nothing of Lian remained, only one message appeared in the darkness.
[Black Silence Has Been Released.]
Then even the darkness could no longer be felt.

sentences.text: But he did not know whether he would also become an Anchor or not, but if he did not, how was the Calamity supposed to enter their world?
Because it was clear that it needed an Anchor to enter their world and allow the Calamity to enter.
"Ah, damn it, this is too confusing, why do I even have to get involved in this stuff?" He sighed from exhaustion.
He was only an eighteen-year-old young man who had not even been an Awakened for very long, so why did he have to get involved in such huge cosmic plots?
"At least my other questions have been answered."
The other questions were answered one after another.
Why Selina?
Because she was from Earth and had at least the required compatibility.
Why did Aren survive?
Because he was the last remaining Anchor connected to another world.
Why did the Cindari want Humans alive?
Not to escape, but to open a path for the Calamity.
Why was the Forgotten Tree dying?
Because it was holding Black Silence inside itself and the Calamity was feeding on its life force.
Why was the Titan still considered the main Vessel while a new embryo was growing inside Selina?
Because the Titan was the prison and the old Vessel, while the Tree was slowly pulling the Calamity out to create a new Vessel.
Why did failing the Main Quest mean that Black Silence would gain access to Earth?
Because Selina and now Lian were Vessels from Earth.
Why had Cindar placed himself between life and death?
Because he was waiting for the day he could become the final Vessel.
Why did Caelus talk about Father, Salvation, and the children?
Because Cindar’s truth had turned into a religion over the generations.
Lian did not know what he felt for a long time, part of him understood the young Cindar, a man who had lost everything.
His family, his home, his lover, his loneliness was real, his pain was real.
Even his first anger was understandable, but none of it justified anything.
He looked at an image of Cindar standing beside the Forgotten Tree and waiting for the Calamity to be transferred.
"You lost your family." Then images of cities destroyed because of Black Silence appeared.
"And because of that, you decided to destroy everyone else’s families."
"You were a victim."
An image of young Cindar, his bloody hands under the ruins, then an image of Cindar the hero, the smiles of the people and ...then betrayal.
"Then you became the worst thing you hated."
But at that moment, Lian noticed another point, some of the memories he had seen should not have belonged to Black Silence.
Cindar’s private conversation with Father, his memories of his family, his feelings toward his lover.
Thoughts that no one had heard, why did Black Silence know them?
And the answer slowly became clear.
The Anchor bond was not one-sided, just as Cindar received a share of the Calamity’s power, the Calamity had also taken a part of him.
Memories, feelings, perhaps even pieces of his Soul, every Anchor left a trace of themselves inside Black Silence.
"The relationship between a Calamity and an Anchor is complicated, it is a two-way relationship, both benefit from each other, both depend on each other."
"But the relationship between a Calamity and a Vessel is not like this, the Calamity forcibly takes over the Vessel and makes all of its consciousness, personality, and existence its own."
Lian suddenly became silent.
"Wait...then if I am its new Vessel right now..."
The memory reacted, all the images shook, for the first time, he felt something inside Black Silence looking at him.
Not at his body but at his memories, he tried to pull his mind back, but it was too late and the images began to break.
Cindar.
Aurelia.
Primordial Root.
Titan.
Father.
Everything fell over one another.
The System appeared.
[Gestation Reconstruction: 99.7%]
[Gestation Reconstruction: 99.8%]
Lian tried to pull himself out of the flow of memories but nothing happened, he was no longer only feeling the past.
Black Silence’s hunger was returning to the present.
And with it he felt something else ...Earth.
Lian could not see Earth, but he could feel it, like a familiar smell behind a very thick wall.
The Mana of his world, its Souls, its life, and to Black Silence a very delicious food.
"Damn it, damn it, damn it!" He suddenly felt all of his consciousness being destroyed, as if something was forcibly erasing everything.
Lian tried to stop it but it was useless.
He tried again and it was useless again.
Something like worry formed in his mind, if this continued, besides himself, both worlds would be doomed!
The space around him became dark again, the memories were gone, everything became dark again but this time the darkness was not empty.
Something was eating Lian, eating him, first his sense of time disappeared, he did not know whether one second or one hour had passed.
Then the sounds disappeared, then his recent memories started to slip away.
The face of a girl appeared in his mind for a moment.
Hair.
One eye.
A sword.
But her name—
What was her name?
Lian grabbed it in fear.
"Seris."
The image became stable and then the giant ant with natural armor.
Its name disappeared for a moment.
"One."
Aren.
Selina.
Earth.
He had to keep every name in his mind, as if he let go of it, Black Silence would eat it.
Then it was his turn.
Who was he?
A blurry image appeared in front of him and even the System in front of him started to break.
[Calamity Bir—]
The message failed.
[Vessel Conscio—]
The words shook.
[Error.]
Then the final number appeared.
[Gestation Reconstruction: 100.0%]
[Calamity Birth Started.]
Black Silence’s hunger rose from deep inside him with several times more force, now it was no longer guessing about a distant world and for a moment Earth appeared in front of him.
A complete world was behind Lian’s existence, billions of lives.
Oceans, cities, forests, Souls, Mana and all of them had only one meaning in the eyes of the Calamity.
Food.
And he finally understood something about Black Silence that was worse than all of Cindar’s truth.
One world would never be enough for it, even ten worlds might not be enough, this being was made to be hungry.
To devour worlds and the thing that called itself Father had five damned children like it.
Now Lian knew everything.
He knew why Black Silence had come to this world, he knew why Cindar had betrayed them, he knew why the Forgotten Tree was dying.
He knew what the Cindari leaders were really looking for and he finally knew why Selina had been chosen.
But none of these answers were comforting, the truth was much worse than what he had imagined.
Cindar had sold his own world for power, Black Silence wanted worlds to feed its hunger.
And Father still existed somewhere out there, a being with power that was even hard to imagine.
And what was even worse than all of this?
There was probably a damn bastard like Cindar in their world too.
A bastard who, for whatever reason, had sold their world and allowed a Calamity to enter their world and was still alive somewhere on Earth.
"Wait..." A very terrifying guess suddenly appeared in his mind.

A crazy guess came to his mind about why Black Silence was not looking for an Anchor to enter Earth, perhaps it wanted to use the same bastard who was already the Anchor of a Calamity in their world as an Anchor?
Could one Human be the Anchor of two Calamities...?
At the same time, another message appeared in the darkness.
[Calamity Birth Is Nearing Completion.]
Lian tried to hold on to the last parts of his consciousness.
His own name, and this was more important than anything else, if he lost it, what would remain?
If he lost his name, then there would be no trace of his existence left.
His name was like a chain to his existence.
If it were forgotten, his personality and existence would also be forgotten.
"Lian Vorhelm."
The name remained bright for a moment and then the darkness began to eat it from the edges.
"Lian...
Vorhelm."
The mental letters disappeared one after another.
Seris.
One.
Earth.
Himself.
They all moved farther away and Black Silence covered the last part of his consciousness.
He frowned, he still had a backup plan, and he wasn’t going to give up so easily.
And just before nothing of Lian remained, only one message appeared in the darkness.
[Black Silence Has Been Released.]
Then even the darkness could no longer be felt.

chapters.title: Chapter 359: Not Lian Anymore I
paragraphs: Seris did not take her eyes off the cocoon.
The sword was still in her hand, although her fingers no longer had much strength to grip the handle.
Fresh and dried blood covered almost all of her clothes, and every time she breathed, pain ran from her cracked ribs to her injured side.
Behind her, One was lying on the ground, and only the very weak movements of one of his antennae showed that he was not completely dead yet.
Aren was also farther away, with both of his arms cut off and his body barely moving up and down, hanging between consciousness and unconsciousness.
And in front of the cocoon, five moving corpses stood in silence.
Four ancient Cindari stood on both sides of the Founder, and Cindar Vael stood in the center, with the same dry face and golden eyes, looking at the thing he had waited centuries to reach.
Seris did not know how many seconds had passed since the number 99.9 appeared.
Maybe only two seconds, maybe ten seconds, but it felt like every second was becoming longer.
Then—
Thump.
A sound came from inside the cocoon, not very loud, but deep enough that Seris could feel its vibration in her bones.
And then everything stopped.
The huge flow of mana that had been pulled from all across the world toward the Forgotten Tree until a few moments ago suddenly stopped.
The golden and black lights twisting across the surface of the cocoon also disappeared.
Even the wind seemed to stop for a few moments.
"Is it over?" She unconsciously held her breath.
No new message from the system appeared, and the number 99.9 had also disappeared.
But then a soft sound came.
Crack.
A thin crack appeared on the white and blackened surface of the cocoon, the crack stretched from top to bottom and a second crack appeared beside it.
Seris immediately changed her sword stance and moved her healthier leg slightly back.
Her body was almost empty of strength, but everything she had left became ready to react at that moment.
The cocoon did not explode, instead, contrary to what she expected, it slowly opened.
Its two halves moved away from each other in a strange way and a thick black liquid poured from the bottom onto the dry ground.
First, one leg came out, then the second leg and finally ...Lian stepped out of the cocoon.
The young Pendragon only stared for a few moments, there were no horns on his head, and no wings had grown from his back.
His body had not turned into some strange creature either, he was just Lian.
The clothes that had been torn during his crazy journey from Rootcrown to here and then during the battle with the Cindari leader were still on his body.
His hair looked the same and even the burned wounds on his hands that had been caused when he pulled Selina out had mostly closed.
If someone only looked at him from a distance, they might not even notice any difference.
But Seris understood immediately, this was not Lian, or at least whatever was controlling that body was not the Lian she knew.
The eyes were the first sign.
Inside his dark pupils, a very weak purple light was shining.
It was not a strong or dramatic light, it was more like a distant star still visible behind a layer of darkness.
But even that was not the real difference, it was his presence.
She had seen Lian’s anger before.
When One was injured, when Kaelos attacked him and Aren, even that frightening calmness before his first punch.
But anger, no matter how cold, was still an emotion, his mocking was human, his curiosity was human, even his desire for battle was something that could be understood.
What was standing in front of Seris now had none of those things.
It was not anger, not hatred and not pleasure, not even cruelty, because cruelty also required something to matter to you.
It was only indifference.

An indifference so deep and cold that when she looked at it, she felt that if the entire forest burned right now, if a thousand people were killed in front of that creature or if this whole world fell apart, not even the slightest change would appear in its eyes.
Life and death were not two different things to it, there was only something that had not been consumed yet.
Seris’s body reacted before her mind, the muscles in her neck tightened and the hair on the back of her neck stood up.
Her heartbeat suddenly increased and her hand gripped the sword handle so tightly that her knuckles turned white.
Her right foot unconsciously moved half a step back, and all her instincts shouted one command.
Run.
Just run.
She immediately stopped her foot.
She was angry that her own body had reacted like that without her permission, but even that anger could not remove the feeling of danger.
Her healthy eye remained fixed on Lian’s face.
"Lian...?" She said in a low voice.
His head slowly turned toward Seris, that was all, there was no other movement and for a moment their eyes met.
And Seris did not find what she was most afraid of seeing in the deepest part of her mind.
Recognition.
There was no recognition in those eyes, not even the smallest sign that the creature in front of her knew who Seris was.
It was as if he was seeing her for the first time, something cold sank into Seris’s chest, she felt her heart hurt ...
The four moving corpses moved at that exact moment.
The ancient swordsman lowered his sword and bowed his head.
The moving corpse that controlled the roots also bent its body slightly forward and the mage, even with one arm cut off and his shoulder almost destroyed, repeated the same bow.
The other one also lowered his head.
The four creatures that had attacked Seris without hesitation to kill her only a few minutes ago were now bowing before Lian’s body.
Only Cindar did not do it.
The Founder stood a few steps away, and finally something that looked like emotion appeared on his dry face.
A small smile, but the deep satisfaction inside him was impossible to hide.
Hundreds of years of waiting, generations of planning and lies that had become history.
Humans who had been hunted, creatures that had been sacrificed and an entire civilization that had been created only to watch over a single plan.
It had finally worked...Black Silence was walking in the world again!
But the creature inside Lian’s body did not even look at Cindar once, his purple eyes calmly passed over Seris and looked into the distance.
Beyond the gray plain, beyond the Forgotten Tree and in the direction of the Giant’s Graveyard.
Something was there, something that the new body knew even without seeing it.
A part of its own existence, trapped and compressed, chained inside the body of a huge creature that had served as its prison for centuries.
This birth had freed it, but it had not made it complete.
What was now inside Lian’s body was only a part of Black Silence, the part that had been pulled out of the Titan over the centuries and gathered inside the tree.
The main part was still there, inside the Corrupted Titan and until that part was also freed, Black Silence was only free, and not complete.
And its hunger instinctively knew its next destination.
The Giant’s Graveyard.
Seris did not know what the creature in front of her was looking at, but she noticed something else.
The look it had given her a few moments ago was exactly the same look a human might give when walking past an ant on a stone.
Part of Seris’s pride was angry about this, and the wiser part of her was afraid.
"It doesn’t even see me as an enemy."
In the corner of her vision, a panel was still open.
[Objective of Evolution: Kill the Calamity.]
She gave it a short look, the Calamity was right in front of her, only a few meters away.
But her body—
Lian’s body.
Her sword did not lower, but she did not attack either and a question more important than the evolution mission was turning in her mind.
Was Lian still in there? Maybe his consciousness had been completely swallowed, maybe only his body remained.
But what if even a small part of him was still deep inside that existence?
What if there was a way to pull him out?
What if he could still return?
The system wanted her to kill the Calamity, but if the Calamity and Lian were no longer separate from each other, what would completing that mission mean?
Seris’s fingers tightened around the sword handle.
She did not know.
But if that creature attacked, there would be no time left to think.
At that moment, a weak sound came from behind her, the sound of something heavy being dragged across the ground.
Seris immediately turned around and her eye widened.
The giant ant was moving, it should not have been able to.
Its stomach and side had two holes in them.
Its natural armor was broken in several places and a pool of dark blood had formed under its body.
But One was pulling himself forward, not by walking, he did not have the strength to do that.
His legs no longer had enough strength and he grabbed the ground with his claws and front part of his body, pulling himself forward a few centimeters.
Then again.
And again.
Every movement should have caused unimaginable pain, but his antennae were moving slowly.
A very weak feeling flowed through the Hive Link.
Happiness and calmness ... his master had returned.
The link had become strange and weak, but it was enough for One, he could feel that same presence, that same body that had always given him orders.
"One, wait—" Seris opened her lips.
It was too late.
The wounded ant reached Lian’s leg, raised its head with difficulty.
One of his antennae touched Lian’s body.
The movement was so weak that it looked more like a childish caress.
One tried to pull himself a little higher, maybe he wanted to touch his master’s hand.
Maybe he even wanted to bring his face closer to him like a loyal animal.
The creature inside Lian’s body looked down, nothing happened for a fraction of a second.
Then his hand rose ...but just before moving, the hand stopped.
Not even a second ...less, so short that Seris might later doubt whether she had really seen it.
The purple light inside Lian’s eyes trembled for a moment and Cindar also saw the same pause from a distance, a pause that showed hesitation.
Then the hand moved, the back of his hand hit One’s body.
Just one hit.

But One’s several-ton body was lifted from the ground like a light object, the sound of the air breaking echoed and the giant ant flew dozens of meters and crashed directly into the lower part of the Forgotten Tree.
BOOOOOM!
The huge dry wood of the tree cracked.
A large crack appeared on the trunk that could once have held several buildings inside it.
A part of it broke and fell.
One made a sound that Seris had never heard from him before.
It was pure pain, a muffled and terrible sound that almost immediately stopped.

chapters.title: Chapter 360: Not Lian Anymore II
paragraphs: One made a sound that Seris had never heard from him before.
It was a pure cry of pain, a low and terrible sound that almost immediately stopped.
His body fell from the trunk, landed on the ground, and did not move again.
"Lian!" Anger inside her burst into flames and her scream spread across the empty field.
This time there was no hesitation in her voice, she did not call Black Silence.
She did not call the Calamity.
She shouted Lian’s own name, but the creature in front of her did not even react to hearing his own name.
Seris’s remaining eye became cold.
If Lian still had control, he would never do something like this! There was no situation where Lian would do this to One.
One was not just a monster or a battle companion to him.
Seris had seen many times how strange and deep the bond between the two of them was.
So either Lian no longer existed, or he was buried so deep inside this creature that his presence made no difference for now.
She did not wait any longer, the panel in the corner of her vision flashed.
[Evolution Objective: Kill a Calamity.]
The sword rose and her body screamed from pain, but she sent the last remaining strength into her legs.
The ground under her feet broke, the young Pendragon shot toward Lian like a dark line.
[Moonless Rift.]
The sword moved toward his neck at full speed, the creature inside Lian only raised one hand.
It did not activate any skill and only tried to catch the attack with its palm, the edge of the sword stopped between its fingers.
For a moment, the girl could not believe it, all the power of the attack, the remaining mana, and the speed she had managed to create with a body that was almost destroyed.
All of it had been stopped with one hand...?
Even the blade did not move one centimeter forward and her remaining eye opened wider.
Before she could pull the sword back, Lian’s other hand grabbed her free wrist.
Seris immediately tried to free herself, the muscles in her arm tightened, she put her foot on the ground and pulled with all her strength.
Nothing happened, it was as if her wrist was stuck inside stone, the difference in their strength was already huge even under normal conditions.
But Lian’s stats alone were twice the total of hers.
And now? Seris was almost completely broken, a large part of her mana was gone.
Her muscles had been damaged from overusing the Mark Leaves and strengthening skills.
She had one eye missing, her legs were injured, and her ribs were broken.
This was not a battle, it was more like a fight between a deer and a tiger, the deer had no chance and could only make itself look like a clown by attacking.
Black Silence struck with its free hand, a simple slap landed on the girl’s face.
Crack!
But Seris’s head violently turned to one side, the skin on her unharmed cheek opened, her lower lip split, and blood sprayed from her mouth.
The bone under her eye made an unpleasant sound and the vision in her only remaining eye turned completely white for several seconds and her body became completely weak.
But Lian’s hand was still holding her wrist, then his fingers closed a little more, the young Pendragon first felt the pressure.
Then the pain and finally... crack.
The bone in her wrist broke.
Seris’s fingers opened without her control, the sword fell from her hand and landed on the ground with a metallic sound.
She let out a painful breath, she did not even have time to scream.
She struck Lian’s stomach with her knee, using almost all the strength she had left, but his body did not move, even his expression did not change.
Black Silence lifted Seris with one hand, her feet left the ground and then it threw her to the side.
The girl’s body rolled several times across the ground, her side and shoulder hit the ground and finally her back hit one of the dried roots of the tree and stopped there.
For several moments, no sound came from her, her body moved only once and then... became still.
Her breathing was so weak that she herself was not sure if she was still breathing.
But through her blurred vision, she saw Lian’s shadow coming toward her.
One step... then a second step.
Her mind no longer had the strength to think clearly, only one simple thought remained.
"He’s going to finish me."
It made sense.
If what she knew was true, Black Silence saw every living creature only as food.
Seris was still alive, One was still alive, Aren was still alive, and Selina was also unconscious not far away.
Why would it leave any of them alive?
Lian stood in front of Seris, his hand rose slightly, she did not even have the strength to lift her head, only her remaining eye was barely open.
Then the movement stopped, the same pause during the attack on One and this time it lasted a little longer, the purple light inside his eyes became weaker for a moment.
Something very weak moved deep inside him.
Black Silence remained still for several seconds, then lowered its hand and turned away.
Seris did not know why, and before she could even think about it, her consciousness completely faded.
But someone else had seen that pause.
Cindar Vael, and the smile on the Founder’s dry face became slightly weaker.
His golden eyes first fell on Seris, then on One and then back to Lian’s body.
Something was wrong.
Cindar knew what Black Silence was better than almost every living creature in this world.
The Calamity did not leave food behind, not because of mercy, not because of morals, not even because of boredom, there was no way the Calamity he knew would leave something alive.
Life was power, death was power, and every weak creature that stood before it without defense was food that there was no reason to ignore.
But now there were four living creatures around it, and the Calamity was leaving them behind.
Cindar said nothing, the undead had basically not spoken since their return.
But the absolute satisfaction in the Founder’s eyes was mixed with a small amount of doubt.
Black Silence did not care, it looked toward the Giant’s Graveyard and a sound came from its throat, it was Lian’s voice, but the tone had nothing similar to him.
Cold, empty and without any emotion.
"Let’s go."
The four undead immediately moved, Cindar also joined them after a short pause.
Two of them stood on both sides of Lian’s body and mana began to form under their feet. One grabbed Lian’s arm and the other lifted his body with mana.
Lian could not fly by himself, but it did not matter and a few seconds later, six figures left the ground.
His purple eyes remained fixed in one direction until the last moment.
The Giant’s Graveyard.
And then everyone moved away from above the Forgotten Tree.
Time passed.
One hour.
Then two hours.
And then more.
None of the bodies left beside the tree moved, the Forgotten Tree was also no longer dying.
It had finally died.
Its last life force had been consumed during the birth of Black Silence and now not even the weakest flow of mana remained in its huge roots.
The branches that once reached kilometers above the ground fell one after another and every fall shook the ground.
The wood broke apart after hitting the ground and some parts of it turned directly into ash.
The roots underground dried up and the springs that had been fed by the root network for centuries slowly became weaker.
The moisture left the soil, and the effect of the tree’s death did not remain limited to this field.
Three forests were connected to it, the flow of water, mana and a large part of the cycle of life were all connected to it.
The death of the tree was like cutting the heart of a huge creature whose veins were spread across this entire world.
The sky also changed and a dark red and sick-looking color slowly spread between the clouds, then it became stronger, until the sky was almost the color of blood.

It was as if the world itself had understood that the Calamity that had been suppressed for years had been released again, the corruption had returned to the world and was quickly spreading everywhere.
Several hours later, Selina’s finger moved.
At first only a little and then her eyelids moved again, and finally her eyes opened.
The first thing she saw was the red sky, she only stared at it for several seconds, nothing matched the last memory she had.
Her head was heavy, her body felt strangely weak and there were still faint signs of pain and burning on parts of her skin.
Selina slowly tried to sit up but the dizziness made her put her hand on the ground.
"Where...?"
The last thing she remembered was the rift, entering the Special Area, a strong light that covered her entire vision for a moment and then appearing in front of a tree.
A tree so huge that even from close by she could not see its highest branches.
And then? Nothing, her consciousness had stopped right there.
"How long...?" She put her hand on her forehead.
Then she looked around, and the words stopped in her mouth.
First she saw the girl, a blood-covered body was lying beside one of the roots.
Half of her face was almost covered with dried blood. One of her eyes was in a terrible condition, her wrist was at an unnatural angle and her clothes were burned and torn in several places.
A few meters away, a giant ant was lying on the ground.
For a moment, Selina was not even sure if it was dead or not.
Its body armor was broken in several places and there were two large wounds on its side and stomach.
Then she saw a middle-aged man, without two arms, both of his arms were cut off above the elbows.
Selina looked at the scene in silence for several seconds.
"Where the hell did I end up?"

chapters.title: Chapter 361: Not Lian Anymore ( Final )
paragraphs: "Where the hell did I end up?"
Her first instinct was to get away, she did not know these people, she did not know what had happened, she did not know who had attacked whom.
Maybe these people were enemies, maybe that girl was dangerous.
And that giant ant? She did not even want to know.
She could stand up, she could leave, but after taking only a few steps, she stopped and her eyes returned to the blood-covered girl.
She fought with herself for several seconds and then let out a frustrated breath.
"Damn it."
She turned back, knelt beside Seris, put two fingers on her neck, felt nothing for a few moments, frowned and moved them slightly.
Then... a pulse, it was very weak but it was there.
"Luckily, you’re alive."
She went to Aren, his pulse was also weak, but it was a little more regular than Seris’s.
The wounds where his arms had been cut off were closed, although his condition still looked dangerous.
Selina then looked at the ant, well, she really did not care whether a monster this scary was alive or dead.
She hesitated for a few seconds and then opened her storage space, she did not have many healing potions.
In this area, every potion could make the difference between her own life and death, but she looked at Seris again.
"I hope you’re not a bad person."
She took out a potion, slowly poured some of it into Seris’s mouth and waited to make sure she could swallow it.
A weak glow appeared over her body, the surface bleeding became weaker, and the torn skin around some wounds started to close.
But her destroyed eye, broken wrist, ribs and deeper wounds remained.
Selina gave another potion to Aren, its effect was similar, his pulse became a little more regular, his breathing became deeper and some color returned to his pale face.
"The rest is up to you." Then Selina moved a few meters away and sat down, she had done everything she could.
Some time later, Seris was the first one to wake up, her remaining eye suddenly opened, for several seconds she could not see anything clearly.
The red sky, the broken trunk of the tree, the face of a girl she did not know and then the memories returned.
The cocoon.
Lian.
Purple eyes.
One.
Her body suddenly moved, pain rose through almost every part of her body and her face tightened.
"Hey! Don’t move, your body—" Selina immediately stood up.
"One." But Seris did not even look at her, there was something more important than her pain right now.
With her healthy hand, she grabbed the ground and tried to pull herself forward, her injured leg did not have enough strength, she could not use her broken wrist, but she still moved.
"What are you doing? I told you not to move!"
The young Pendragon reached One, put her hand on the healthier part of his body armor and felt nothing for several seconds.
Her heart sank... was he really dead?
Then suddenly... the ant’s antenna moved very weakly!
Seris let out a breath, he was alive, although if this could be called living, and she turned her head toward Selina.
"Do you have more of what you gave me?"
"Yeah, but wait, who are you people? I don’t even know where this—" Selina said, still confused by her behavior.
"Give it to him." Seris interrupted her.
"What?
"The same potion." She pointed at One with her chin.
"I don’t even know what this is." Selina looked at the ant, then back at Seris, why should she help an unknown monster?
"Lian’s friend."
"Lian?" The name was enough to make the girl’s eyes open wider as she looked at both of them in surprise.
"We’re his friends too." Seris nodded.
For a moment, the word itself felt strange in her mind.
Friend.
But she had no time to think about it.
"Save him. Then I’ll explain what’s going on."
Selina looked at her seriously for several seconds, then let out a frustrated breath.
It was strange that this girl knew Lian, what exactly was happening here? Why was a giant ant a friend of Lian? None of this made sense.
"Fine."
She took out another potion, knelt beside One’s head and carefully poured the liquid into his mouth.
Nothing happened for several seconds, then a weak healing light moved over the broken parts of his armor and the bleeding from the large wound on his side became slower.
His very weak breathing became a little easier to notice, but Seris understood with one look that it was not enough.
"Another one."
"I only have one more."
"Give it to him."
"But this is my last healing potion." Selina frowned.
"Give it to him." Seris said this time in a cold voice, her voice was not loud, but there was a clear warning in it.
"Do you know that we might need it ourselves in a few hours?"
"If Lian comes back and finds out that we let One die, your last potion will be the least of your problems."
Selina stared at her for several seconds, then her eyes moved to the ant, and finally she took out the last potion and gave it to One too.
The second potion had a clearer effect and the bleeding almost stopped, the movement of his body became more regular and his right antenna slowly rose and then fell back onto the ground.
Seris let out a breath of relief, the pressure that had been on her chest since she woke up became a little lighter.
’I never thought I would be this happy about an ant staying alive.’ she thought.
At that moment, a sound came from behind them, Aren opened his eyes, the man first looked at the sky in confusion.
Then he unconsciously tried to move a hand toward his head, but no hand moved, his face tightened for a moment and the memory returned like a hit.
His arms had been cut off in the battle with the Cindari leader.
He closed his eyes and took a hard breath and then looked again, Seris, One and the unknown girl who had been inside the cocoon... wait, the unknown girl who had been inside the cocoon?
How had this girl gotten out of the cocoon? And where was Lian?!
"Where is Lian?" Aren immediately asked.
Seris stayed silent and after hearing Lian’s name again, Selina did not wait this time and sat down in front of the young Pendragon.
"Alright, I gave two of my potions to you and two more to a giant ant that I don’t even know where it came from."
"Now I’d really appreciate it if someone told me who you are, what is happening here and how you know Lian."
"You were trapped inside a cocoon and you were turning into the vessel of a Calamity." Seris looked at her for several seconds and then said in the same direct tone she always used.
"...What?"
"Lian took your place to save you, the Calamity has taken Lian’s body and left."
Selina opened her mouth, but nothing came out, because she did not understand even one word of what she had heard.
"What did you say? The Calamity has taken Lian’s body?" But Aren suddenly raised his head and concern immediately replaced the confusion on his face.
Seris only nodded and Aren did not even breathe for several seconds.
He knew more than Selina what that sentence meant, Black Silence, the same thing that had destroyed the world, the same thing that had corrupted the Titan and was now inside Lian’s body.
"Wait." At the same time, Selina was still trying to put the previous sentences together and raised her finger.
"Cocoon?"
"Calamity?"
"Lian took my place?"
"Why was I even inside a cocoon?" she then asked in disbelief.
"Because the Calamity wanted to use you as its vessel." Seris simply said.
"Why me?"
"I don’t know."
"You don’t know?"
The young Pendragon picked up her fallen sword with her healthy hand, the pain from her broken wrist made her face tighten for a moment, but she said nothing.
"That’s it?" Selina was still staring.
"What do you mean, that’s it?"
"That was your explanation?"
"Yeah."
"Do you think what you said was understandable?" Selina really did not know what to say for several seconds.
"We don’t have time to explain." Seris tried to stand up, her knees shook for a moment and she had to lean against the root beside her.
"I don’t even know who you people are"
"Lian’s friends."
"You’ve said that three times"
Seris ignored her and gave One a short look and then Aren.
"If we can’t separate Lian from the Calamity..." She paused a little, the next words were not easy.
The Evolution Quest panel was still somewhere in her mind.
[Kill the Calamity.]
"We have to kill the Calamity."
Even if it was still inside Lian’s body? Seris had no answer to this question herself.
Her remaining eye fell on the ground, the image of those emotionless eyes returned to her mind, One being thrown into the tree, her own broken wrist.
But also that pause, that very short stop before the attack, and then the second pause, when the creature could have finished the job but did not.
She decided to first try to separate them, but if there was no way... then she would have to make another decision.
Then she straightened her body, almost immediately pain spread through her entire side again but she finally stood.
"We need to go back to the others."
"What others?" Selina frowned.
"Your friends, those annoying girls, Liana, Seraphina and that guy Rindo is there too."
Hearing those names made some of the tension leave Selina’s face, not because she understood what had happened, in fact, she might have been even more confused than before.
But finally, she had found a few familiar names among all this confusion.
And the blood-red sky above them was still becoming darker, the Forgotten Tree behind them was completely dead.
And somewhere much farther away, a creature with Lian’s face was moving away... a creature that Seris still did not know whether she should save... or kill.

"Alright, I gave two of my potions to you and two more to a giant ant that I don’t even know where it came from."
"Now I’d really appreciate it if someone told me who you are, what is happening here and how you know Lian."
"You were trapped inside a cocoon and you were turning into the vessel of a Calamity." Seris looked at her for several seconds and then said in the same direct tone she always used.
"...What?"
"Lian took your place to save you, the Calamity has taken Lian’s body and left."
Selina opened her mouth, but nothing came out, because she did not understand even one word of what she had heard.
"What did you say?
The Calamity has taken Lian’s body?" But Aren suddenly raised his head and concern immediately replaced the confusion on his face.
Seris only nodded and Aren did not even breathe for several seconds.
He knew more than Selina what that sentence meant, Black Silence, the same thing that had destroyed the world, the same thing that had corrupted the Titan and was now inside Lian’s body.
"Wait." At the same time, Selina was still trying to put the previous sentences together and raised her finger.
"Cocoon?"
"Calamity?"
"Lian took my place?"
"Why was I even inside a cocoon?" she then asked in disbelief.
"Because the Calamity wanted to use you as its vessel." Seris simply said.
"Why me?"
"I don’t know."
"You don’t know?"
The young Pendragon picked up her fallen sword with her healthy hand, the pain from her broken wrist made her face tighten for a moment, but she said nothing.
"That’s it?" Selina was still staring.
"What do you mean, that’s it?"
"That was your explanation?"
"Yeah."
"Do you think what you said was understandable?" Selina really did not know what to say for several seconds.
"We don’t have time to explain." Seris tried to stand up, her knees shook for a moment and she had to lean against the root beside her.
"I don’t even know who you people are"
"Lian’s friends."
"You’ve said that three times"
Seris ignored her and gave One a short look and then Aren.
"If we can’t separate Lian from the Calamity..." She paused a little, the next words were not easy.
The Evolution Quest panel was still somewhere in her mind.
[Kill the Calamity.]
"We have to kill the Calamity."
Even if it was still inside Lian’s body?
Seris had no answer to this question herself.
Her remaining eye fell on the ground, the image of those emotionless eyes returned to her mind, One being thrown into the tree, her own broken wrist.
But also that pause, that very short stop before the attack, and then the second pause, when the creature could have finished the job but did not.
She decided to first try to separate them, but if there was no way... then she would have to make another decision.
Then she straightened her body, almost immediately pain spread through her entire side again but she finally stood.
"We need to go back to the others."
"What others?" Selina frowned.
"Your friends, those annoying girls, Liana, Seraphina and that guy Rindo is there too."
Hearing those names made some of the tension leave Selina’s face, not because she understood what had happened, in fact, she might have been even more confused than before.
But finally, she had found a few familiar names among all this confusion.
And the blood-red sky above them was still becoming darker, the Forgotten Tree behind them was completely dead.
And somewhere much farther away, a creature with Lian’s face was moving away... a creature that Seris still did not know whether she should save... or kill.

chapters.title: Chapter 362: Returning To Vhalaris
paragraphs: The return to Vhalaris took six days.
Six days that felt even longer to Seris than the battle at the Forgotten Tree itself.
Every hour of walking, every forced stop and every time they had to slow down felt like driving a new needle into her nerves.
Her body still had not recovered from what she had gone through.

Her left eye was gone, the wounds on her side and thigh had only partly closed despite Selina’s potions, and after using her enhancement powers too much, her muscles started shaking after every few hours of movement.
Even so, she almost never suggested stopping herself.
Every time her legs became heavier, she only slowed down a little. Every time the pain in her ribs became worse, she took shorter breaths and continued.
Aren was in an even worse condition.
The man who had spent twenty-five years in this world had now lost both of his arms on top of his old physical weakness.
The wounds where his arms had been cut off were closed, but his body was still suffering from blood loss, shock and the huge amount of mana he had used in the previous battle.

Sometimes his balance was lost while walking, and since he no longer had hands to catch himself, he would fall directly onto his shoulder or knee. Selina had to help him up from the ground several times, and even Seris, despite her own condition, stopped whenever necessary.
But One was in the worst condition.
The giant ant had survived after the two healing potions, but there was a huge difference between being alive and being healthy.
Parts of its natural armor were cracked, and the two large wounds on its stomach and side were still being pulled with every movement.
One would sometimes walk for a few hundred meters, then its legs would give out.
Its body would fall heavily onto the ground, and it would take several minutes before it could even raise its head again.
At such times, its antennae would move nervously, as if it was more annoyed than anyone else about slowing the group down.
Seris never said anything, not even once, her anger was not directed at One but at time.
With every hour that passed, the Black Silence was getting farther away.
Every night when they were forced to stop for a few hours, Seris stared into the darkness of the forest with her remaining eye and only thought about where Lian was now.
Or perhaps it was better to say where the thing that had taken Lian’s body was now.
Six days.
Six full days of time.
The Calamity could have done anything during this time.
And she did not even know if anything of Lian was still inside that body.
Unlike the other three, Selina was healthy.

That fact basically made her the main support of the journey back. She carried water and food, checked the surroundings, helped Aren whenever he collapsed and stayed alert whenever One was forced to stop.
On the second day, Seris increased her speed again.
Her steps were still much slower than normal, but it was clear that she wanted to make the time between their stops shorter.
"If you keep going like this, you’ll die before we reach our destination." Selina looked at her from behind.
"Then walk even faster." Seris did not even turn around.
"You really have a lovely personality."
"I know." The young Pendragon answered without slowing down.
Aren looked at the two of them with tired eyes.
For a moment, something like a smile appeared on his pale face, but it quickly disappeared with the next wave of pain.
That same day, they saw the first real sign.
At first, it was only the sound of growling.
Seris immediately put her hand on her sword, and Selina also raised her mana. One raised its head despite its weakness and turned its antennae toward the sound.
A few minutes later, they reached an open space between the trees.
There were six wolves there.
At first, Seris thought they were sharing prey, but when she got a little closer, her steps slowed.
There was no prey, the wolves were eating each other!

One of them had opened the stomach of an injured wolf with its teeth. That wolf was still alive, its legs struggling against the ground, and yet two other wolves were tearing the flesh from its side without caring about its cries.
The fourth wolf suddenly raised its head from the half-alive body and attacked one of its own companions for no clear reason.
The two rolled across the ground, their teeth sinking into each other’s necks and blood splashing onto the dirt.
"Is this normal here?" Selina frowned.
"No." Seris did not take her eyes off the monsters.
Black veins could be seen under the wolves’ skin.

Their eyes had almost completely turned black, and dark foam was coming from the corners of their mouths. There was no sign of fear, normal hunger or even the instinct to protect the pack in their behavior.
There was only violence.
One of the wolves sensed the Humans and charged directly at them.
Seris drew her sword, and despite her injured body, her attack was still fast, the blade passed through the wolf’s lower stomach and cut through its side almost to its chest.
The monster fell to the ground, but it did not stop, with its stomach open and some of its organs hanging out, it tried to stand again.
She stared at it for a moment, and the monster bit toward her leg.
Selina came from the side, a wave of mana fell onto the wolf’s head and the sound of bones breaking rang out, and the animal’s body finally became still.
She then looked at the corpse with disgust.
"What the hell is this?"
Aren stood behind them, his expression serious.
"This should be the same corruption."
Seris said nothing, but the image of Lian’s purple eyes appeared in her mind for a moment, she had not expected it to start spreading this quickly.
Over the next few days, things became worse.
They saw a group of herbivores attacking each other with their horns and teeth for no understandable reason.
Somewhere else, they saw several hunting monsters of the same species fighting each other to the death, while the fresh corpse of another creature was lying only a few meters away.
On the fifth day, they even came across a group of creatures that were eating the corpses of their own kind while also injuring each other to reach different parts of the body.
The world had changed.
Or perhaps something that had always been hidden under its surface had awakened again.
On the morning of the sixth day, the towers of Vhalaris finally appeared across the gray horizon.
Selina let out a sigh of relief and Aren closed his eyes for a moment, even One raised its antennae a little higher.
But Seris felt no relief, only anger.
Six days, the number repeated in her mind, six damn days for the Black Silence.
Six days for something that had been able to push One and herself aside like toys only moments after its birth.
Six days to do something that they did not even know about yet.
Seris made her steps a little faster, this time Selina said nothing, and when they got close to the city, the first thing they saw was the flags.
The flags of Cinderhold in the east, the forces of Ashenreach in the north and the armies of Emberrol in the southeast.
And groups of Rootcrown forces scattered among the other positions.
The siege was still going on, but something was strange, there was no battle taking place, no sound of siege weapons, no magic explosions and no clash of swords.
The Cindari forces were still in their positions, but instead of advancing, they were only keeping the circle around the city.
A ceasefire, or something close to it, had probably happened.
The reality was almost exactly that.
After the whole world shook, the sky changed color and the strange flames of Heartwood went out, Rindo and Tavern had been forced to enter another negotiation.
No peace had been made and there was no trust, but Maelor, Kael and Tharos were still in the hands of the Humans, and the Cindari were still keeping the siege around the city.
But both sides had reached a simple conclusion.
As long as they did not know what was changing the world itself, killing each other would only make the work of another creature easier.
Rindo had told the Cindari that they had sent a group toward the Forgotten Tree, and one of Tavern’s conditions was also clear.
If Lian’s group returned, the information about the Forgotten Tree had to be shared with them.
They did not know about the truth that their ancestors had hidden.
Seris also did not know about this yet, and before they even reached the first outer gate, movement began around them.
Several groups of Cindari came out from between the trees and ruined buildings.
Ten at first.
Then twenty.
Then more.
Within a few minutes, they were surrounded by a half-circle of armed soldiers.
One even tried to put its body into a defensive position, but one of its legs shook under its weight.
Seris was not in much better condition, but she drew her sword at that moment.
"Put your weapons down." One of the Cindari middle-ranked commanders stepped forward a few steps.
"The city is under siege."
"Surrender."
Seris raised her sword slightly higher, and Selina turned her head toward her.
"Seriously?"
"Yes."
"Do you know that if they attack, we probably won’t last even three seconds?"
Seris looked at the soldiers around them.
"Probably."
"And you’re still not lowering your sword?" Selina waited for a few seconds.
"No."
"Very well." Then she put her hand into her storage space.
"What are you going to take out?" The young Pendragon asked after a little hesitation.
"A way to make sure we don’t die three seconds from now."
An emergency Beacon.
The same thing that Liana and Seraphina had activated in the Glesthorn Forest, and it caused Lian to find them.
