chapters.title: Chapter 363: Reunion I
paragraphs: The Emergency Beacon was an artifact Lian had bought from the black market, and before entering the Special Area, he had given one to each member of his group.
But except for Liana and Seraphina, none of the others had used this thing until now.
Selina placed her finger on the center of the device, mana entered it and light gathered inside it for a moment.
Then a bright pillar shot straight into the sky.
The light opened several hundred meters above them and spread like a huge crown, covering the entire sky around Vhalaris.
The Cindari’s reaction was immediate, swords were drawn, bows were raised and mana gathered in the hands of the mages.
"It’s a war signal!" the commander shouted.
Selina looked at these idiots, had they really taken this thing as a war signal? Of course, they were somewhat right.
If she were in their place, she probably would have reacted the same way.
One of the mages stepped forward, Seris fully raised her guard, the space was only one step away from an explosion.
Then a voice came from far away.
"Wait!" Several people turned around.
Rindo was approaching from the inner positions of the city, almost at the same time, Tavern came out from among the Cindari ranks.
The lower-ranking commanders immediately stepped back.
"It’s him." Selina let out a relieved breath when she saw Rindo and whispered, Seris really had not lied.
Rindo first saw Selina, his steps slowed.
Then Seris.
Aren.
And finally One.
For several moments, he said nothing, the four people standing in front of him did not look like a group that had returned from a difficult mission.
They looked more like people who had been taken by death and then returned for some reason.
One of Seris’s eyes was gone.
Aren had no arms.
One was barely standing on his feet.
And Selina was the only one who looked relatively healthy...but when the group had left this place, this girl had not been with them, so where had they found her?
And one person was missing.
Rindo looked around them once more, behind Seris, behind Selina and even between the trees ...there was no one.
A cold feeling formed in his stomach, where was Lian?
"Are these your people?" Tavern looked closely at the group, then asked him.
"Yeah." Rindo paused for a few seconds.
Tavern’s eyes stayed on Aren without arms, then on One.
"All of them?"
"Yeah, let them in." Rindo stepped forward.
Tavern’s frown became deeper, it was clear that he did not want to let an unknown armed group pass through the blockade without checking them.
But then he raised his hand.
"Open the way."
The soldiers moved aside unwillingly.
Seris did not lower her sword until they had actually passed through the first ring of forces.
When Rindo also moved with them, Tavern’s voice came from behind him.
"Don’t forget our deal."
"I won’t forget." the Student Council President said calmly.
The young Pendragon gave him a short look, but did not ask anything, and as soon as they moved away from the main lines, Rindo said in a low voice.
"For now, don’t say anything, not here." And not long after that, they entered Ashfall, or at least what was left of it.
Then he called several nearby Awakened.
"Take him directly to the infirmary." He pointed at the ant.
Three people carefully stepped forward.
"Be careful, if anything happens to him, I’ll kill you." Seris immediately said.
One of them looked at her remaining eye, her tone made it clear that no further explanation was needed and they barely swallowed.
To move One, they used a wide board and several reinforced ropes and carefully lifted the giant ant.
One could not even protest, his antenna moved toward Seris only once.
"Go." Seris moved her head very slightly.
Aren, Seris and Selina entered the central part of Ashfall with Rindo, what remained of the area was very different from before.
The walls were broken, parts of the streets were buried under rubble, many buildings had burn marks and marks from the roots.
But the Humans were still there, one of the few buildings that was almost undamaged had been turned into the main base.
As soon as they entered, Aren could no longer continue, he sat down beside a wall and then almost let himself fall onto the ground.
"I just... five minutes..." His head rested against the wall, he closed his eyes and said nothing else..
"Did he fall asleep?" Selina looked at him with concern.
"If he’s lucky." Seris answered.
It did not take more than a few minutes before the sound of many footsteps came from outside.
Marcus entered first, then Ethan, Cassian, Liana and finally Seraphina.
Liana’s eyes first fell on Seris, her frown became deeper when she saw her condition, but the moment she turned her head, her entire face froze.
Selina was standing in front of her.
For several seconds, neither of them said anything, she seemed unable to believe what she was seeing.
"Selina...?"
"Liana." Selina gave a very small smile.
Liana’s expression changed at once, shock was replaced by excitement and she ran forward without thinking.
Selina did not even have time to open her arms before Liana hugged her tightly.
"You’re alive!"
The hug was so strong that Selina almost lost her balance for a moment.
"Yeah... apparently."
After a few seconds, she also wrapped her arms around Liana and the small smile on her face was real.
"You’ll have time to catch up later." But Rindo did not let the scene continue any longer.
Liana reluctantly stepped back and the Student Council President stood in the middle of the room, his eyes moving from one person to another.
"Now someone tell me what happened, what happened to you, and where is Lian?"
Seraphina had said almost nothing since entering, but when she heard Lian’s name, all her attention fixed on Seris.
The young Pendragon stayed silent for a few seconds, then, just as she had explained to Selina before, she went straight to the main point.
"Selina was chosen as the host of the Black Silence, Lian got her out of the cocoon, then he took her place, the disaster was born and took Lian’s body, and then it left."
Absolute silence filled the room for several seconds.
Rindo blinked several times and then raised one hand.
"Wait." He carefully started putting the sentences together again.
"Selina was going to become the host of the Black Silence."
Seris nodded.
"Lian took her place."
"Yeah.
"Now the Black Silence is inside Lian’s body."
"Yeah."
"And... it was born too?" Rindo’s frown became deeper.
"Yeah."
The entire room became silent, the amount of information they had learned from those few sentences was so much that understanding it all in a few moments was impossible.
Ethan gave a nervous smile for a moment, but it disappeared very quickly.
Because the meaning of Seris’s words was only now starting to fully sink into everyone’s minds.
"So... what do we do now?" Liana slowly moved away from Selina.
No one answered, how were they supposed to fight a disaster? Especially a disaster that had taken Lian’s body?
Seraphina suddenly moved and before anyone could react, she grabbed Seris by the collar and roughly pulled her one step forward.
"How did you let him do this?"
Everyone turned and looked in shock.
"How could you let him sacrifice himself?!"
Seris’s remaining eye narrowed and Seraphina tightened her grip on her collar.
"Damn it, then why did you go with him?!"
"Shut up." Seris raised her healthy hand and forcefully pushed her arm away.
"And what if I don’t?" Seraphina stepped forward.
The atmosphere in the room suddenly became cold, from Seris’s gaze, despite her injuries and exhaustion, something very dangerous appeared in her only remaining eye.
Even a weak trace of killing intent.
"Alright..." Marcus let out a breath.
"Enough." Rindo quickly stepped between them.
Both of them looked at him.
"Now is not the time for this bullshit, if you want to kill each other, at least let us first find out where the thing that is going to kill all of us is and what exactly we should do about it."
Seraphina pressed her teeth together, but stepped back.
"Isn’t it obvious? We find the disaster, and destroy it." Seris did not take her eyes off her, then said simply.
"The disaster is inside Lian’s body right now." Seraphina immediately replied, her voice was lower this time but there was more anger in it.
"That means if you want to destroy the disaster, you have to destroy Lian too, and we are not doing that, so shut up." Her eyes became cold.
Seris took one step forward and the distance between them became small again.
"If Lian can be saved, we’ll save him." She paused for a moment and then said something that made the room even colder.
"If he can’t... he will just be one of the casualties of this war."
Seraphina’s expression changed, this time her anger went out of control, she went straight toward her.
"We will not hurt him under any circumstances!"
The young Pendragon stood in front of her, there was no retreat in her eyes.
"Then choose, Lian or the world, if we can only save one, which one will you choose?"
Silence filled the room for several seconds, Seraphina opened her mouth, but no answer came out, she pressed her teeth together and closed her fist.
"Seraphina." Rindo said in a low voice.
She turned toward him and this time there was no anger in his voice, and maybe that made it worse.
"Seris is right."
For a moment, Seraphina’s eyes looked truly hurt and the Student Council President continued.
"If the choice really is between one person and the whole world... the choice is clear."
Seraphina gave him a very cold look, she said nothing, but there was no sign that she accepted his words.
In that silence, a short laugh came from somewhere, everyone turned around, Aren was still sitting beside the wall, his eyes were half-open and his laugh sounded more like a tired breath.
"The main problem is not your decision, do you really think you have the power to kill Lian?"

sentences.text: The Emergency Beacon was an artifact Lian had bought from the black market, and before entering the Special Area, he had given one to each member of his group.
But except for Liana and Seraphina, none of the others had used this thing until now.
Selina placed her finger on the center of the device, mana entered it and light gathered inside it for a moment.
Then a bright pillar shot straight into the sky.
The light opened several hundred meters above them and spread like a huge crown, covering the entire sky around Vhalaris.
The Cindari’s reaction was immediate, swords were drawn, bows were raised and mana gathered in the hands of the mages.
"It’s a war signal!" the commander shouted.
Selina looked at these idiots, had they really taken this thing as a war signal?
Of course, they were somewhat right.
If she were in their place, she probably would have reacted the same way.
One of the mages stepped forward, Seris fully raised her guard, the space was only one step away from an explosion.
Then a voice came from far away.
"Wait!" Several people turned around.
Rindo was approaching from the inner positions of the city, almost at the same time, Tavern came out from among the Cindari ranks.
The lower-ranking commanders immediately stepped back.
"It’s him." Selina let out a relieved breath when she saw Rindo and whispered, Seris really had not lied.
Rindo first saw Selina, his steps slowed.
Then Seris.
Aren.
And finally One.
For several moments, he said nothing, the four people standing in front of him did not look like a group that had returned from a difficult mission.
They looked more like people who had been taken by death and then returned for some reason.
One of Seris’s eyes was gone.
Aren had no arms.
One was barely standing on his feet.
And Selina was the only one who looked relatively healthy...but when the group had left this place, this girl had not been with them, so where had they found her?
And one person was missing.
Rindo looked around them once more, behind Seris, behind Selina and even between the trees ...there was no one.
A cold feeling formed in his stomach, where was Lian?
"Are these your people?" Tavern looked closely at the group, then asked him.
"Yeah." Rindo paused for a few seconds.
Tavern’s eyes stayed on Aren without arms, then on One.
"All of them?"
"Yeah, let them in." Rindo stepped forward.
Tavern’s frown became deeper, it was clear that he did not want to let an unknown armed group pass through the blockade without checking them.
But then he raised his hand.
"Open the way."
The soldiers moved aside unwillingly.
Seris did not lower her sword until they had actually passed through the first ring of forces.
When Rindo also moved with them, Tavern’s voice came from behind him.
"Don’t forget our deal."
"I won’t forget." the Student Council President said calmly.
The young Pendragon gave him a short look, but did not ask anything, and as soon as they moved away from the main lines, Rindo said in a low voice.
"For now, don’t say anything, not here." And not long after that, they entered Ashfall, or at least what was left of it.
Then he called several nearby Awakened.
"Take him directly to the infirmary." He pointed at the ant.
Three people carefully stepped forward.
"Be careful, if anything happens to him, I’ll kill you." Seris immediately said.
One of them looked at her remaining eye, her tone made it clear that no further explanation was needed and they barely swallowed.
To move One, they used a wide board and several reinforced ropes and carefully lifted the giant ant.
One could not even protest, his antenna moved toward Seris only once.
"Go." Seris moved her head very slightly.
Aren, Seris and Selina entered the central part of Ashfall with Rindo, what remained of the area was very different from before.
The walls were broken, parts of the streets were buried under rubble, many buildings had burn marks and marks from the roots.
But the Humans were still there, one of the few buildings that was almost undamaged had been turned into the main base.
As soon as they entered, Aren could no longer continue, he sat down beside a wall and then almost let himself fall onto the ground.
"I just... five minutes..." His head rested against the wall, he closed his eyes and said nothing else..
"Did he fall asleep?" Selina looked at him with concern.
"If he’s lucky." Seris answered.
It did not take more than a few minutes before the sound of many footsteps came from outside.
Marcus entered first, then Ethan, Cassian, Liana and finally Seraphina.
Liana’s eyes first fell on Seris, her frown became deeper when she saw her condition, but the moment she turned her head, her entire face froze.
Selina was standing in front of her.
For several seconds, neither of them said anything, she seemed unable to believe what she was seeing.
"Selina...?"
"Liana." Selina gave a very small smile.
Liana’s expression changed at once, shock was replaced by excitement and she ran forward without thinking.
Selina did not even have time to open her arms before Liana hugged her tightly.
"You’re alive!"
The hug was so strong that Selina almost lost her balance for a moment.
"Yeah... apparently."
After a few seconds, she also wrapped her arms around Liana and the small smile on her face was real.
"You’ll have time to catch up later." But Rindo did not let the scene continue any longer.
Liana reluctantly stepped back and the Student Council President stood in the middle of the room, his eyes moving from one person to another.
"Now someone tell me what happened, what happened to you, and where is Lian?"
Seraphina had said almost nothing since entering, but when she heard Lian’s name, all her attention fixed on Seris.
The young Pendragon stayed silent for a few seconds, then, just as she had explained to Selina before, she went straight to the main point.
"Selina was chosen as the host of the Black Silence, Lian got her out of the cocoon, then he took her place, the disaster was born and took Lian’s body, and then it left."
Absolute silence filled the room for several seconds.
Rindo blinked several times and then raised one hand.
"Wait." He carefully started putting the sentences together again.
"Selina was going to become the host of the Black Silence."
Seris nodded.
"Lian took her place."
"Yeah.
"Now the Black Silence is inside Lian’s body."
"Yeah."
"And... it was born too?" Rindo’s frown became deeper.
"Yeah."
The entire room became silent, the amount of information they had learned from those few sentences was so much that understanding it all in a few moments was impossible.
Ethan gave a nervous smile for a moment, but it disappeared very quickly.
Because the meaning of Seris’s words was only now starting to fully sink into everyone’s minds.
"So... what do we do now?" Liana slowly moved away from Selina.
No one answered, how were they supposed to fight a disaster?
Especially a disaster that had taken Lian’s body?
Seraphina suddenly moved and before anyone could react, she grabbed Seris by the collar and roughly pulled her one step forward.
"How did you let him do this?"
Everyone turned and looked in shock.
"How could you let him sacrifice himself?!"
Seris’s remaining eye narrowed and Seraphina tightened her grip on her collar.
"Damn it, then why did you go with him?!"
"Shut up." Seris raised her healthy hand and forcefully pushed her arm away.
"And what if I don’t?" Seraphina stepped forward.
The atmosphere in the room suddenly became cold, from Seris’s gaze, despite her injuries and exhaustion, something very dangerous appeared in her only remaining eye.
Even a weak trace of killing intent.
"Alright..." Marcus let out a breath.
"Enough." Rindo quickly stepped between them.
Both of them looked at him.
"Now is not the time for this bullshit, if you want to kill each other, at least let us first find out where the thing that is going to kill all of us is and what exactly we should do about it."
Seraphina pressed her teeth together, but stepped back.
"Isn’t it obvious?
We find the disaster, and destroy it." Seris did not take her eyes off her, then said simply.
"The disaster is inside Lian’s body right now." Seraphina immediately replied, her voice was lower this time but there was more anger in it.
"That means if you want to destroy the disaster, you have to destroy Lian too, and we are not doing that, so shut up." Her eyes became cold.
Seris took one step forward and the distance between them became small again.
"If Lian can be saved, we’ll save him." She paused for a moment and then said something that made the room even colder.
"If he can’t... he will just be one of the casualties of this war."
Seraphina’s expression changed, this time her anger went out of control, she went straight toward her.
"We will not hurt him under any circumstances!"
The young Pendragon stood in front of her, there was no retreat in her eyes.
"Then choose, Lian or the world, if we can only save one, which one will you choose?"
Silence filled the room for several seconds, Seraphina opened her mouth, but no answer came out, she pressed her teeth together and closed her fist.
"Seraphina." Rindo said in a low voice.
She turned toward him and this time there was no anger in his voice, and maybe that made it worse.
"Seris is right."
For a moment, Seraphina’s eyes looked truly hurt and the Student Council President continued.
"If the choice really is between one person and the whole world... the choice is clear."
Seraphina gave him a very cold look, she said nothing, but there was no sign that she accepted his words.
In that silence, a short laugh came from somewhere, everyone turned around, Aren was still sitting beside the wall, his eyes were half-open and his laugh sounded more like a tired breath.
"The main problem is not your decision, do you really think you have the power to kill Lian?"

chapters.title: Chapter 364: Reunion II
paragraphs: "I don’t know how strong you guys are, but even before that thing took his body, Lian was already a monster on his own." His tired smile disappeared.
"Now? I doubt you can even get close to him." he had never seen the others fight.
But he did not feel that he needed to see it to understand that they could not even compare to Lian, he had seen that man’s power.
Both when he saved him from the prison and during their journey to the Forgotten Tree, and that alone was enough for him to know that these people definitely could not fight him.
What he said was bad enough, but Seris added the next sentence.
"He isn’t alone."
"What do you mean?" Cassian immediately looked at her.
"He has five Cindari with him, you could call them walking corpses, their levels are from thirty-four to thirty-eight."
Their expressions changed, but Seris was not finished yet.
"Cindar Vael is with them too."
"The Founder?" Rindo frowned.
"Yeah."
"How? Wasn’t he supposed to be dead? How is he still alive?"
"I don’t know either." Unlike Lian, she did not know the truth and did not know how something that was supposed to be dead was still alive.
"At least you know his level, right?"
"He is Level 38."
Then Seris gave them a short explanation.
About the five walking corpses that had appeared beside the tree.
About how one of them was the same corpse of Cindar who was known as the Founder of the Cindari and should have been dead, but for reasons she did not know, he was still alive, at least in some way.
About how the other four had levels much higher than theirs, and how after the birth of the Black Silence, all of them had left the place together with Lian’s body.
When the explanation ended, the room became silent again for a short time, the news was bad, very, very bad, and the more they heard, the more they understood how bad the situation was.
"We can’t fight them." Marcus said simply.
No one disagreed, because there was nothing to disagree with.
During the siege of Vhalaris, they had already used almost all their forces just to hold back enemies weaker than those five.
The level difference was not just a number.
Physical strength, speed, mana, skills, ability to take hits, all of them grew with level.
Even having more people was not a guarantee, several of those present clearly looked hopeless, and they had every reason to feel that way.
What could they do against five beings who were at least 15 levels higher than all of them? If they tried very hard, maybe all of them could barely stop one of them.
But defeat one? Impossible.
Fight all five of them? It was not even possible in their dreams.
And besides those five, there was also a disaster with the power to destroy the world.
But Seris noticed one exception.
Seraphina, she was angry, she was worried, but she did not have that completely hopeless look, there was something in her mind, something she still did not want to share with the others.
Seris noticed it, but did not ask anything and Ethan finally broke the silence.
"I have a suggestion."
Everyone looked at him, hoping to hear a really good suggestion.
"Let’s ignore all of this, saving the world? Screw that, let’s find the Key and get out of this hell."
For several seconds, no one spoke, as if they were not sure whether he was joking or not and then, after making sure he was serious, they gave him meaningful looks.
"What? I’m just bringing up the options." Ethan raised his hands slightly.
"We don’t know where the Key is." Rindo said.
"Wasn’t it supposed to be near the Forgotten Tree?" Ethan asked in confusion and then looked at Seris.
"Didn’t you find anything there?"
"No." She thought for a few moments and then answered.
Now that she thought about it, according to normal logic, there should have been a Key at the most central point of the world, which meant the Forgotten Tree.
At least that was the normal standard, but there was nothing like that there.
"Great." Ethan let out a disappointed breath and Rindo moved closer to the large map on the table.
"In any case, we can’t ignore this situation, if we don’t stop the disaster, it will eventually find a way into our world."
"But how are we supposed to fight them?" Liana asked.
"You don’t need to fight the disaster, hold back the five Cindari, I’ll face Lian." This time Seris answered.
"Alone?" Rindo frowned.
"Yeah."
"Are you sure?"
"Do you have another way?" Seris slightly raised her healthy shoulder and then her tone became calmer.
"I’ve fought Lian once before, I can do it one more time." The truth was that she knew better than anyone how incomplete those words were.
The creature she had faced beside the tree was not just Lian, the strike that had thrown One dozens of meters away, the hand that had stopped Seris’s sword without using any skill.
The difference in power had not even allowed a real battle to begin.
She knew all of this, but she did not need to say it now.

"Let’s make one thing clear, we are not going to defeat those five, we simply can’t, even if we have more people, the level difference is too large." Rindo looked at her for several seconds and then said, and finally added.
"I don’t know how you and Lian fight enemies fifteen levels above you, but the rest of us don’t have that ability."
"At best, with numbers, suitable ground, traps and a few tricks, we can hold them back for a few minutes."
"Can I trust you that those few minutes will be enough?" He then asked directly.
"Enough." Seris did not hesitate even for a moment.
Rindo held her gaze for several seconds and then nodded.
"Then before that, everyone needs to become as strong as possible." He looked at the others.
"Most of us reached Level eighteen or nineteen after the siege, anyone who has not reached twenty yet must reach it tonight."
"We can also choose several groups from the strongest remaining Awakened." Cassian said.
"Only people who, if someone Level thirty-five appears in front of them, will at least not run away or die within a few seconds." Rindo agreed.
"That’s a very hopeful standard." Ethan said with a raised eyebrow.
"It’s a realistic standard." Marcus said.
Rindo turned back to the map, but after a few seconds Ethan spoke again.
"One more small problem."
"What is it this time?" Marcus asked tiredly.
"Where are we going to look for him?"
Everyone stopped, he was right, six days had passed, the Black Silence could have gone anywhere in this small world.
And they had no way to find or track it either, so where were they supposed to find it?
The silence continued for several seconds until Seris finally said.
"Maybe I know."
She opened the Main Quest panel, the familiar text appeared in front of her.
[Main Quest: Prevent the complete awakening of the Corrupted Titan.]
She looked at it for several seconds and then added.
"Our main goal was never to save the Forgotten Tree, even stopping the birth of that cocoon was not the main goal." She pointed at the main quest line with her finger.
"This was the goal from the beginning."
Rindo also opened his own panel, his eyes stayed on the same sentence.
Despite the death of the tree, despite the birth of the disaster, despite the fact that the cocoon no longer existed, the quest description had still not changed.
The Corrupted Titan.
Now that he thought about it, it was strange, because in a way they should have failed the Quest after the disaster was released.
But no such announcement had appeared and the Main Quest still existed, and that could only mean one thing.
"So it’s not over yet." Rindo said quietly.
Seris nodded.
"That’s right." Then she said what she had been thinking about during the entire journey.
"I think part of the Black Silence is still inside the Titan."
"If that is true, then the thing that took Lian’s body is not complete." The Student Council President also thought for a moment.

chapters.title: Chapter 365: Reunion ( Final )
paragraphs: Part of their Quest was to stop the Titan from awakening before the tree died, but the real objective was to stop the Corrupted Titan from awakening.
So as long as they can stop the Titan from awakening, there may still be a chance, a chance to save everything.
The reasoning seemed logical, at least considering that the Main Quest was still available.
"Probably." Seris said.
"And if it wants to become complete, it has to return to the remaining part." Rindo continued.
"Exactly."
Finally, they had something that looked like a path, and if their guess was correct, their destination would be the Giant Graveyard.
Although it was only a guess, it was all they had, it might be wrong, but they had no choice except to check it.
"So maybe we still have a chance." Rindo took a deep breath.
"If we reach it before it releases the remaining part, maybe we can stop it from becoming complete." Cassian said.
"Decision made, we move tomorrow." The Student Council President nodded and then looked at Seris and Aren.
"But you two need to go to the infirmary first."
Seris immediately raised an eyebrow, but Rindo continued before she could object.
"I’m not discussing this, I’ll send every healer who can still stand, we’ll use every remaining medicine and healing tool we have."
Seris said nothing, she knew Rindo was right, if she faced Lian with her current body, the result would be even shorter than last time.
With all the healers using their healing powers on the two of them, her eye and Aren’s two arms had to be fully restored so they could use them again.
For the final battle ahead, a battle that could decide the fate of two worlds, all of them needed to be at their best.
"One will also be treated, by tomorrow we’ll restore as much of his body as possible." Rindo continued, that ant could also be a great help.
Seris only nodded and the meeting seemed to be over, several people were about to leave the room when Seraphina’s voice came.
"If the goal of this mission is to kill Lian, I’m not coming."
Everyone suddenly stopped and looked back at the person who had spoken.
"The first goal is to save him, first we will check whether we can separate the Black Silence from him or not." Rindo frowned and then his tone became heavier.
"If the answer is no... you have to accept that maybe there is no Lian left anymore." He did not want to give false hope.
Seraphina stayed silent for a long time, her eyes moved from Rindo to Seris and then to the floor, as if she was fighting something inside herself and finally let out a sigh.
"Fine, as long as we really try to save him, I’ll help." Then she paused.
"And maybe I have a way to suppress those five Cindari for a while."
Several people looked at her at the same time.
"How?" Rindo asked.
"If the place we are going to really has the Corrupted Titan, maybe it can be done." Seraphina did not answer directly, more exactly, she herself did not seem sure.
"What kind of help?" But the Student Council President seemed doubtful.
"You’ll find out later."
Seris looked at her for several seconds, the same feeling again, Seraphina knew something, but she clearly did not want to say it now.
’Could it be related to the inheritance she received?’ She thought for a moment, no matter how annoying this girl was, she had received a great inheritance.
The inheritance of a being that had managed to defeat and seal the Black Silence disaster once, many years ago.
That was why Seris truly did not underestimate her.
"Okay." Rindo finally nodded.
And finally, everyone left the place...
That night, Seris was lying in the Ashfall infirmary.

Several healers had taken turns working on the wounds on her body. Her broken ribs had mostly healed, her broken wrist had been put back into the correct position and the muscle damage caused by putting too much pressure on her body was quickly healing.
But her left eye was still hidden behind a layer of cloth and healing covering.
It was not supposed to return this quickly, according to the healers, it could take until morning.
The room was almost dark, but she could not sleep, a small panel opened in front of her only healthy eye.
[Evolution Goal: Kill the Disaster.]
Seris looked at the same sentence for a long time, then the image of Lian came to her mind.
Not normal Lian, but the thing that had come out of the cocoon.
Purple eyes, an empty look, the strike that had slammed One into the tree.
Then herself, the hand that had caught her sword, the slap, the broken wrist and finally that pause.
She brought her eyebrows together.
Why did he not kill them?
If the Black Silence had truly taken full control, what reason did it have to leave ready food behind?
One.
Seris herself.
Aren.
Selina.
All of them were alive, all of them were weak, none of them could stop it, but it left and ignored them.
Was it because of mercy? Or did that disaster not even consider them worthy of being called insects? Or... was it resistance from the real Lian?
Seris closed the panel.
If she had to, could she really push her sword into Lian’s heart?
She did not answer.
Because she had not been forced to yet and until she was forced to, she did not want to know the answer.
In the morning, Ashfall seemed calmer than the night before, but this calm was not real, it was only the silence before another movement.
Seris came out of the infirmary.
Her body had recovered from all the injuries. Her mana had completely returned and she no longer felt a sharp pain in her side with every step and her lost eye had finally returned as well.
Aren was also in much better condition, the color had returned to his face and his mana was no longer dangerously low, his two arms had also returned.
One had also managed to stand on his own feet again.
His movement was still a little slow and several large cracks remained on his natural armor, but compared to six days ago, he looked almost like a different creature.

Rindo.
Marcus.
Cassian.
Ethan.
Liana.
Seraphina.
Selina.
Seris.
Aren.
One.
And several other Awakened who had been chosen from among the strongest remaining people.
Everyone was ready to move.
Rindo looked at the people in front of him, they were about to begin the journey to the Giant Graveyard.
They were going toward a creature that Lian might still be alive inside, or maybe there was nothing left of him anymore, they were going to a place they might never return from alive.
He opened his mouth to give the order to move, but before he could say even one word, the sound of running came from one of the side streets.
An Awakened was running toward them at full speed, his face had no color, part of his clothes was covered in blood.

"Sir!"
"What happened?"
The man tried to control his breathing, but could not.
"Something very bad happened."
"What?" Rindo’s frown became deeper.
The Awakened looked behind him for a moment, there was real fear in his eyes.
"Everyone..."
He took another breath.
"Everyone is attacking each other."
Several people changed their stance at the same time.
"What? Who? Why?" Marcus asked.
"The Awakened, the western barracks... the infirmary... even the guards." The man answered.
From not far away, a loud scream was heard, then the sound of breaking glass, then another scream.
"They’re killing each other! For no reason! One moment they’re normal, then suddenly it’s like they lose their minds!" The Awakened continued.
At that moment, the sound of an emergency horn rose from outside Ashfall, everyone turned their heads.
Once.
Then a second time.
And a third.

Everyone knew that sound, but the horn was not an attack signal from the Humans, this time it was an internal warning from the Cindari, which meant something had also happened on the other side of the walls.
Several more screams came from the streets of Ashfall.
Seris stood completely still, the images from the past six days returned to her mind one after another.
Wolves tearing open the stomachs of their own kind.
Monsters fighting their own groups for no reason.
Creatures that, even after their bodies were torn open, only thought about killing.

Seris took her eyes away from the street and looked at the blood-red sky above Vhalaris, the sounds of fighting inside the city were becoming louder.
And outside the walls, the emergency horns of the Cindari continued to sound one after another.
"It has started, those monsters we saw on the way, all of them were going crazy." Seris’s voice became colder.
The sound of a sword hitting something came from one of the nearby buildings, followed by a painful scream, now she knew exactly what had happened.
The Forgotten Tree was dead.
The disaster had been born.
And now the same nightmare that had brought this world to the edge of destruction years ago was spreading again.
Seris looked at the sky one last time.
"The Black Silence is infecting this entire world again."

sentences.text: Part of their Quest was to stop the Titan from awakening before the tree died, but the real objective was to stop the Corrupted Titan from awakening.
So as long as they can stop the Titan from awakening, there may still be a chance, a chance to save everything.
The reasoning seemed logical, at least considering that the Main Quest was still available.
"Probably." Seris said.
"And if it wants to become complete, it has to return to the remaining part." Rindo continued.
"Exactly."
Finally, they had something that looked like a path, and if their guess was correct, their destination would be the Giant Graveyard.
Although it was only a guess, it was all they had, it might be wrong, but they had no choice except to check it.
"So maybe we still have a chance." Rindo took a deep breath.
"If we reach it before it releases the remaining part, maybe we can stop it from becoming complete." Cassian said.
"Decision made, we move tomorrow." The Student Council President nodded and then looked at Seris and Aren.
"But you two need to go to the infirmary first."
Seris immediately raised an eyebrow, but Rindo continued before she could object.
"I’m not discussing this, I’ll send every healer who can still stand, we’ll use every remaining medicine and healing tool we have."
Seris said nothing, she knew Rindo was right, if she faced Lian with her current body, the result would be even shorter than last time.
With all the healers using their healing powers on the two of them, her eye and Aren’s two arms had to be fully restored so they could use them again.
For the final battle ahead, a battle that could decide the fate of two worlds, all of them needed to be at their best.
"One will also be treated, by tomorrow we’ll restore as much of his body as possible." Rindo continued, that ant could also be a great help.
Seris only nodded and the meeting seemed to be over, several people were about to leave the room when Seraphina’s voice came.
"If the goal of this mission is to kill Lian, I’m not coming."
Everyone suddenly stopped and looked back at the person who had spoken.
"The first goal is to save him, first we will check whether we can separate the Black Silence from him or not." Rindo frowned and then his tone became heavier.
"If the answer is no... you have to accept that maybe there is no Lian left anymore." He did not want to give false hope.
Seraphina stayed silent for a long time, her eyes moved from Rindo to Seris and then to the floor, as if she was fighting something inside herself and finally let out a sigh.
"Fine, as long as we really try to save him, I’ll help." Then she paused.
"And maybe I have a way to suppress those five Cindari for a while."
Several people looked at her at the same time.
"How?" Rindo asked.
"If the place we are going to really has the Corrupted Titan, maybe it can be done." Seraphina did not answer directly, more exactly, she herself did not seem sure.
"What kind of help?" But the Student Council President seemed doubtful.
"You’ll find out later."
Seris looked at her for several seconds, the same feeling again, Seraphina knew something, but she clearly did not want to say it now.
’Could it be related to the inheritance she received?’ She thought for a moment, no matter how annoying this girl was, she had received a great inheritance.
The inheritance of a being that had managed to defeat and seal the Black Silence disaster once, many years ago.
That was why Seris truly did not underestimate her.
"Okay." Rindo finally nodded.
And finally, everyone left the place...
That night, Seris was lying in the Ashfall infirmary.
Several healers had taken turns working on the wounds on her body.
Her broken ribs had mostly healed, her broken wrist had been put back into the correct position and the muscle damage caused by putting too much pressure on her body was quickly healing.
But her left eye was still hidden behind a layer of cloth and healing covering.
It was not supposed to return this quickly, according to the healers, it could take until morning.
The room was almost dark, but she could not sleep, a small panel opened in front of her only healthy eye.
[Evolution Goal: Kill the Disaster.]
Seris looked at the same sentence for a long time, then the image of Lian came to her mind.
Not normal Lian, but the thing that had come out of the cocoon.

Then herself, the hand that had caught her sword, the slap, the broken wrist and finally that pause.
She brought her eyebrows together.
Why did he not kill them?
If the Black Silence had truly taken full control, what reason did it have to leave ready food behind?
One.
Seris herself.
Aren.
Selina.

chapters.title: Chapter 366: Spreading Calamity I
paragraphs: "The Black Silence is infecting this whole world again."
Seris’s voice was still echoing through the square when a scream came from the western street. Almost at the same time, everyone turned their heads.
A blood-covered man ran out from around the corner of the street. One hand was pressed against his torn side, and with the other, he tried to keep his sword behind him.
"Don’t let him get close to me! Help me!" Only a few meters behind him, another Awakened was running after him.
The second man showed no clear sign of corruption. His skin looked normal, his eyes had not turned black, and there were no strange veins visible on his body.
But the look on his face was not normal.

His face was so full of anger that it looked like someone had killed the person he loved most right in front of him. The veins on his forehead were visible, and he held his blade above his head with both hands.
"It was you!"
"What are you talking about?!" The injured man stepped back in fear.
"You wanted to kill me from the beginning!"
"I don’t even know what you’re talking about!"
The attacker ignored his answer, and his sword came down.
Seris moved at that exact moment.
Her body was no longer falling apart like the day before, and the treatment from last night had brought her speed back. In a few short steps, she moved between the two.
The attacker’s sword was still coming down when Seris turned her body, and instead of using the blade, she struck the man directly on the temple with the handle of her sword.
A dull sound came out, the man’s eyes lost focus for a moment, and his body fell to the ground.
"Don’t kill anyone!" Rindo shouted immediately.
Several Awakened who had already drawn their weapons stopped.
"Restrain them first! We still don’t know if this condition can be reversed."
Seris bent down and looked at the unconscious man, and a few seconds later, the system finally reacted.
[Corruption of the Calamity detected.]
Her eyes narrowed, and more messages appeared.
[Type: Black Silence Corruption]
[Stage: Initial]
[Recorded Signs:]
[Increased Aggression]
[Extreme Suspicion]
[Distorted Perception]
[Reduced Behavioral Control]
Then the final warning appeared.
[Warning.]
[Continued corruption may lead to a complete collapse of reason.]
Seris stared at the words without moving for several seconds.
So this was what they had seen on the way, the wolves that tore open the stomachs of their own kind.
The creatures that attacked each other for no reason, the monsters that kept thinking only about killing even after their stomachs had been torn open.
Those were the final stages, what was lying in front of her now was only the beginning, and that might have been the most frightening part of all.
The injured man barely managed to reach the wall.
"I didn’t do anything to him." His voice was shaking.
"I swear. We were on guard duty together last night. We even ate together."
"Was there any problem between you before this?" Rindo asked.
"We argued over the division of potions a few days ago." The man thought for a few moments.
"That’s all?"
"Yeah."
Seris kept her eyes on the unconscious man, so the Black Silence did not create hatred from nothing.
It found something that was already there, a small annoyance, an old doubt, jealousy, fear, anger, and then it pulled it, twisted it and made it so large that it consumed all of a person’s reason.
Another scream came from the direction of the medical center, followed by the sound of something breaking...
"Damn it." Rindo raised his head.
Seris picked up her sword.
"The medical center."
Liana immediately moved with her.
The situation inside the medical center was even worse.
Two healers were fighting in the middle of the hall. One of them was the woman who had spent several hours working on Seris’s wounds last night.
"You kept all of it for yourselves!" The same woman was now holding an empty bottle and shouting with a red face.
"What?" Another healer stepped back.
"The potions!"
"There are no more potions!"
The woman threw the bottle toward his head.
"Don’t lie! I saw you!"
On the other side of the room, a man who should have been treating an injured soldier had both hands placed on the patient’s chest.
But instead of healing, his mana was entering the man’s mana channels in an unstable way, and the patient screamed in pain.
"Stop! What are you doing?!"
"If I heal you, you’ll kill me later." The healer stepped back with terrified eyes.
"What?!"
"You’re all going to do the same thing."
Seris moved forward and grabbed the healer’s wrist, the man turned around and tried to punch her without thinking.
Seris simply moved her body to the side and knocked him unconscious with one strike to the neck.
At the same time, the female healer attacked her coworker, Liana moved between them, and the woman tried to scratch her face while screaming.
"You’re with them too!"
"I don’t even know who you mean by them!" Liana grabbed her wrist.
The woman attacked with her knee, Liana blocked it, twisted her arm and, despite her strong resistance, forced her down onto the floor.
A few moments later, two Awakened entered and tied the woman’s hands.
Liana let out a breath, and for a moment, she looked at the same woman who had saved several people’s lives last night.
"Yesterday, she was treating people."
"Today, she thinks those same people want to kill her." Seris answered.
Liana looked at her, and Seris stayed silent for a few seconds.
"The Calamity doesn’t create something new inside your mind, it only finds what is already there." Her eyes fell on the unconscious healer.
"Then it makes it so big that nothing else is left."
Liana’s face slowly became more serious, if this analysis was correct, no one was completely safe, every human had something inside them.
Fear.
Anger.
Jealousy.
Hatred.
Guilt.
Even love, if it was twisted in a sick way, could turn into something dangerous.
Seris thought of Seraphina for a moment, then immediately pushed that thought away.
Rindo created a new system in less than ten minutes.
Every street was checked by groups of three. No one was allowed to move alone, and everyone was required to report even the smallest strange behavior from their companions.
"Take their weapons first." His voice could be heard from the central square.
"Then restrain them, and keep the corrupted people separated."
"What if they resist?" one of the Awakened asked.
"Keep them alive if you can, only kill them when there is no other way to save yourselves or the others." They had no idea whether this condition could be reversed or treated.
And until they knew that, he did not want to kill their own kind, the best thing was to capture anyone who had been corrupted.
But there was a question ... how did someone even become corrupted?
Then he turned toward Cassian.
"Double the guards around the Cindari prisoners."
Cassian immediately understood what he meant.
If a corrupted Awakened entered the prison and killed Maelor, Kael or Tharos, the temporary ceasefire would be destroyed in an instant.
"What about the guards? What if they become corrupted?" Cassian asked.
"Change the groups every thirty minutes, no guard stays with the prisoners without two others beside him." Rindo answered.
Then his eyes moved toward the chaotic streets, Ashfall had been relatively quiet for the first time in a long while only a few minutes ago, and now screams were coming from three different streets.
And outside the walls, the Cindari emergency horns still did not stop.
But unfortunately, the problems did not end there.
Tavern entered the negotiation area half an hour later, this time he had no ceremony with him and had come with only two officers.
His black armor was covered with blood in several places, and his large blade still had a red mark on it, but the blood did not belong to him.
He walked directly toward Rindo.
"Is this your doing?"
"If it were our doing, why are our own people killing each other?"
Tavern looked into Ashfall, two Humans in the distance were restraining a man who was screaming that everyone around him was a traitor.
The Cindari commander still said nothing, the trust between them was so low that even such a scene was not enough to convince him.
But at that exact moment, one of the Cindari officers behind Tavern moved.
Seris was the first to notice the change in his expression, the officer put his hand on his sword, while the commander was still facing Rindo.
The blade came out and Seris opened her mouth.
"Behind—"
Tavern noticed it himself, his body turned and the officer’s sword struck the flat side of Tavern’s large sword with a heavy sound.
"You sold us out!" The officer’s eyes were full of anger.
"What?" Tavern froze for a moment.
The officer attacked again.
"Ever since those outsiders came, we have only been retreating!"
The blades collided.
"They took our commanders and you did nothing but talk!"
"Drop your weapon." Tavern knocked the blade away with one movement of his sword.
"Traitor!"
This time, the officer attacked directly at his neck, the Cindari commander no longer had time to hold back.
He stepped forward, let the attack pass beside his face and struck the officer directly in the jaw with the handle of his large sword.
The man fell to the ground and became unconscious.
A strange silence formed between the Humans and Cindari present, and the Cindari commander told his other officer to take this corrupted one away.
Rindo looked at the fallen officer for a few seconds and then at Tavern.
"Do you still think this is our doing?"
Tavern did not answer, there was something in the Cindari commander’s eyes that did not look like doubt.
It was fear, not fear for himself, but fear of something much bigger.
"Our camp is falling apart from the inside." He said a few seconds later.
"Ashfall is the same." The Student Council President answered calmly.
"We had three other cases, and this is the fourth." Tavern looked at the unconscious officer.
"They will become more common, if this is the same thing we saw on the way, in a few hours it will be much harder to contain them." Seris said.

Tavern did not answer, there was something in the Cindari commander’s eyes that did not look like doubt.
It was fear, not fear for himself, but fear of something much bigger.
"Our camp is falling apart from the inside." He said a few seconds later.
"Ashfall is the same." The Student Council President answered calmly.
"We had three other cases, and this is the fourth." Tavern looked at the unconscious officer.
"They will become more common, if this is the same thing we saw on the way, in a few hours it will be much harder to contain them." Seris said.

chapters.title: Chapter 367: Spreading Calamity II
paragraphs: "What do you mean, the path? Have you seen something like this before?" Tavern asked with a frown.

"We were in the forest for six days, and during that time I saw many things, at first the monsters were attacking each other, and in the end we saw creatures from the same pack eating each other, even when there was food right beside them."
"Their goal was not hunger, they just wanted to kill."
Tavern stayed silent for a long time, then said something very quietly.
"When the beast ate its brother, the cities closed their gates, when the intelligent ones killed their brothers... there were no cities left."
A short silence followed, the sentence described the current situation very well.
"What is that?" Rindo asked.
"An old saying, something our children hear from the older generations." Then a kind of bitterness appeared in his voice.
"Until today, I thought it was just a legend."
Seris understood that even ordinary Cindari people had kept pieces of the First Calamity in the form of stories and warnings passed down from one generation to another.
But the truth had become so old that no one believed it anymore, now the legend was alive in front of their eyes.
Tavern then left after making sure that they were not responsible for what had happened there, he had to return and deal with the situation.
After he left, the two of them also returned to the main base.
"We move right now." Then Seris looked directly at Rindo and said.
"In this situation?"
"Exactly because of this situation, if we wait until tomorrow, maybe half of your people will no longer be themselves."
"And every hour, the number of people we can trust becomes smaller." Cassian, who was standing a little farther away, nodded.
Rindo looked around, several infected people had been restrained in the distance.

The sound of fighting was still coming from the western part of the city, then his eyes fell on one of the report panels, almost everyone who had been infected until that moment had one thing in common.
They were weak, and in terms of level and power, they were all among the weakest people left.
"There is one more thing, so far none of the high-level people have shown any signs." Then he mentioned this point.
"All the cases we recorded were from the weaker groups." Cassian confirmed.
"So either stronger Awakened are more resistant to the infection..." Seris thought for a moment.
"Or the infection is not strong enough yet to affect us too." Rindo continued.
Neither of these two possibilities was comforting, the first only meant that the weaker ones would fall first, the second meant that the stronger ones had not been affected yet.
"Then someone has to stay here." Marcus put his arm across his chest.
"Please don’t say me." Ethan looked at him.
"You two are staying." Rindo looked at them and said, one person was enough to control the situation, but it was better for two people to stay just to be safe.
"Great." Ethan sighed.
"Marcus, you handle the internal defense, Ethan, coordinate the restraint groups and the medical center."
"Me?" Ethan raised an eyebrow.
"Yeah."
"Why?"
Rindo gave him a short look.
"Because unlike the things that come out of your mouth, when things really get bad, you don’t run away."
"That was a terrible compliment." Ethan stayed silent for a few seconds and then shrugged.
"Don’t worry. I’ll translate it for you. He means he trusts you." Marcus said.
"That made it worse."
The atmosphere became a little lighter for a few seconds, but only for a few seconds, another scream came from the distance and everyone remembered why they were standing there.
"The weaker people stay inside Ashfall, the stronger people either come with us or stay to defend the city." The Student Council President said in the end.
Seris looked at the blood-red sky, for the first time she fully understood what could happen if Black Silence reached Earth.
At first, maybe only a few humans would become more aggressive.
Then a few murders.
Then cities.
Armies.
Countries.
Billions of humans with fears, hatred, and grudges that the Calamity could turn into weapons.
Black Silence did not even need to destroy the cities itself, it only needed to make the people destroy them by themselves.
"If this thing enters our world..." Cassian also seemed to be thinking about something similar and said quietly.
He did not finish his sentence, there was no need.
"It must not enter." Rindo said seriously.
This time no one disagreed.
Even Seraphina, whatever disagreement they had about Lian, one truth did not change.
If the Calamity found a way to Earth, they might no longer have a chance to save anyone.
They did not have much time to prepare, the main group gathered their things in less than an hour.
Seris sat on One, the ant’s body was still not completely healed, but it moved much better than the day before and was able to carry one person.
Aren was also placed on a mount taken from the Cindari, with the help of one of the Awakened.
Seraphina, Liana, Cassian, and Selina were ready.
Rindo was giving his final orders to Marcus and Ethan when Tavern’s voice came from behind him.
"Where are you going?"
Rindo turned around, Tavern was standing there in the same blood-covered armor.
Beside him was the same young woman in the white Rootcrown robe who had been with him during the first negotiation, and several other high-level soldiers were also standing behind them.
"We’re going to stop whatever started this chaos."
"Where?" Tavern looked at him for a few seconds and then asked seriously.
"Are you going to stop us?" Rindo did not answer directly.
Several Cindari’s hands unconsciously moved toward their weapons and Seris also gave Tavern a cold look.
"No, I’m coming with you." But after a few seconds of silence, the Cindari commander said.
This time several Humans clearly frowned, the young Pendragon said nothing, but her hand tightened around the handle of her sword.
"Why?" The Student Council President asked.
Tavern looked at the walls of Vhalaris, the city his army had come to take back, now it was falling apart from the inside even without a war.
"If there really is no way out of this world, just as you told me, then I will at least try to save what is left."
Six days ago, before the temporary truce was made, Rindo had told the Cindari many times that they really did not know a way out of this world.
The Cindari still believed that the only way to save their race was to escape from this world, and they did not know the real truth that their leaders had hidden from them.
At that time Tavern had not believed Rindo’s words, but now he had no other choice, and besides, the evidence showed that these humans really were trapped here.
"I came here to save my race, if the way to save it is not escape, then maybe we have to save this world."
"If you want to come, that is your choice, but you do not give us orders in the middle of the mission." Then Rindo shrugged.
Tavern nodded and then raised his hand, eight Cindari separated from the forces.
All of them were high-level units, a swordsman, a mage, two heavy soldiers and a root controller, two archers and the same white-robed Rootcrown woman.
Seris focused on the woman for a few seconds, from their first meeting she had noticed that her mana presence was strange.
Dense, controlled, and very calm, but she still did not know what her role was.
"These are enough." Then the Cindari commander said calmly.
Rindo gave his people a short look, in his opinion, every extra person meant a few more seconds against the moving dead.
And in a battle where the whole plan was based on buying time, a few seconds could be the difference between victory and destruction.
"We move."
The Ashfall gate opened.
Humans and Cindari moved along the same path for the first time, not on two sides of a battlefield.
Not as friends, not as allies who trusted each other, but only as creatures that had finally understood that if the Calamity won, there would be nothing left for them to fight over.
One moved his legs forward, Seris was the only one sitting on his back, the wind gently moved her hair aside and her eyes were fixed on the horizon.
Somewhere in the distance, the Giant Graveyard was located, and Lian was probably there too, her fingers slowly tightened around the handle of her sword.
The same question was still in her mind.
Was Lian alive? Or was only his body left?
She had no answer.
But what she had seen when she came out of the cocoon was still fixed in her mind.
Purple eyes, inhuman coldness, One being thrown away with a single strike and then—
That pause.
"Lian... we’re coming." Seris’s eye became colder.
At the same time, very far from Vhalaris, there was no wind.
The Giant Graveyard was covered in heavy silence, the Titan was still trapped under the ground and rocks.
Its body stretched like a huge mountain range across the graveyard, and seven ancient chains had pinned different parts of its body to the ground.
One of the chains slowly shook.
Only once.
Then again...and the sound of metal spread through the silence of the graveyard.
A human hand was placed on the surface of the chain, the fingers slowly moved over the ancient writings.
A purple light shone in the darkness and a voice that once belonged to Lian Vorhelm said without the slightest emotion.
"Finally."
For a moment, nothing happened.
Then—
Crack.
A very thin crack appeared on the first ring of one of the seven chains.

chapters.title: Chapter 368: The City Of Crystaline
paragraphs: Vhalaris was still visible behind them when Tavern opened an old map on the saddle of his mount. The lines on the map were old, but the military routes of the Cindari were marked much more carefully than the normal roads.
"I thought we should go through the same border that Lian and the others used before, if I’m not mistaken, its name was Cindervein." Rindo, who was moving beside him, looked at the map and said.
He did not know exactly which passage they had used before and only knew its name.
"If we take that route, we’ll lose more time." Tavern moved his finger along a thin line without looking up and then tapped another route.
"If we go from here, we’ll arrive in less than two days."
"Two days?" Rindo raised an eyebrow.
Tavern nodded.

"The Forgotten Tree is almost at the center of this world, and from there there are paths to all three forests. There is even a direct path from there to the Giant Forest and then the Giant Graveyard."
"But from where we are now to the tree itself is almost four days away. Going there would only waste time."
"Then what’s the faster route?" Seris, who was sitting on One’s back, gave the map a short look.
"We leave through the eastern military route, enter Glassthorn, pass by Crystaline, and go directly into the Giant Forest."Tavern added and then looked at the others.
"From there, the Giant Graveyard isn’t very far."
"Crystaline..." Rindo thought for a few seconds, this was the first time he had heard the name of such a place.
"It’s a city belonging to the natives of Glassthorn." Tavern looked at him.
"Not all the Awakened appeared in Emberroot, many of them must have fallen in Glassthorn from the beginning." The Student Council President thought for a moment.
This possibility clearly caught his attention.
The number of Awakened who had entered the Special Area had reached several hundred, but only around a few dozen were present in Emberroot.

So the rest were clearly scattered across the other forests and if they were still alive, they might be able to find valuable forces there, and that was why he asked if a short stop in Glassthorn was possible.
"Don’t count on it too much." Tavern quickly lowered his hopes.
"Why?"

"The people of Glassthorn have always been isolated, they don’t have a good relationship with outsiders, even before the world became like this, they barely let anyone enter their city, and now? If the corruption has also spread there, I doubt they’ll even let you get close to the gate."
Rindo stayed silent for a few seconds, if that was true, the chance that other Awakened had managed to enter the city would also become lower.
Even so, they were not going to change their route just to check this.
Simply passing around Crystaline would be enough to find out what had happened there.
The group continued moving without stopping.
The effect of Black Silence could be seen almost along the entire route.
Several hours later, they passed a group of beasts lying on the dry road. No hunter had killed them.
Each one had marks from the teeth and claws of its own kind on its body.
Two larger monsters had fallen on top of each other a little farther away.
One of them had pushed its jaws into the other’s throat until the last moment, and the other had pushed its claws through its opponent’s stomach.
Both were dead, but even in death they had not separated.
Selina did not take her eyes off them for a few moments.
"They’re getting worse."
"Maybe we’re just seeing the next stages." Aren, who was sitting on another mount, said quietly.
A little later, their path passed by a small village, while it was expected that apart from the five cities, the Cindari did not live anywhere else, but this way of thinking was wrong.
There were also small villages, but their population barely reached a few dozen people and most of them were built near fertile areas and mines so they could watch over those places.
Several stone houses, a small square and corpses lying in the streets.
There were no signs of an army or monster attack, everyone had been killed with their own weapons.
Seris kept her eyes on a man for a few moments, a short sword was stuck in his chest.
A few steps away from him, a woman had fallen, her hands were still wrapped around the handle of the same sword.
"Mom!" Then a voice came from a half-ruined house.
The group slowed down.
"Mom, open the door! I’m fine now!"
"I swear I’m fine!" The boy was hitting the door hard, but there were bloody chains in his hands that had clearly been used as weapons.
No one inside the house answered.
When the group passed the window, they saw a Cindari woman sitting behind the door.
Both of her hands were over her mouth, tears were running down her face, on the other side of the door, her son knocked again.
"Open the door!"
The woman only shook her head, as if she did not dare to open the door, as if she knew that her son was no longer what he had been.
No one in the group said anything.
"If this reaches Earth..." Liana said very quietly afterward, she did not even want to finish the sentence.
"We won’t let it." Rindo did not even look at her and gave a short answer.
But everyone knew that talking about something like this was easier than doing it.
Black Silence did not need to kill billions of people itself.
It did not need to destroy cities with its own hands.
It was enough to make one person’s fear a little bigger, make the second person’s hatred deeper, make the third person’s jealousy sick, and then just watch.
The world would kill itself.
This thought made even those who were still unsure about saving or killing Lian feel the weight of their goal more strongly.
If the Calamity reached Earth, it was not only about one person’s fate.
Time passed slowly, almost one day after leaving Vhalaris, the environment began to change.
The trees of Emberroot became fewer, the dark and soft ground under their feet was replaced by brighter and harder ground.
Then the first glass tree appeared.
Selina unconsciously slowed down, as if she was surprised by what she was seeing, the trunk of the tree was half-transparent.
Lines of light moved through its depths and the branches rose into the sky like long crystals.
The leaves also looked like thin, colored glass, when the wind moved through them, instead of the sound of leaves, the sound of very soft bells spread through the air.
The farther they went, the more Emberroot completely disappeared behind them, Glassthorn surrounded them from every side.
The glass trees broke the sunlight and hundreds of colors fell onto the ground.
Some trunks were light blue, some were pink, and some were almost colorless.
"This one is prettier than the previous forest." Selina looked around for a few seconds.
"Until something jumps out from inside a tree." Liana added sarcastically.
"Can you at least make one beautiful place not look scary?" Selina looked at her.
She did not answer, because she was actually telling the truth, this place might be more beautiful but it was also more dangerous.
And then they saw Crystaline.
The city could be clearly seen even from very far away.
Several layers of transparent walls rose among the trees and tall crystal towers spread the sunlight across the entire forest.
Transparent bridges stretched between the towers.
Buildings that looked more like pieces of crystal that had grown from the ground than structures built by living creatures.
"This is even bigger than Vhalaris." Seraphina said in surprise.
"It should be." Tavern answered naturally and then added.
"Almost all the intelligent creatures of Glassthorn live in this city, we Cindari have five large cities, they only have this one, so naturally they spend everything they have on this place."
Rindo stared at the city, the gates of Crystaline could be seen even from that distance, but there was no sign of a large disturbance around them.
At least nothing that could be seen from outside.
"We’ll pass by it."
