It was enough to make one person’s fear a little bigger, make the second person’s hatred deeper, make the third person’s jealousy sick, and then just watch.
The world would kill itself.
This thought made even those who were still unsure about saving or killing Lian feel the weight of their goal more strongly.
If the Calamity reached Earth, it was not only about one person’s fate.
Time passed slowly, almost one day after leaving Vhalaris, the environment began to change.
The trees of Emberroot became fewer, the dark and soft ground under their feet was replaced by brighter and harder ground.
Then the first glass tree appeared.
Selina unconsciously slowed down, as if she was surprised by what she was seeing, the trunk of the tree was half-transparent.
Lines of light moved through its depths and the branches rose into the sky like long crystals.
The leaves also looked like thin, colored glass, when the wind moved through them, instead of the sound of leaves, the sound of very soft bells spread through the air.
The farther they went, the more Emberroot completely disappeared behind them, Glassthorn surrounded them from every side.
The glass trees broke the sunlight and hundreds of colors fell onto the ground.
Some trunks were light blue, some were pink, and some were almost colorless.
"This one is prettier than the previous forest." Selina looked around for a few seconds.
"Until something jumps out from inside a tree." Liana added sarcastically.
"Can you at least make one beautiful place not look scary?" Selina looked at her.
She did not answer, because she was actually telling the truth, this place might be more beautiful but it was also more dangerous.
And then they saw Crystaline.
The city could be clearly seen even from very far away.
Several layers of transparent walls rose among the trees and tall crystal towers spread the sunlight across the entire forest.
Transparent bridges stretched between the towers.
Buildings that looked more like pieces of crystal that had grown from the ground than structures built by living creatures.
"This is even bigger than Vhalaris." Seraphina said in surprise.
"It should be." Tavern answered naturally and then added.
"Almost all the intelligent creatures of Glassthorn live in this city, we Cindari have five large cities, they only have this one, so naturally they spend everything they have on this place."
Rindo stared at the city, the gates of Crystaline could be seen even from that distance, but there was no sign of a large disturbance around them.
At least nothing that could be seen from outside.
"We’ll pass by it."

chapters.title: Chapter 369: A Vorhelm...?
paragraphs: "We’ll pass by it."
No one objected, their main goal was still the Giant Graveyard, and it made no sense for any of them to lose more time just hoping to find a few more Awakened.
So they changed their path slightly and moved away from the southern part of the city, everyone trying to move quietly.
One also slowed down his steps, and they continued on their way, thinking that everything was going smoothly, less than fifteen minutes later—
The light on one of the glass tree trunks changed, it was only a short flash, but Seris saw it.
Her head turned at that exact moment, something moved through the air, a crystal arrow came toward Tavern at terrifying speed.
She rose from One’s back, her foot pressed against the ant’s natural armor, and her body jumped into the air.
Her sword came out of its sheath.
Clang!
The blade hit the arrow, and the crystal broke in midair, dozens of clear pieces fell to the ground like rain.
The entire group stopped at the same moment, their weapons came out...they were under attack!
"Which bastard did that?" Tavern shouted angrily.
No one said anything, they only checked their surroundings, and at first, no one could be seen.
Then one of the reflections on a tree moved.
Then a second.
Then a third.
And suddenly, more than twenty creatures appeared among the glass tree trunks and branches.
Not that they had actually come out from inside the trees.
Their skin, clothes and armor reflected the light around them, and as long as they stayed still, the image of the trees was reflected on their bodies.
They almost disappeared into the environment.
The natives of Glassthorn.
Most of their skin looked human, but very thin, clear lines could be seen under their skin.
Glass-white hair was common among them, their eyes had no clear pupils, and the surface of their eyes looked more like smooth, polished stone than real eyes.
Each of them held a crystal weapon, bows, spears, thin swords, all of their weapons were made of glass.
"It’s them." Tavern said quietly.
One of the natives said something in his own language.
He frowned, it was clear that he understood nothing, after all, he did not know their language.
[What the hell is a Cindari doing here?] But for the Awakened, the System’s translation appeared immediately.
"He’s asking what you are doing here." Rindo slightly turned his head toward Tavern.
"How nice." Tavern said with annoyance.
"They are also... those creatures? Humans?" Another native moved his clear eyes over the Humans, and for a moment there was a sign of fear in his voice, which was strange.
"Apparently, they know us too." Rindo raised an eyebrow this time, and he also noticed that short moment of fear.
Several other natives moved on the branches, their weapons were still raised, and there was no sign that they were calming down.
One of them jumped down from the tree, he was slightly taller than Rindo and had short white hair.
A panel appeared above his head.
[Glass skins]
[Level: 21]
He came forward a few steps and did not lower his crystal spear.
"What are you doing here?"
"We are only passing through, we are not looking for your city, and we are not looking for a fight." Rindo stepped forward, keeping his hands away from his weapon.
"How are we supposed to know that? How do we know you are not Forsaken?" The creature, or rather, Siran, asked with distrust, and then his gaze became a little colder.
"Forsaken?" Rindo frowned.

"Those who lose their minds, see friends as enemies, attack their own families, even kill their own kind...there are many of them among you Humans." He looked at the Awakened again with eyes full of hatred.
The Student Council President’s expression changed immediately, so other Awakened really had reached Glassthorn.
"You attacked us without checking just because you thought we had lost our minds? You are the ones looking for a fight!" Liana raised her voice with mockery.
"All of you Humans are trouble." Siran stayed silent for a few seconds, then a short and rough sound came from his throat.
"How were we supposed to know you were not Forsaken? Killing you was the safer choice, it’s not like you are dead now." His eyes fell on the broken arrow on the ground.
Rindo said nothing, it was clear now, they were not only careful around outsiders, they hated Humans, and they probably had a reason for that hatred.
And according to what he had understood, they had definitely met Humans before, and since they knew about the Awakened becoming corrupted, that meant there had to be Humans inside that city.
The corruption had started less than a day ago, and if these creatures had learned about the condition of the Humans this quickly, it could only mean one thing.
Seris, however, had no interest in checking their past, she raised her sword and said in a cold voice.
"We don’t have time to waste, either get out of our way, or you die here."
The atmosphere changed in an instant, the natives raised their weapons higher, and mana gathered around the bodies of several of them.
Siran also pointed his spear directly at Seris.
Rindo said nothing this time, under normal conditions, he might have tried to stop the fight, but they truly had no time now.
If this group decided to stop them, they would have to go through them, and it did not look like they wanted to move aside, it was clear that they were mainly targeting them because they were Humans.
But before anyone could make the first move, a voice came from among the trees.
"Siran."
Everyone stopped, it was a man’s voice, calm, but that single word was enough to change Siran’s expression and make his body become slightly stiff.
"I am sure I told you not to leave your position." The voice continued.
The reflection of one of the trees behind the natives changed.
"And if you see a new Forsaken, report it first.
Someone stepped out from the light, a young man with dark hair, wearing simple clothes whose surface copied the reflections of the surroundings just like the natives of the forest.
But unlike them, he was completely Human, he was a Human! And the natives reacted immediately when they saw him, their weapons were still not lowered, but almost all of them lowered their heads.
Not out of normal respect, but out of fear!
"S-Sorry, Your Majesty." Siran’s face became a little pale.
Several of the Awakened looked at each other when they heard that title, why was this Glass skin, who seemed to hate Humans, calling one of them Your Majesty?

The young man looked at Siran without immediately paying attention to the other Humans, his gaze became colder every second, as if he would punish those Glass skins badly if he did not receive a good answer.
"We saw these intruders, we thought they might be Forsaken, so we came to check."
The man said nothing and then looked at the group, Rindo stood a little straighter and Liana looked at him with curiosity.

But Seris became completely still, she did not know the face, but she knew the resemblance, the jawline, the dark hair, the eyes, and the way he slightly tilted his head when examining the people in front of him.

For a strange moment, she felt like Lian was standing in front of her, but this man was not Lian, he did not have that constant coldness on his face, instead of coldness, there was cruelty on his face.
Even though the similarity between their faces was extremely strange, he looked strangely similar to Lian.
However, something about his presence bothered Seris, his cruel appearance matched the feeling of danger she got from him.
He was not weak, not at all, in fact, she felt that except for herself and Tavern, there was no one else here who could fight this man.
She unconsciously moved her hand slightly closer to the handle of her sword.
"I did not expect to see Awakened again this soon." The man noticed her movement, but smiled.
"We did not expect it either, I am glad that at least another group is still safe." Rindo also gave a short smile.
"Me too, anyway, you came from another forest, right?" The man laughed.
"We came from Emberroot."
"I guessed."

A few more short sentences were exchanged, and the atmosphere slowly moved away from its explosive state, Siran and his forces were still standing farther back, but they were no longer holding their weapons directly at the group.
"I guess you are traveling, right? Why don’t you rest in Crystaline for a while?"
Rindo wanted to politely refuse the offer, but Seris answered faster.

"No need, we need to reach our destination as soon as possible, we have already wasted too much time here." Her tone was cold, she could somehow smell a strong Vorhelm scent from this boy, and she did not like this smell at all.
Lian was an exception, of course, and in any case, he did not have a smell either.
Her words made the atmosphere become a little tense again, not enough to become a real conflict, but it was clear that her tone was not very friendly, and Rindo sighed.
"Your face looks familiar to me, and that sharp tongue reminds me of the Pendragons." Then the man’s gaze stayed on Seris, he looked at her more carefully for several seconds and finally said.
"You also remind me of the Vorhelms." The young Pendragon answered again in a emotionless tone.
"That’s natural, after all, I am a Vorhelm." The man’s smile became a little wider.
"Vorhelm?" Rindo was the first to react, had they randomly found a Vorhelm?
"What is your relation to Lian?" But Seris asked the main question directly.
"Where do you know my brother from?" This time, the man really paused.

chapters.title: Chapter 370: One More Vorhelm
paragraphs: Two hours later, the group’s decision to quietly pass by Crystaline, which had only taken a few minutes, had turned into a stop at the central palace of the city.

From the moment it became clear that the man in front of them was one of Lian’s brothers, Rindo could no longer see him as just an unknown Human, and besides, that Vorhelm himself no longer let them leave.
They learned that his name was Darian, and that he was one of the seven children of the Vorhelm Patriarch.
On the way into the city, something else had caught their attention.
Wherever Darian passed, the natives moved aside, their heads lowered, their eyes on the ground, and some of them did not even dare to breathe normally until he had passed.
Of course, they also saw some Awakened, but instead of fear, they showed them respect.
"What did you do to them that they are this afraid of you?" Rindo finally could not stop himself from asking.
Of course, this also made him curious about whether Siran’s hatred and the hatred of the other Glass skins could be related to this same fear.
"They attacked us first, so we took their city, and now I am their king." Darian answered very naturally.
For a few seconds, Rindo was not sure whether he was joking or not, but there was no sign of a joke on his face.
"Is this whole family not normal?" Liana muttered.
No one answered, but it was not a bad question, taking control of an entire intelligent race in a foreign world was not a small thing.
And apart from not being a small thing, it was crazy, how had he even managed to do something like this?
The Crystaline Palace was also made of huge crystals, just like the city itself, the walls were semi-transparent, and light flowed inside them.
Even the floor of the main hall changed its color depending on the angle from which it was viewed.
When everyone sat down, Darian finally gave them a short explanation about the situation in the forest.
"When we entered this area, around seventy or eighty Awakened were scattered throughout Glassthorn."
"Did all of them survive?" Rindo listened more seriously, from his conversation with Tavern, he had learned that the Cindari had captured dozens of Humans around their cities.
And if he counted them, then the Awakened inside Vhalaris, and then these seventy or eighty people, the total number of Awakened should add up correctly.
"No, many died before reaching the city, some were killed by the natives, some by monsters, and of course, there are definitely some we never found."

"After I organized them, we decided to find a place that could tell us more about this world, but the people here attacked us, and we took the city, we have been here for a while, and yesterday some of them suddenly started going crazy."

"At first, we thought it was some kind of mental illness, people became angry for no reason, they started suspecting each other, then they started attacking." His eyes moved toward the crystal windows for a moment.
"We called them the Forsaken."
"Only the Awakened? Or did the Glass skins also suffer from it?" Rindo asked.
"The natives were affected too, then the monsters, weaker people went crazy faster, for now, most of the high-level people are still healthy." Darian added.
Rindo’s face became darker, his and Seris’s analysis was being confirmed again, the lower the level, the faster the corruption affected them.
"Now tell me where my brother is." Then, after giving them some time to understand this information, he moved to the main subject.
A short silence appeared, Rindo looked at Seris, and Seris only stared back, showing no sign of whether she wanted him to tell everything or not.
Rindo made the decision himself, he knew nothing about the relationship between Lian and Darian.
He did not know what was happening inside the Vorhelm family, he did not know whether this brother might be Lian’s ally or his rival, so he did not tell him the whole truth.
Then he gave a short summary, but the summary had many parts censored and hid many things.
But at least it gave him information about the Calamity, Lian’s current condition, the Main Quest, the Titan, and the corruption.
Darian’s gaze became deeper, it was not clear what he was thinking, whether he was surprised by the information or not.
"We are currently going to the Giant Graveyard, we think the Calamity’s next target is there." Rindo paused for a moment.
Darian looked away for a moment and opened his own Main Quest panel.
[Main Quest: Prevent the complete awakening of the Corrupted Titan.]
"So this is what this Main Quest was for." He stared at it for a few seconds and then added.
"So you don’t know exactly where Lian is right now?"
"We don’t know, that’s why we are going to the graveyard, maybe we can find him there." Rindo said.
At least this part was not a lie, they really did not know Lian’s exact location, and they really did not know whether they would find him in the graveyard.
"I am coming too." Darian stayed silent for a few seconds and then said very simply.
"No." Seris answered immediately.
Everyone looked at her.
"No?"
"I don’t trust you." Seris looked straight at him.

"I don’t trust you either, Miss Pendragon, but apparently you are one of the last people who saw my brother, and this is about my brother, so we will have to tolerate each other for a while." Darian stared at her for a moment and then a very small smile returned to his face.
Seris did not like his answer, but she said nothing, though she really preferred that another Vorhelm did not come with them, Lian was an exception, but the other Vorhelms could not be trusted.
"It will take me half an hour to get ready, rest for a while during that time." Darian stood up and then left the hall.
As soon as the door closed, a short silence appeared.
Seris kept her gaze on the door, the Vorhelm family had seven known children for the Patriarch.
Two of them officially had five-star classes, Diana Vorhelm, and the eldest son of the family.
Diana had only recently awakened, and a large ceremony had even been held for her awakening.
The eldest son had also been known for a long time as one of the family’s main talents, but he was not ambitious and had shown no interest in becoming the successor or competing for the inheritance.
But there were also two other children among these seven whose story was different, they had been sent outside the country for years.
Each of them was in a different country for training and gaining experience, or on missions that no one knew much about.
Their identities were not secret, but almost all important information about them was.
Class.
Talent.
Level.
Ability.
Activities.
All of them were either hidden or intentionally not made public.
These were all the pieces of information Aurelia Pendragon had once told Seris.
(To avoid confusion, there are two Aurelias, one who is Seris’s family member, and the other is a native of this world.)
The Pendragons had always guessed that the two of them were probably four-star, the reason was simple.
Having four five-stars in one generation was almost ridiculous.
The Vorhelms already had two known five-stars.
Then there was Lian, an anomaly that no one still fully understood, and every day he became more confusing and unknown.
If those two hidden children were also five-stars, then it would no longer be called luck, it would prove that the Vorhelms were a family favored by the gods.
No matter how lucky, powerful, or great a family is, there has never been a case where four Awakened with five-star classes appeared in the same generation.
It had never happened in history, and even now, the Vorhelms were already extremely lucky to have two geniuses with five-star classes, along with Lian.
Even the Pendragons and the other major powers of the world never thought that the reason all the information about those two children was hidden was because of their classes.
Instead, they probably thought it was some kind of mission, at least according to their guess.
’Then he must be one of those two.’ Seris came to this conclusion after thinking about Adrian.

Rindo made the decision himself, he knew nothing about the relationship between Lian and Darian.
He did not know what was happening inside the Vorhelm family, he did not know whether this brother might be Lian’s ally or his rival, so he did not tell him the whole truth.
Then he gave a short summary, but the summary had many parts censored and hid many things.
But at least it gave him information about the Calamity, Lian’s current condition, the Main Quest, the Titan, and the corruption.
Darian’s gaze became deeper, it was not clear what he was thinking, whether he was surprised by the information or not.
"We are currently going to the Giant Graveyard, we think the Calamity’s next target is there." Rindo paused for a moment.
Darian looked away for a moment and opened his own Main Quest panel.
[Main Quest: Prevent the complete awakening of the Corrupted Titan.]
"So this is what this Main Quest was for." He stared at it for a few seconds and then added.
"So you don’t know exactly where Lian is right now?"
"We don’t know, that’s why we are going to the graveyard, maybe we can find him there." Rindo said.
At least this part was not a lie, they really did not know Lian’s exact location, and they really did not know whether they would find him in the graveyard.
"I am coming too." Darian stayed silent for a few seconds and then said very simply.
"No." Seris answered immediately.
Everyone looked at her.
"No?"
"I don’t trust you." Seris looked straight at him.

"I don’t trust you either, Miss Pendragon, but apparently you are one of the last people who saw my brother, and this is about my brother, so we will have to tolerate each other for a while." Darian stared at her for a moment and then a very small smile returned to his face.
Seris did not like his answer, but she said nothing, though she really preferred that another Vorhelm did not come with them, Lian was an exception, but the other Vorhelms could not be trusted.
"It will take me half an hour to get ready, rest for a while during that time." Darian stood up and then left the hall.
As soon as the door closed, a short silence appeared.
Seris kept her gaze on the door, the Vorhelm family had seven known children for the Patriarch.
Two of them officially had five-star classes, Diana Vorhelm, and the eldest son of the family.
Diana had only recently awakened, and a large ceremony had even been held for her awakening.
The eldest son had also been known for a long time as one of the family’s main talents, but he was not ambitious and had shown no interest in becoming the successor or competing for the inheritance.
But there were also two other children among these seven whose story was different, they had been sent outside the country for years.
Each of them was in a different country for training and gaining experience, or on missions that no one knew much about.
Their identities were not secret, but almost all important information about them was.
Class.
Talent.
Level.
Ability.
Activities.
All of them were either hidden or intentionally not made public.
These were all the pieces of information Aurelia Pendragon had once told Seris.
(To avoid confusion, there are two Aurelias, one who is Seris’s family member, and the other is a native of this world.)
The Pendragons had always guessed that the two of them were probably four-star, the reason was simple.
Having four five-stars in one generation was almost ridiculous.
The Vorhelms already had two known five-stars.
Then there was Lian, an anomaly that no one still fully understood, and every day he became more confusing and unknown.
If those two hidden children were also five-stars, then it would no longer be called luck, it would prove that the Vorhelms were a family favored by the gods.
No matter how lucky, powerful, or great a family is, there has never been a case where four Awakened with five-star classes appeared in the same generation.
It had never happened in history, and even now, the Vorhelms were already extremely lucky to have two geniuses with five-star classes, along with Lian.
Even the Pendragons and the other major powers of the world never thought that the reason all the information about those two children was hidden was because of their classes.
Instead, they probably thought it was some kind of mission, at least according to their guess.
’Then he must be one of those two.’ Seris came to this conclusion after thinking about Adrian.

chapters.title: Chapter 371: The First Seal Breaks
paragraphs: "Your thoughts?" Rindo thought for a few seconds and then said.
"I don’t trust him." Seris answered without hesitation.
"Just because he is a Vorhelm?" Liana said, from her point of view, that did not seem like a good enough reason, Lian was also a Vorhelm and so far, he had been like the savior of all of them.
So on the contrary, she had a very good opinion of the Vorhelms.

"Part of the reason, and don’t think that just because Lian is good, the other Vorhelms are good too, they are selfish, cruel, greedy bastards and they only do things for themselves, and they are stubborn."
"But you are exactly like that too, so what is the difference?"
For a moment, the group’s eyes moved between the two, and Seris’s eyes became cold, she opened her mouth to answer, but no answer came out.
In the end, she only grunted and said they could do whatever they wanted.
"I don’t trust him either." Rindo said.
"Then we don’t take him with us." Cassian frowned, he did not know why his senior had such a feeling, but she had never been wrong before, so he preferred to trust her.
But he also did not have a good feeling about him, none of them did, they felt that—
"The problem is that I don’t think we can stop him." Rindo looked at her and continued, "From the moment I saw him, I had a bad feeling."
"Not that kind of bad feeling, the kind that tells you that if the other side decides to fight, they will be trouble."
"Then let him come, we already don’t have enough people to hold back those five walking corpses." Aren, who was sitting near the wall, said very simply.
Seris did not like this logic, but she could not reject it, one more person, especially a Vorhelm who clearly seemed powerful, was a great help.
But was it really right to trust someone they had only met a few hours ago?
The door opened, and Darian entered, but this time he was not wearing simple clothes, heavy dark armor covered his body.
Transparent crystal lines ran across its surface and changed the way the light reflected as he moved.
But what attracted the most attention was the bow on his back.
The bow was huge.
Its curved body was made of crystals of different colors, and whenever light passed through it, colored lines appeared on the walls and floor.
Seris understood at once, this was not an ordinary weapon.
[Seven-Colored Sky Bow]
[Rank: S]
An S-Rank weapon, and it was clear that he had obtained it from this forest, and probably from this city, either through a trade or by force...
"I’m ready." Darian smiled, he was not alone either, four other people were standing behind him.
Rindo looked at the four people behind him, all of them were Awakened, four Humans with a powerful presence, and clearly stronger than the Humans they had seen in the city.
"These are coming with us."
"Only four people? If you can bring more support, wouldn’t it be better to bring more?" Liana added.
"The city still needs the others, and four people are enough."
Less than an hour later, the group was on the road again.
Crystal-line slowly became smaller behind them, this time four new Awakened and Darian were also traveling with them.
During the first part of the journey, Rindo and Liana were almost openly trying to get more information about their new guest.
"So which one of Lian’s brothers are you exactly?" Liana finally asked.
"That’s a strange question, but the simplest answer is that I’m his best brother." Darian looked at her for a few seconds.
Liana was genuinely surprised for a moment, Seraphina and Selina also looked at him from the side.
"She asked because all the other children of the Vorhelm family are known, but we have never heard about you." Seraphina finally added.
She had lived in Medes for years, she had sometimes seen Lian’s other brothers and sisters, but not Darian.
"Because I had been outside the country for a long time."
"Oh? How many years have you been outside your country?" The Student Council President asked with curiosity.
"A few years."
Rindo waited for more, but nothing else came.
"Where were you?"
"Outside." Darian smiled.
Rindo stared at him for a few seconds, then stopped asking questions, this man was annoyingly good at giving no information without actually telling a lie.
"Are you close with Lian?" Liana, however, did not give up.
"It’s complicated." This time Darian did not answer immediately, and his smile became slightly smaller.
Not good.
Not bad.
Just that.
"Does he still always have that look like he can deal with any problem?" He asked himself a moment later.
"Yeah." Liana could not stop herself from laughing.
"Then he hasn’t changed much." Darian’s facial expression did not change much.
Seris was hearing this conversation from a little farther away, she did not interfere, but she kept Darian’s short answer in her mind.
Complicated, that meant there was something between the two, it was just not clear what.
Meanwhile, One turned his head toward Darian several times, his antennae moving slowly.
"I didn’t expect you to use an ant as a mount." Darian finally noticed.
"He belongs to Lian."
"Oh? What’s his name?"
"His name is One." Seris answered coldly.
Darian looked more closely at the giant ant, as if he was trying to examine him, and then laughed.
Seris gave him a strange look and then ignored him, she had no interest in wasting her time.
At the same time, very far away, there was no color in the sky.
The Giant Graveyard was covered in heavy darkness.
The Titan’s body stretched like a buried mountain range between the soil and rocks.
Seven huge chains were still holding its body to the ground.
But one of them was no longer still and was shaking, the Runes on its surface were going out one after another.
Lian was standing in front of it, his expression did not change at all, only the purple light inside his eyes was shining in the darkness.
Four walking corpses stood motionless around him, and Cindar was standing a few meters behind them.
He was not saying anything either, he was only watching.
The hand of Black Silence was placed on the first ring of the chain.
Crack.
The previous crack spread, another Rune went out, and then another.
The ancient chain made a sound like a groan after hundreds of years.
One of the rings broke, then the next ring, and it continued like that...
Cindar smiled and then—
BOOM!
The first chain collapsed, the ground of the Giant Graveyard shook for kilometers, and a mass of darkness came out from under the Titan’s huge skin.
Something thick and ancient, a wave of darkness rose into the air and covered the sky above the Titan for a moment.
Then its path changed, directly toward Lian, directly toward his body, and the darkness entered him.
His body reacted, he took one step back, his fingers shook for a moment, his head dropped, and a short silence followed.
Then he raised his head again, the purple light in his eyes had become stronger.
Cindar kept his smile.
One chain, only one, after centuries of planning and waiting, the thing he had lived for was finally happening.
"Congratulations." He opened his mouth and said.

He expected that now that one of the chains had been opened, part of his power would also return, after all, after the final battle and the sealing of the Calamity, his power had also slowly decreased.
All the power he had was thanks to Black Silence, and after it was sealed, all the power he had gained through it disappeared over the years.
And only the power he had before becoming an Anchor remained for him.
But a few seconds later, his smile became slightly smaller, his power had not changed at all, he felt nothing through the Anchor connection, not even a little.
Black Silence had always shared their powers through that connection... but now, there was nothing like that, in fact, it could have done this ever since it was released.
But it did not.
Cindar first thought that maybe the Calamity was waiting to take back its power from the Titan and then share its power with him like before.
But it still did not do that... and worse than that, it did not even answer him, Black Silence did not look at him even once.
No recognition, no gratitude, not even attention, as if Cindar, the man who had sold his world for this creature, did not even exist.
And at that moment, a notification appeared for all the Awakened.
[Another part of Black Silence has merged with the new host.]

chapters.title: Chapter 372: The Tools Left Behind
paragraphs: The farther the group went toward the Giant’s Graveyard, the less the forest looked like a forest.
The huge trees of Glassthorn had disappeared behind them hours ago, and even the vegetation of the Giant’s Forest had slowly become less common.

At first, there was simply more distance between the trees, then the bushes disappeared, and finally there was nothing left except dry ground, huge rocks, and the remains of creatures that had died long ago.
Bones were everywhere.

Some were so large that the group had to change their path to pass around them. The ribcage of one dead creature stuck out of the ground like the ruins of a multi-story building, and its white bones disappeared into the gray sky.
A little farther away, a skull as large as a house was stuck between two rocks.
"So the reason they call it the Giant’s Graveyard is pretty clear." Liana said in a low voice and looked around at the huge remains.
No one answered, and everyone except Seris was wondering just how huge the creatures of the Giant’s Forest could be.
Tavern had also become quiet, and his attitude had changed since they entered this part of the world.
The Cindari man spoke less and looked around more. Sometimes he checked old paths on the ground, and sometimes he looked at the remains of pillars that might have once marked borders.
Seris was sitting on One’s back, she had been looking straight ahead the whole time, and the closer they got, the stronger that heavy feeling in her chest became.
There was something there, not just something, something whose presence could be felt in the air even before they saw it.
The mana had become heavier, the air smelled of burnt soil and metal, and every few minutes, a very weak vibration passed through the ground.
No one said anything, they had all felt it and seemed to be preparing themselves mentally for whatever they were about to face.
"These vibrations aren’t normal." Cassian said with a deep frown and looked down at the ground.
"No, we’re close now." Rindo answered calmly and placed his hand on his weapon.
A few minutes later, they went around the last huge rock and everyone stopped.
Even Seris.
Even Tavern.
Even Darian, whose calm and confident expression had almost never changed during the entire journey.
What stood before them was more than the mind could understand the size of at first glance.
A Titan.
They had heard its name many times.
Seris had seen parts of its body from different distances.
Aren had told stories about a creature chained deep inside this area.
But none of those things could show them the true size of the creature standing before them.
The Titan’s body was buried between the earth and the sky.
One of its arms alone was like a huge mountain range lying across the ground, and each of its fingers looked larger than towers.
A large part of its chest was buried under layers of soil and rock.
Its huge head was very far away, and the upper half of it disappeared into the black fog that had gathered around the graveyard.
"Is that... a living creature?" Selina said in disbelief and almost unconsciously took one step back.
No one answered, because at that moment, one of the Titan’s fingers moved.
Only a few centimeters, but the ground under everyone’s feet shook and several rocks fell from one of the broken pillars.
One spread its legs wider to keep its balance, Darian also did not take his eyes off the Titan.
An announcement appeared in front of everyone.
[Warning.]
[The awakening of the Corrupted Titan is progressing.]
[Awakening Level: 42%]
Rindo stared at the number, only a few seconds passed before the number changed.
[Awakening Level: 43%]
Rindo’s face immediately became darker, this was no longer an uncertain problem about time, the damn percentage was rising very quickly.
Seris also frowned, the last time they had been here, this percentage had barely reached five, but now it was 43.
"We’re too late." Rindo said in a low voice and moved his eyes from the panel back to the Titan.
Seris then noticed something else, four chains, only four huge chains were still holding the Titan’s body to the ground.
Their rings were so large that a human could stand inside one of them and still have a lot of space on both sides.
But three other chains had broken.
Pieces of their rings were scattered across the graveyard, some of the pieces were as large as a small house.
Some still had a very weak light, but the seals on them had gone out.
"She broke three chains." The Young Pendragon said coldly and got down from One.
No one said anything, but they felt the urgency of the situation, it was clear that Black Silence had been breaking the chains during this time, and it had been quite successful.
Then Rindo followed the path of the remaining chains with his eyes.
And finally, he saw him.
A human figure looked almost like a small black dot against that huge body, standing beside the fourth chain.
Lian.
His body had no clear difference from the last time they had seen him.
The same clothes, the same hair, the same face, but even from this distance, the purple light inside his eyes could be seen.
His hand was resting on one of the chain’s rings, five other figures stood behind him, five Undead, one of them was Sindar.
Darian became completely still when he saw Lian, until that moment, the small and almost constant smile on his face had remained throughout the journey.
Now it disappeared, completely, and his hand slowly moved toward his back, his fingers closed around the body of the Seven-Colored Sky Bow, a cold light passed through his eyes, but he said nothing.
Seris looked at him for a moment, there was no clear emotional reaction, neither anger nor worry and no attempt to go toward her brother.
Only that sudden coldness, and that could be more worrying than a strong reaction.
But before she could think about it more, the voice of a Cindari caught her attention.
"...Founder?" Tavern said with a voice that slightly shook.
The Cindari soldiers with him also froze, one of them even fell to his knees without realizing it.
"Cindar Vael..." The soldier whispered the name like an old prayer and lowered his head.
Tavern did not kneel, he only stared, his whole childhood had passed with that name.
Cindar Vael, the Founder, the last survivor of the Final Battle, the one who brought back the First Root, the one whose name had shaped their race.
The hero who, without him, according to all the stories they had heard, the Cindari would not even exist.
Every city had his statues, every great family connected their history to him, his name existed in oaths, prayers, and old texts.
And now that same man was standing before them, not fighting the Calamity and not even dead, the Founder who should have been dead was alive.
And worse than anything, he was standing beside the Calamity that had caused the destruction of their world.
Tavern could not put these two images together.

"Maybe... maybe he’s being controlled." He said in a very low voice and tightened his jaw, he could not accept that the man who had been like a role model and hero to him his entire life was serving the Calamity.
No one answered, everyone knew that it was not easy for the Cindari to accept the truth.
Cindar turned his head toward them at that moment, the distance was great, but their eyes met for a moment.
Tavern held his breath, there was no recognition and no affection in those eyes, no surprise at seeing Cindari who were alive hundreds of years after he should have died.
There was not even pride in what he himself had created, nothing.
The look Cindar gave them was not even as warm as the look of a ruler toward his subjects, they were simply things he no longer needed.
It was very clear from that look that to him, the Cindari were nothing more than tools whose use was already finished.
And Tavern suddenly understood something, or at least his mind finally dared to accept the possibility for the first time.
Maybe they had never been the "Children of the Founder."
Maybe the Cindari race had never been a legacy for the future of the world.
Maybe they were only tools, a generation that had been created to protect something, to continue a project whose real owner could not stay awake for centuries for it.
And now the project had succeeded.
Black Silence was free, so the tools no longer mattered.
Tavern’s stomach tightened for a moment, his feeling was not even anger, nor hatred, but something closer to nausea.

"Is that... a living creature?" Selina said in disbelief and almost unconsciously took one step back.
No one answered, because at that moment, one of the Titan’s fingers moved.
Only a few centimeters, but the ground under everyone’s feet shook and several rocks fell from one of the broken pillars.
One spread its legs wider to keep its balance, Darian also did not take his eyes off the Titan.
An announcement appeared in front of everyone.
[Warning.]
[The awakening of the Corrupted Titan is progressing.]
[Awakening Level: 42%]
Rindo stared at the number, only a few seconds passed before the number changed.
[Awakening Level: 43%]
Rindo’s face immediately became darker, this was no longer an uncertain problem about time, the damn percentage was rising very quickly.
Seris also frowned, the last time they had been here, this percentage had barely reached five, but now it was 43.
"We’re too late." Rindo said in a low voice and moved his eyes from the panel back to the Titan.
Seris then noticed something else, four chains, only four huge chains were still holding the Titan’s body to the ground.
Their rings were so large that a human could stand inside one of them and still have a lot of space on both sides.
But three other chains had broken.
Pieces of their rings were scattered across the graveyard, some of the pieces were as large as a small house.
Some still had a very weak light, but the seals on them had gone out.
"She broke three chains." The Young Pendragon said coldly and got down from One.
No one said anything, but they felt the urgency of the situation, it was clear that Black Silence had been breaking the chains during this time, and it had been quite successful.
Then Rindo followed the path of the remaining chains with his eyes.
And finally, he saw him.
A human figure looked almost like a small black dot against that huge body, standing beside the fourth chain.
Lian.
His body had no clear difference from the last time they had seen him.
The same clothes, the same hair, the same face, but even from this distance, the purple light inside his eyes could be seen.
His hand was resting on one of the chain’s rings, five other figures stood behind him, five Undead, one of them was Sindar.
Darian became completely still when he saw Lian, until that moment, the small and almost constant smile on his face had remained throughout the journey.
Now it disappeared, completely, and his hand slowly moved toward his back, his fingers closed around the body of the Seven-Colored Sky Bow, a cold light passed through his eyes, but he said nothing.
Seris looked at him for a moment, there was no clear emotional reaction, neither anger nor worry and no attempt to go toward her brother.
Only that sudden coldness, and that could be more worrying than a strong reaction.
But before she could think about it more, the voice of a Cindari caught her attention.
"...Founder?" Tavern said with a voice that slightly shook.
The Cindari soldiers with him also froze, one of them even fell to his knees without realizing it.
"Cindar Vael..." The soldier whispered the name like an old prayer and lowered his head.
Tavern did not kneel, he only stared, his whole childhood had passed with that name.
Cindar Vael, the Founder, the last survivor of the Final Battle, the one who brought back the First Root, the one whose name had shaped their race.
The hero who, without him, according to all the stories they had heard, the Cindari would not even exist.
Every city had his statues, every great family connected their history to him, his name existed in oaths, prayers, and old texts.
And now that same man was standing before them, not fighting the Calamity and not even dead, the Founder who should have been dead was alive.
And worse than anything, he was standing beside the Calamity that had caused the destruction of their world.
Tavern could not put these two images together.

"Maybe... maybe he’s being controlled." He said in a very low voice and tightened his jaw, he could not accept that the man who had been like a role model and hero to him his entire life was serving the Calamity.
No one answered, everyone knew that it was not easy for the Cindari to accept the truth.
Cindar turned his head toward them at that moment, the distance was great, but their eyes met for a moment.
Tavern held his breath, there was no recognition and no affection in those eyes, no surprise at seeing Cindari who were alive hundreds of years after he should have died.
There was not even pride in what he himself had created, nothing.
The look Cindar gave them was not even as warm as the look of a ruler toward his subjects, they were simply things he no longer needed.
It was very clear from that look that to him, the Cindari were nothing more than tools whose use was already finished.
And Tavern suddenly understood something, or at least his mind finally dared to accept the possibility for the first time.
Maybe they had never been the "Children of the Founder."
Maybe the Cindari race had never been a legacy for the future of the world.
Maybe they were only tools, a generation that had been created to protect something, to continue a project whose real owner could not stay awake for centuries for it.
And now the project had succeeded.
Black Silence was free, so the tools no longer mattered.
Tavern’s stomach tightened for a moment, his feeling was not even anger, nor hatred, but something closer to nausea.

chapters.title: Chapter 373: The Battle Of Giants’ Graveyard I
paragraphs: Rindo gave him a brief look, but now was not the time for centuries-old beliefs to fall apart.
"Everyone, get closer." he said firmly and gathered the group with a hand gesture.
Everyone moved a few steps toward him, Seris stood beside One, Darian had taken his bow from his back.
Seraphina stood beside Liana, Cassian, Selina, and Aren also got ready.
"The plan is the same." He pointed at the five figures behind Lian with his hand.
"We separate these five from Lian, and we keep them busy for as long as necessary." Rindo said in a short and serious tone, then his eyes stopped on Seris.
"You go directly for the Calamity." Rindo continued.
Seris nodded with a cold calmness, and then everyone’s eyes almost naturally turned toward Darian.
He was the only one who had a very direct personal reason to disagree, the Calamity was inside his own brother’s body, but Darian only touched the string of his bow with one finger.
"I heard the plan." The Vorhelm said without even taking his eyes off Lian.
"You don’t have a problem with it?" Rindo asked with some doubt, after all, this was about his brother, maybe he wanted to go save his brother himself...?
"If I wanted to disagree, I would have done it by now." Darian seemed to really not care, and simply answered, then looked toward his brother again.
Seris frowned very slightly, this answer should have made them feel relieved, but it did not, it was too easy and too fast.

The man who had been asking about Lian a few hours ago and had clearly joined them to find him, had now accepted Seris going directly toward his brother’s body without even asking a single question about what exactly "fighting the Calamity" meant.
A bad feeling appeared in her mind again, the same feeling she had from the first time she met Darian.
But she looked away from him, there was a more important matter now, later, if there was a later.
"I think it is time, you said you have a way to suppress or weaken them." Liana said seriously and looked at Seraphina.
"I do." Seraphina answered and moved away from the group.
She walked a few steps forward, her eyes fixed on the four remaining chains, for several seconds she only stared at them, at what remained inside them.
The will and pieces of the souls of those who had given their lives to create that seal.
She raised her right hand, the mana around her body changed, a very old feeling appeared in the air.
Even Sindar turned his head toward her, for some strange reason, looking at her gave him a familiar feeling that he really did not like.
[Final Command]
Seraphina closed her eyes, at first nothing happened, then suddenly a thin line of light came out from her palm.
It went directly toward one of the four chains.
The second line.
The third.
The fourth.
Four lines of light connected Seraphina’s body to the four remaining chains, for a moment everything stayed still.
Then the ground shook.
GRRRRRRRR!
The first chain moved, the rings that had been lying on the ground for years slowly rose from the dirt.
Each ring rose like a huge tower, then the second chain, the third, and finally the fourth.
The rocks around them broke apart, the ground cracked and pieces of stone were thrown several meters into the air.
For the first time after hundreds of years, the four remaining chains moved not only as seals but also as weapons.
The five undead immediately reacted.
The swordsman raised his head, the root controller took a step back, and the mage frowned, and the last one lowered his body.
Even Sindar took a step back, now he understood why that annoying familiar feeling he was getting from that girl was there.
This girl is Aurelia’s heir!
And she was using that woman’s special skill! That damn skill that he knew very well!
[The remaining will of the seven awakened heroes has awakened.]
[Temporary Seal Command activated.]
[Five targets have been affected.]
A few seconds later, a more important message appeared.
[Power Suppression: 30%, Flight Suppression, Spirit Power Suppression: 30%]
[Remaining Time: 10:00]
"Thirty percent? This is great!" Rindo said in disbelief and gave a short smile.
What Seraphina had done caused thirty percent of the power of the five Cindari to be suppressed for ten minutes! Thirty percent was a very large amount.
With this amount, they could fight them much better and maybe they could do much more than just buy time.
But another question also came to his mind ... how did this girl do this?
After all, he did not know that she had obtained a legacy.
Sweat had already appeared on Seraphina’s forehead, four lines of light were passing through her hands and body, and every time the chains moved, the muscles in her arms trembled.
"This is the best I can do, as long as I stay here, around thirty percent of their power will be suppressed." She said between heavy breaths and pressed her teeth together.
Rindo looked at the five enemies, until a few minutes ago, even with their numerical advantage, their chance of success had been very low.
The levels of the five creatures were between thirty-four and thirty-eight, this was a great help to them and really deserved thanks.
"Everyone ready, nobody tries to kill them." He shouted and spread his eyes across the group.
"The goal is only to hold them, ten minutes, every second we buy belongs to Seris."
The panel flashed again.
[Remaining Time: 09:53]
Seris looked at the number, then at Lian, he was still standing beside the fourth chain, he had shown no reaction to the movement of the chains.
He did not even look at the group, as if the battle that was about to begin had no importance to him.
His hand was still on the chain and he was trying to break the fourth chain as well.
"One." The Young Pendragon drew her sword and said shortly.
The giant ant raised its antennae, its body lowered, ready to run.
But before anyone could move, the first chain under Seraphina’s command moved through the air like a huge whip.
The wind caused by its movement pushed the dust away for hundreds of meters and the huge ring came down directly between the five undead.
BOOOOOOM!
The ground exploded.
The rocks broke apart.
The five figures were forced to move away from each other.
"Now!" Rindo shouted and the group moved.
There was no time to waste, the battle that could decide the future of two worlds had finally begun.
The swordsman was the first to come out of the dust, he was neither in a hurry nor angry, he simply pulled his sword out of its sheath in one movement.
Tavern, Cassian, and two Cindari soldiers stood directly in front of him.
The swordsman took a step and Tavern attacked at the same time, the two blades collided.
Clang!
Tavern immediately understood that he had made a mistake, his hand became numb from the impact and the swordsman had not even taken a step back.
The second attack came and he barely defended against it.
The third attack—
The blade passed less than an inch from his neck.
If one of the Cindari had not forced the swordsman to change direction with an attack from the side at that exact moment, Tavern’s head would have fallen to the ground.
He jumped back and his breathing became faster.
There were no flashy skills, only swordsmanship, perfect, clean, and without a single extra movement.
After those three attacks, he understood that if the thirty percent suppression had not existed, the first clash would probably have been the last clash of his life.
The difference in power was too great even for him with his level, so only God knew how it was going to be for the Humans.

Of course, a large part of the difference in power also came from the difference in experience, apart from level, their opponents were creatures who were older than them, had lived longer, and had much more experience.
"So the legends were not lying about everything, at least." Tavern said through clenched teeth and raised his guard again
The swordsman did not answer and only attacked.

chapters.title: Chapter 374: The Battle Of Giants’ Graveyard II
paragraphs: On the other side of the battlefield, the ground cracked, dozens of huge roots shot out from under the dirt toward a group of Humans.
Liana threw herself backward, but Aren did not move, the man simply slammed his right foot into the ground and mana from the bottom of his foot went directly into the dirt.
The ground under the roots moved like a wave and their path changed.
Three roots that should have passed through the Humans suddenly turned to the right and went into a large rock.
The undead who controlled the roots turned his head toward Aren.
"You faced the wrong opponent." Aren said with a smile, for a Cindari who could control roots, the worst enemy was an Earth Element mage.
Then he pressed his other foot into the ground as well, the dirt in front of him rose and a huge wall formed between the group and the next roots.
Liana passed beside him.
"Good, then I will handle the close-range fight." Liana said with a short smile and summoned her Shadow Wolf to help her attack.
Aren said nothing, because the next wave of roots had already arrived.
An explosion of ash spread across another part of the battlefield, Selina raised both hands in front of her and a huge ring of water formed around her body.
The wave of water moved toward the Cindari mage who could use fire and ash, for a moment it seemed that Selina had the full advantage.
Water against fire and ash, but when the two elements collided, what she expected did not happen.
The ash dissolved into the water, the water turned black and then all the liquid suddenly started boiling and burning steam spread through the air.
Selina immediately lowered her hand and slammed the flow of water into the ground.
"Damn, it was not supposed to work like this." Selina said with a frown and took several steps back.
The mage raised his hand, a large part of the ground in front of him melted and then suddenly became cold when it touched Selina’s water, and a layer of black glass formed between them.
The girl kept her eyes on it and then gave a very small smile.
"Okay, then we will find another way." Selina said in a more serious tone.
The water around her turned into hundreds of thin blades.
Of course, she was not alone, several other awakened who had come from Vhalaris to help were also helping her fight the mage.
Their battle had only just begun.
On another side, the undead with the largest body attacked directly toward the center of the group’s formation.
Rindo and Cassian almost moved in front of him at the same time, the guardian’s first attack hit the shield of one of the heavy awakened who had the role of a tank.
The metal bent and the man was thrown several meters backward with his shield.
The student council president entered from the right and his sword hit the guardian’s side.
A wound appeared but the creature did not even look at him.
Cassian attacked from behind and still nothing stopped it, the Cindari’s body was being damaged but it seemed as if pain did not exist for him.

His only goal was to break the formation and for this, he seemed ready to sacrifice anything necessary, this was the formation that had formed between the five Cindari and the body of the infected Titan, where Lian was also standing.
Of course, there was still one Cindari on the other side, the same Cindari that Aren was fighting, the root controller, and they were waiting for a chance to pull him out from that side as well.
And in any case, the awakened had no plan to let them pass through again.
Rindo clenched his teeth.
"Hold the line! It does not need to fall! Just don’t let it pass!" Then he shouted and threw himself in front of the creature again.
And in the center of everything, Sindar moved.
Darian had kept his eyes on him from the very beginning, he raised the Seven-Colored Sky Bow, his left hand held the body of the bow and his right hand moved backward.
But there was no physical arrow in his hand.
He pulled the string, light gathered around the bow.
Red.
Orange.
Yellow.
Green.
Blue.
Indigo.
Purple.
The seven colors gathered at one point and Sindar turned his eyes toward him.
Darian released the string, a thin arrow of light was fired, for a moment even the sound seemed to fall behind.
Then—
BOOOOOOM!
Sindar raised both hands, the arrow of light hit in front of him, the force of the explosion pushed the dirt around him away for dozens of meters.
His body even moved several meters backward ...not much but it moved backward!
For a moment, almost everyone who had a chance to look turned their heads toward Darian.
Rindo even gave a short smile in the middle of the battle.
"I knew it."and then said under his breath, now he understood why he had felt danger from this boy, so the truth was that he was hiding great power.
Darian did not care, he raised his bow again and the light started gathering once more.
But this time Sindar did not wait, in one moment he disappeared from his position.
The Vorhelm could only place his bow horizontally in front of his body to at least block the incoming attack.
Cindar’s fist hit it, the sound of the impact spread across the battlefield like an explosion.
Darian was pushed dozens of meters across the ground, his feet created two long lines in the dirt, but he did not fall and a small cold smile appeared on his face.

"Well, I did not expect dealing with you to be easy either." Then he said with a sharp look and raised his bow again, while also looking at the four awakened he had brought with him and signaling them to attack.
Cindar clearly did not care and prepared for his next attack, although Tavern left his own fight at that moment to strike Sindar from the side.
But before he could reach him, one of the young Cindari soldiers moved ahead of him, it was the same soldier who had fallen to his knees when he saw Sindar.
The man’s eyes still showed confusion, maybe part of him still could not see the Founder as an enemy.
Even so, he raised his weapon.
"Founder! Why?!" The soldier shouted with a trembling voice.
Cindar looked at him, only for a moment, then his hand moved and the soldier’s body stopped in the air.
His chest suddenly sank, blood came out of his mouth and his body fell to the ground like a broken puppet.
Tavern froze, something inside him exploded.
"He was one of your people!" He shouted with pure anger and attacked directly toward Sindar.
Cindar did not even look at him, that was worse.
Tavern brought his sword down with all his strength and the Founder caught it with one hand, the metal stopped between his dried fingers.
The Cindari commander looked into his eyes for a moment.
Nothing.
No regret.
No anger.
Not even boredom.
And right there, he understood, no, that soldier was not one of Cindar’s people, none of them were, they never were.
He had created them, but not like a father who creates a child, but like a craftsman who makes a tool.
He hated his own Founder without any doubt anymore.
[Remaining Time: 07:42]
Seraphina bent her knees slightly, a line of blood ran down from her nose.
The four lines of light were still active, the chains were still moving, but holding them became harder every second.
"Are you okay?!" Liana shouted from the middle of the battle.
"I am fine! Just fight." Seraphina answered with a rough voice and then moved her hand.

At the same time, one of the chains moved again, this time it passed above the battlefield and the root controller was forced to raise several roots to avoid a direct hit, but he was still pushed hundreds of meters away from his position.
Finally, the path was open! All five Cindari had officially moved away from the place where the infected Titan was sleeping.
"Seris!" Rindo shouted.
Seris had been waiting for this moment from the beginning and then ordered One to move at full speed.
One moved with all his strength, the dirt under his feet cracked and his body crossed the battlefield like a huge bullet.
The root controller immediately reacted, a spear made of roots came out of the ground, directly toward One.
But Aren slammed his foot into the ground, the dirt rose and the root changed direction at the last moment, passing only a few centimeters away from One’s side.
"Keep going!" Aren shouted.
Another arrow came toward Seris from a distance, this one was an arrow created by the Cindari mage.
The Young Pendragon frowned, she was ready to dodge, but at that moment colored light passed beside her face.
The attacking arrow split apart in the air.
Darian lowered his bow and then focused his attention on Sindar again.
One increased his speed, the Cindari swordsman noticed them passing, in one moment he disappeared from in front of Tavern.
Seris only saw the flash of the blade.
But Tavern also threw himself between them with all his speed, the swords collided and he almost fell onto one knee.
Blood flowed from his palm but he blocked the path.
"Go!" Tavern shouted angrily.
One passed beside them, another chain passed above their heads and dust covered everything.
When One finally passed out of the battle line, only one person remained in front of them.
Lian.
Beside the fourth chain.
His head slowly turned toward them, the purple light in his eyes shone through the mist and darkness of the graveyard.
One slowed down, the Young Pendragon jumped down from his back and her sword came out of its sheath.
For several seconds she only looked at him, the same face, the same body, but whatever was inside those eyes no longer had any similarity to the man she knew.
She raised her sword.
"It is time for you to pay for that slap you gave me." Seris said in a cold voice and pointed the tip of her blade directly at Lian.
