chapters.title: Chapter 394: The Death That Never Happened
paragraphs: Lian looked at the face of the brother he had never really had the chance to know throughout his entire life.
Darian was only two years older than him.
But almost from the time he had clear memories of his childhood, his brother had spent most of his time outside the country.
Training periods, family missions, studies, and things that even many members of the Vorhelm family did not have exact information about.
Their meetings were limited to a few family dinners, several formal events, and sometimes a few days of Darian staying at the mansion before disappearing again for several months or even longer.
They had not spent enough time together to become close, but the more important point was that they had not even spent enough time together to become enemies.
Then why?
Why did Darian want to kill him?
Lian looked at his brother’s calm face for a few more moments, there was no memory of an old argument and as far as he knew, there had been no serious rivalry between them.
Even when they were children, their ages and circumstances had not allowed them to build a relationship that could later turn into hatred.
But then a second thought came to his mind.
Two women.
His father’s first wife and second wife.
Lian still remembered clearly that both of them, each for their own reasons, saw his removal as a desirable result.
Darian did not necessarily need to hate him personally, perhaps he had simply received an order.
"I have such a lovely family." He sighed and said sarcastically in his mind.
But that thought brought another memory out from the depths of his mind.
During his first hours after entering Base Number 9 and before entering the Special Area, at that time, while he was looking around the base, he had felt something.
A cold and powerful killing intent that was focused directly on him.
That feeling had appeared for such a short time that even with his instincts, he had not been able to find its exact source.
He was only sure that someone there had truly been thinking about killing him.
Then everything had happened one after another and among all those events, a few seconds of killing intent had become completely unimportant and had almost disappeared from his mind.
But now Lian remembered that moment completely again.
Darian had been in this area from the beginning and now he had also admitted himself that Lian’s death had made his "job much easier."
Could that killing intent have come from him? Of course, he had no proof, at least not yet, but the possibility was too reasonable for him to ignore.
Lian’s feelings immediately became cold, Darian was his brother, they shared the same blood, but for him, that fact had a limit.
"If you really came here to kill me, then I don’t care whether you’re my brother or not." He said quietly in his mind, and his gaze became colder.
At that moment, the panel in front of his eyes changed.
[Body reconstruction: 100%]
[Restoration process completed.]
[Stored life has been consumed.]
[The holder has returned to the flow of life.]
Suddenly, the sound of his heartbeat echoed, and after several minutes of complete silence, blood suddenly entered his veins with strong pressure.
Lian’s lungs opened and air entered them violently, but at the same moment, he controlled his instinct and did not allow a deep and noticeable breath to leave his mouth.

The feeling of his body had returned, the weight, the temperature, and the cold ground under his back, his clothes were torn and wet with blood, but the thing he had expected, the pain, was not there.
He checked the condition of his body for a moment.
The heart that Seris had pierced was healthy, his chest had been completely rebuilt, and there was no sign of the deep wound on his skin.
The broken bones from his previous battles were also completely gone.
All the damage that Black Silence, Seris, and the pressure of the past few days had caused to this body had disappeared.
Only the blood-covered and torn clothes showed what condition this body had been in a few minutes ago.
He did not open his eyes, nor did he get up.
Darian was only a few meters away and the four undead were still on the battlefield, and more importantly, Darian did not know that Lian had heard his words.
So there was no reason to throw away this advantage right now.
He could not stop his heartbeat, but he kept his breathing as low as possible and remained completely still.
For now, being dead was useful.
On the battlefield, something else was happening, and the situation had become even worse than before.
The four Ancient Cindari had realized that Black Silence was dead, they could no longer feel its presence.
Black Silence.
One of the Father’s children.
An existence that had become something beyond death, time, and defeat in the beliefs of their different generations for centuries, was gone, and this disappearance was not simply a sealing.
Its presence had completely disappeared.
For several seconds, all four beings remained motionless, the swordsman had lowered his blade, the root controller had kept his fingers on the ground.
The Cindari mage had even stopped the movement of the ashes around him, and the last Cindari had turned his head toward the place where Lian’s body was lying.
Then something broke inside them, more exactly, the belief that had been the foundation of their existence for centuries, the Father’s children did not die.
They could be sealed, they could be stopped, they could be kept away from the world for a while.
But destruction? Impossible.
And yet, nothing remained, and that alone was enough for their beliefs to begin falling apart and for them to question all of their beliefs and ideas.
The Cindari swordsman suddenly released a wordless scream from his throat and his complete calm disappeared.
His sword moved, but this time it had nothing in common with precise and controlled swordsmanship.
It was wild, as if his only goal was to go crazy and destroy everything in his path so he could control his emotions that were burning like fire.
The root controller slammed his foot into the ground.
BOOOOM!
The entire area exploded and hundreds of roots came out of the ground without caring whether they were friend or enemy.
The Cindari mage opened both hands and turned part of his half-destroyed body into ash.
He was no longer even trying to preserve his own existence.
And the other Cindari also roared and attacked the nearest living being.
Rindo barely blocked the first attack.
"Fall back!" He shouted as a warning, but he knew there was nowhere left to retreat.

Those four beings no longer wanted to stay alive, they did not want to win, their belief had died, and because of that, they only wanted to take everything that was still alive with them before they fell apart themselves.
Seraphina held her sword with both hands, tears were falling from her eyes, tears that she did not even have time to wipe were moving through the blood and dirt on her face.
These were tears that had started falling from her eyes when she saw Lian’s dead body.
The Cindari mage extended his hand and a huge wall of ash moved toward her and Selina.
"Down!" Selina shouted and released the last of her large amount of remaining mana.
A wave of water rose from the ground and the ash hit the water, hot steam covered the entire area.
Seraphina moved through the steam and mana gathered around her sword, and she struck the mage directly in the side.
The blade entered, but the creature struck the girl’s shoulder with his broken hand and sent her body flying backward.
Seraphina rolled on the ground, but immediately stabbed her sword into the ground and used it to pull herself back up.
Her eyes unconsciously moved toward Lian’s motionless body and she clenched her jaw, another tear fell from her eye and she attacked the enemy again.
Selina also looked at Lian for one moment longer than she should have, her face tightened, but another wave of ash forced her to immediately raise her hands.
On the other side of the battlefield, Liana was also making the same mistake again and again.
Every few seconds she took a short look and then immediately turned her face away.
Because she knew that if she allowed herself to think about it even one moment longer, she would not be able to fight.
Only a few meters away from Lian, Seris was lying on the ground.
Sovereign’s Last Stand had ended long ago.
And with its end, all the debt of her body had been collected at once, the pain had been so strong at first that she thought her body was burning.
Then, little by little, even the pain had gone away and turned into something worse, she could not feel anything.
She could not feel her fingers and her legs felt like they were no longer part of her body.
Her left arm did not respond at all and even moving her neck a few centimeters made darkness gather at the edge of her vision.
Seris did not know how many more minutes she would stay alive.
Maybe ten minutes.
Maybe one minute.
Maybe if she closed her eyes right now, she would never open them again.
But strangely, she did not care that much anymore and slowly turned her head.
Lian was lying beside her, his face was too calm, the same man who had returned for a fraction of a second only a few seconds ago.
He had shown her his real eyes.
"Do it." He had said.
Seris had done it, she had driven her sword straight through his heart, she had felt his heartbeat stop.
The system panel had confirmed the death of the vessel.
And Seris did not try to repeat the usual sentence in her mind or tell herself an excuse such as that it was to save the Earth, that she had no other choice, or that everyone would die.
She knew those things were true and she had no other choice.
But even so... her heart did not accept any excuse like her mind did... and it was burning with pain like hell.

chapters.title: Chapter 395: End Of Quest
paragraphs: Seris ignored the pain, she was not someone who would regret her actions, not when it had already been done.
She only looked at Lian’s face.
"At least you wanted it yourself." She whispered softly, and a strange heaviness formed in her chest.

Those two short words that had come from Lian’s mouth in his final moments had taken a heavy weight off her shoulders, but at the same time, the thought that part of him was still truly alive bothered her.
Her lips moved only slightly.
"Bastard... you even made me responsible for your death." She whispered in a voice so weak that it could barely be heard.
At that moment, the sound of approaching footsteps made her raise her gaze slightly.
Darian.
Before fully returning to the battlefield, Lian’s brother had noticed that Seris was still conscious and more importantly, he had realized that she had heard his words.
Their eyes met for a few seconds, and his smile was gone, leaving only a cold look.
"You can die too, Pendragon." He said simply, as if he was talking about something completely normal.
Seris looked at him for a few moments, she did not even have enough energy to become angry, and a very weak and mocking smile appeared on her blood-covered lips.
"I didn’t like you from the beginning." Seris replied in a rough voice.
Darian ignored her, as if replying to a girl who already looked dead was not worth his time.
Then, without saying anything, he turned around and raised his bow toward the Cindari swordsman.
The Young Pendragon also put her head back on the ground, she truly did not think it mattered anymore, with their current situation, it was unlikely that anyone would leave this place alive.
The four Cindari had gone mad and she was sure that no one had the power to deal with them anymore, they had not had that power from the beginning.
She also had no strength left to help.
There was no hope for anyone anymore...
But at that exact moment, a huge panel appeared in front of all the remaining Awakened.
[An abnormality has been detected in the result of the mission.]
Rindo saw the panel for a moment while moving back from the Cindari mage’s attack.
Seraphina also kept her sword raised and gave the words a quick look.
[Re-evaluating the current condition of the world...]
[Checking the final result...]
[Corrupted Titan: Dead.]
[Black Silence: Destroyed.]
[Threat of the Calamity reaching the Origin World: Removed.]
[The failure condition of the mission is no longer active.]
[The result of the main mission has been changed.]
Then a larger message appeared, a message that brought hope back into all of them.
[Congratulations.]
[You have successfully saved the world.]
For several seconds, no one reacted, because that sentence was too big.
Had the world really been saved?
After all those deaths?
After the Forgotten Tree?
The Titan?
Black Silence?
After all the difficulties they had gone through?
After all the sacrifices?
Rindo closed his eyes for a moment, but the battle was still continuing, so he immediately raised his weapon again.
The next panels appeared one after another.
[Calculating the contribution of all participants...]
[Calculation complete.]
[The reward of the main Quest has been applied with changes:]
[+3 Levels]
[+100 Fragments]
[+250 Stat Points]
[Special Treasure Chest ×1]
[Title: Calamity Survivor]
Seris looked at the words with one half-open eye, some of the rewards seemed to have changed, could it be related to the way they had completed the Quest?
However, at that moment, another notification appeared for her.
[The Host has reached the current level limit before evolution.]
[Level rewards will be stored until the completion of the evolution.]
Three levels.
One hundred Fragments.
Two hundred and fifty Stat Points.
Even after burning half of her stats, seeing the last number created a bitter feeling inside her for a moment.
She had lost one thousand points and now two hundred and fifty had returned.
Well... better than nothing, but she knew that bringing her stats back to 2000 would take a long time.
[The participants with the highest contribution to saving the world have been identified:]
[Lian Vorhelm]
[Seris Pendragon]
Seris’s eyes stayed on the first name for a moment.
Lian.
Even after his death, the system had still placed his name in the ranking, but there was no doubt that he had made the greatest sacrifice for this success...
[Outstanding Contribution Reward:]
[Golden Treasure Chest ×1]
[Special Title]
And Seris’s special panel immediately showed another message.
[Special Condition fulfilled.]
[You personally destroyed the Anchor of a Calamity.]
[You personally destroyed the Vessel of a Calamity.]
[Special Title received: Calamity Slayer]
"Calamity Slayer." She looked at the title for a few moments, for some reason, this title gave her a strange feeling.

But she did not care much about that strange feeling and turned her attention to the notification for the Golden Treasure Chest, she opened it without hesitation and another panel appeared only in front of her eyes.
Seris’s eyes moved over the lines, and the description of the reward she received from the Treasure Chest made her raise an eyebrow and stare at the panel for several seconds.
Then the corner of her lips moved up very slightly.
"Not a bad compensation for all this trouble." She whispered with weak satisfaction.
[Rewards for both Outstanding Contributors have been delivered.]
Seris frowned, rewards for both Outstanding Contributors?
Her eyes returned to the motionless body beside her.
Lian was dead, she had seen it herself, so what did "delivered" mean?
Did the system transfer the rewards of dead people to their families?
As far as she knew, no.
So maybe it was just a general way of writing the message, but something about that message bothered her.
The system usually did not use such unclear words for no reason.
She herself did not know why, but those words had caused a small hope to appear in her heart, a hope that had unconsciously excited her.
She was about to check the panel again when another warning covered everything.
[End of the main mission confirmed.]
[All surviving participants of the mission will be returned to the Ruined Realm in 10 seconds.]
The Cindari swordsman roared and attacked, and Darian fired a seven-colored arrow.
The arrow hit the sword and an explosion of light covered the battlefield.
Another Cindari punched, and Rindo threw himself in front of Cassian and blocked the attack with his sword.
Both of them moved several meters back.
The Root Controller blew up the entire ground.
"Break!" Aren shouted as he slammed his foot hard against the ground, and a wall of stone rose between the survivors and the roots.
The wall split apart instantly, and Liana pulled herself behind Aren.
The Cindari mage released a wave of fire and ash, and Selina was directly in the path of the attack, she had no mana left to defend herself.
Seraphina stepped forward, held her sword with both hands, her legs were shaking and tears were still on her face.
The transfer light slowly formed around the bodies of the survivors, and the four Undead became even more violent when they saw the light.
In the middle of all that chaos, Lian slowly opened his eyes.
His eyes were no longer purple, they were his own eyes again and his gaze was fixed directly on Darian’s back.
At that moment, Darian turned slightly to the side to fire his next arrow.
And maybe
Just maybe
He saw a movement from the corner of his eye and quickly turned his gaze toward Lian’s body.
But the transfer light became stronger.
Darian frowned, had he seen it correctly?
Or had the light simply changed the appearance of the dead man’s face?
Had he just imagined it?
He had no time to check.
[Foreign Human detected within the mission area.]
[Origin Alignment: Confirmed.]
[Emergency Return Conditions: Accepted.]
[Transfer Permission Granted.]
Then, for all the surviving Awakened, the entire world became white.
There was no sound, they could not feel any pain or the ground, and the only thing that existed was light.
But a moment later, everything returned.
Dozens of bodies appeared almost at the same time on a hard surface.
Some were standing, some were on their knees, and some had fallen to the ground from the very beginning
And the area they saw in the distance was completely different from a few seconds ago
Huge walls made of metal and stone.
Lights, watchtowers, and behind them, the same huge crack they had passed through to enter the Special Area, which slowly began to close after they came out.
They had returned to the Ruined Realm and Base#9

chapters.title: Chapter 396: After Nine Months
paragraphs: The guards who were on the other side of the area could only stare.
The returnees almost did not look like the people who had been sent off nine months ago, dried blood covered all of their clothes.
Their armor was broken and their faces were thin, wounded, and tired.
Rindo only looked at the familiar area around him for a few seconds, and that alone gave him a sense of relief, and his shoulders finally dropped after so long.
It was over, at least for now he did not need to worry about anything.
Selina sat down on the same ground, her legs could no longer support the weight of her body.
Liana also had a bitter expression on her face, her eyes were wet, she had lost both her friend and her summon.
She tried to say something but did not feel like talking...
Seraphina looked around once, the walls, the guards, the humans, and there was no sign of the Titan, no Ancient Cindari, and no Calamity.
They had really returned, and that certainty was the last thing her body needed to keep standing.
Her eyes closed and she fell to the ground.
"Seraphina!" Rindo called out with concern, but he was also barely staying conscious.
Cassian sat down a few meters away, his weapon fell from his hand and he rested his head against the wall behind him.
"Finally..." he whispered in a weak voice.
Aren was the only one whose reaction could not be turned off immediately even by exhaustion.
He was standing and looking at the area around him.
He had escaped from that damned world...? The same world where he had lived for 25 years...? He had been trapped there for 25 years?
His eyes kept moving between the towers, the lights, and the people running toward them with equipment.
Was this his own world? He looked at the sky, and when he saw its color, he became certain that this really was his own world...
But why did he not remember this place? Could it have been built during the years he was gone? It was possible, and even likely, after all, a lot of time had passed.
Unfortunately, he still did not know that he, Lian, and the rest of his saviors... were not even from the same world.
One of the officers recognized their faces and his eyes widened.
"They’re back!" he shouted in disbelief.
Several others immediately turned around.
"What?!"
"They’re them!"
"The Special Area group is back!"
"Nine months..." the man said in shock.
"After nine months, they finally came back!"
The area exploded in an instant, and the sound of sirens, the shouts of commanders, and the running of soldiers and medical teams came from several entrances.
The officers tried to count the number of people, but they did not even know where to start.
Nine months had passed since the expedition team entered that rift, and now that they had returned after nine months, all of them were in terrible conditions.

Nine months was not enough time for them to think that all the members of the expedition had died or that something had happened to them, exploring Special Areas was normally something that took time.
Especially considering that in the past, there had also been cases where differences in time had existed.
Seris could barely see any of them properly, the voices were far away, the lights were too bright, and her eyes could barely stay open.
Her body was lying on the ground and she could not even lift her head, she could only see shadows running around them.
Someone knelt beside her and said something about her blood pressure, and another person became more serious and acted faster after seeing her wounds.
The healers were quickly treating all of them.

She did not care, her eyes only moved to the other side for a few seconds to look at the surroundings, but her mind no longer had the strength to analyze anything, and without being able to see anything, her eyes slowly closed.
The last thing she heard was the voice of one of the healers.
"Take this one immediately!"
Then darkness covered everything.
Three days later
Their return took less than an hour to become the biggest news in the world.
Nine months.
Almost nine full months had passed since hundreds of young Awakened entered the Special Area.
The families had waited for months and the governments had no exact explanation, they could not see what was happening inside the rift, and it was even possible that there was no rift anymore.
But this did not mean that they had been terrified and had uncontrollable worry, everyone knew about Special Areas and knew that spending months, and in some cases even years, inside them was normal.
There were even times when differences in the passage of time happened, which could make everything more complicated.
Some of the worry came from the fact that most of the Awakened who had entered and been sent there were young people with good talents and promising futures.
Their families and the people behind them were waiting for their return and to see how much they had improved.
And suddenly the survivors returned, on a completely normal day and in a way that nobody expected.
But their number was only about one-third of the people who had entered.
And even that one-third had not returned safely, some had lost parts of their bodies, some had permanent damage to their mana paths.
Some had almost completely healed bodies, but their minds had not.
A young man who hid under his bed at the smallest sound of an explosion.
A girl who, after waking up, refused to stay alone even for a few minutes.
A man who shouted the names of his dead friends every time he fell asleep.
Some survivors only cried when they saw their families.
Some had no reaction at all and only stared, as if their minds still had not understood that they had really returned.
This caused the related organizations to fall into shock, wondering exactly what had happened to these young Awakened that such fear had taken over them.
Something that could create such serious trauma was not just a few fights with some monsters, and it was clear that much bigger and more frightening things had happened to them.
Something that even now they could not move past.
The interviews started very quickly.
And stories came out from the mouths of the Awakened, healers, soldiers, and families.
Stories of Awakened who had been in Glassthorne, those who, with the help of a Vorhelm, had brought down an entire city called Crystal Line.
Stories of Awakened who had acted alone and looked for their own opportunities and had avoided forming groups.
And finally, stories of the Awakened who had been trapped in Vhalaris, a story that caused the most noise and different reactions.
Intelligent creatures called Cindari, a giant tree that was connected to the life of the world.
A war with a non-human civilization, being captured and capturing them, and how with the help of an Awakened named Lian Vorhelm, they had taken the entire Vhalaris within a few hours.

Being forced to cooperate with them and trying to stop the war that had happened between them, a war that ended in a huge massacre on both sides, the same war in which they had managed to stand their ground with the help and leadership of an Awakened named Rindo.
And that terrible madness and corruption that had suddenly spread everywhere and caused madness, the desire to kill, and massacres.
And for several hours, one word appeared everywhere, Calamity.
Several survivors had talked about a creature named Black Silence.

One said it was a monster that had corrupted a world, another claimed that it had taken the body of a human, and another person claimed that if they had not stopped this Calamity, it would have entered their world.
The names Lian Vorhelm and Seris Pendragon were also repeated in some of the stories.
But a few hours later, everything changed.
Videos that directly talked about the "Calamity" disappeared.
Parts of the interviews were removed, and the major media no longer used that word.
The official statement only talked about "a very powerful and unknown creature at a level beyond recorded threats."
Even some survivors who had spoken freely on the first day were unwilling to answer questions about that part on the second day.
It was clear that much higher powers had entered the matter, but even censorship could not erase the entire story.
But everything spread only as rumors and unclear stories, and no complete explanation was published by the organizations, official institutions, or the Awakened Federation.
For three full days, the return from the Special Area remained the number one news story in the world.
And during those three days, they started waking up one by one.
Rindo woke up earlier than many of the others.
Cassian a few hours later.
The first thing Liana did after waking up was ask about Selina.

Aren was placed under heavy supervision almost immediately after his initial treatment, an unknown man who spoke an unknown language, and after questioning, it was discovered that he was a native of the Ruined Realm.
He never expected that after returning to his world, the first thing that would happen to him would be getting arrested and being questioned.
But some people needed more time to fully heal and recover, and one of them was Seris Pendragon.
Three days after their return, her eyes slowly opened.

Three days after their return, her eyes slowly opened.

chapters.title: Chapter 397: He Is... Alive?
paragraphs: At first, she could barely see the white light, it was too white, and for a few seconds she could not see anything clearly.
Then the image slowly became clear, and the hospital ceiling, white walls, and small lights also entered her field of view.
Seris blinked and her eyes became slightly narrower, she was in the base, in Base #9, they had really returned and everything had not been just an illusion.
Her memories slowly came back.
The cemetery, the Titan, Black Silence, and Lian and all those damned events that she had experienced inside that Special Area, each one of them replayed in her mind.
And the scene that she could never forget... the moment when her blade had pierced through Lian’s chest.
Seris closed her eyes, but Lian’s face did not leave her mind, so she opened them again.
"Damn..." she whispered in a weak voice.
She did not want to think about it right now, she needed to calm her mind, and to distract herself, she opened the System panel.
[First Evolution Quest: Completed.]
[Evolution Path is available.]
[Evolution Path: Blade of moon]
Seris stared at the name for a moment, blade of moon, a name that strangely matched most of her path of power.
[Evolution information is available.]
[Would you like to view it?]
She was still about to choose the option when she heard the door opening, she turned her head slightly and a woman entered the room alone.
She had no guards with her, and of course, she did not need any.
Aurelia Pendragon entered with calm steps, and as soon as she noticed that Seris’s eyes were open, a smile appeared on her face.
"Finally awake." she said with satisfaction and walked directly to the bed.
Seris looked at her with a little surprise.
Without calling a healer, Aurelia held her palm a few centimeters above the girl’s body.
A very thin wave of mana passed through.
For someone at her level, checking the general condition of an Awakened did not require a healer or a doctor.
A few seconds later, she lowered her hand, and from her expression, it was clear that the young Pendragon was completely fine.
"I didn’t expect you to come yourself." Seris said in a voice that was still weak, but her familiar cold tone was slowly returning.
"We had no news about the greatest genius of our family for nine months." Aurelia said in a tone as if the answer should have been completely obvious.
Seris froze for a moment.
"Then suddenly they tell us that you came back and you’re almost at death’s door, and I’m your guardian, of course my family would send me."
"Nine months?" Seris was still stuck on the first part of the sentence and asked with a frown.
"Almost."
She stayed silent for a few seconds, she knew that there was a difference in time, she knew that time inside that world was not the same as outside.
But... nine months? Almost a year had passed in the outside world.
So many things had happened inside that the length of time no longer had a clear meaning for her.
And that meant that while they had spent about one month inside, the other Awakened had had nine full months to hunt, advance, and become stronger.
Probably all the geniuses their age had already completed their first evolution and were now getting close to their second evolution.
And them? It could not even be said that they had really completed their first evolution yet.
Then her thoughts moved for a moment toward the special reward that the System had given her before the transfer.
The corner of her lips moved very slightly, considering what she had received, perhaps those nine months were not completely worthless.
"Looks like a lot of things are going through that head of yours." Aurelia saw her expression and her eyes became slightly narrower.
She sat more comfortably in the chair and then changed her tone.

"What the hell did you guys do in there? I’ve heard a hundred stories with hundreds of different versions for three days, one says you fought an entire civilization, another says the world was going crazy, and some people talk about the death of a tree that they say the life of the world was connected to."
Seris said nothing, none of them were wrong, there were many stories to tell.
"But the most interesting version is the most popular one, in that one, you’re the hero of the story." Aurelia continued with amusement.
The young Pendragon’s face looked emotionless and surprised, and she laughed when she saw her reaction.
"When I first heard it, I couldn’t believe it, you? Playing the hero?"
"Lian was the main hero." Seris answered seriously, almost without thinking.
"Lian Vorhelm?" Aurelia asked with curiosity.
"He sacrificed himself to save everyone." She nodded and lowered her gaze slightly, and the image of his motionless body appeared in her mind again.
Silence filled the room for a few seconds, and then Aurelia laughed, at first it was only a short sound, but a moment later her laughter became louder.
Seris’s face immediately became cold, her eyes fixed on Aurelia in a dangerous way.
"What are you laughing at?" she asked in a calm but completely threatening voice, and there was even a kind of hidden killing intent in it.
But Aurelia only became more amused.
"Oh? Why did you become so defensive?" Aurelia said with a raised eyebrow, becoming even more amused, and then her smile became wider.
Seris frowned, suddenly she had a bad feeling, and she could predict that she was not going to like the next sentences.
Aurelia studied her face for a few moments, and then as if she had suddenly found something very interesting, she laughed again.
"Don’t tell me you actually fell in love in that world?" she asked mischievously.
"Shut up." The young Pendragon made a sound like an annoyed growl from her throat and answered with a frown.
"Okay, okay, don’t be so sensitive." Aurelia said while still laughing.
Seris looked at her without interest, and it was clear that she did not like those laughs at all.
"I wasn’t laughing at Lian."
"Then what were you laughing at?" She said coldly.
"The word sacrifice, why are you talking as if that boy is dead?" Aurelia asked with slight disbelief.
The entire room became silent for Seris, and for several seconds she could not hear any sound, as if her brain had received such a shock that it ignored everything.
"Because he’s dead, I killed him." she finally answered completely seriously.
"What?" This time the woman’s eyebrows really rose, and she asked in disbelief.
"I stabbed his heart with my sword, I felt his heartbeat stop myself." Seris lowered her gaze for a moment and said in a calm voice.
Aurelia said nothing for several seconds, her face slowly taking on an expression between confusion and worry, the first possibility that came to her mind was obvious.
Mental trauma.
Medicine.
Shock.
"Could the injuries you suffered have caused you to hallucinate?" she then asked carefully.
"I’m completely conscious." Seris’s eyes immediately became cold, and she answered in a firm tone.
Aurelia was still not convinced.

"Wait, if you’re sure you weren’t hallucinating, then are you sure we’re talking about a boy? Lian Vorhelm? The same handsome boy we saw at Diana Vorhelm’s birthday ceremony?" Aurelia asked with emphasis.
Seris only nodded.
Yes.
The two of them only stared at her for a few seconds.
"Seris... he’s completely alive."
The young Pendragon did not even blink, as if the sentence had reached her brain, but her mind still could not process its meaning.
And Aurelia continued.
"Actually, out of all of you, he was the healthiest person who returned." she said, surprised by this fact herself.
Seris’s eyes opened a little wider.
Aurelia was now truly sure that there was something in this story that she did not know about.
"When you all came out of the rift three days ago, almost all of you were either unconscious or barely alive."
"But him? He didn’t even have a single scratch."

Seris was now completely motionless, she was absolutely sure that she remembered everything, the blade entering his heart, the blood splashing, and Black Silence’s hand only a few centimeters away from his head.
The stopped heartbeat and even the System notification.
[Death of the Vessel detected.]
She had seen all of it, all of it had been real, she was sure that Vorhelm was dead.

"But he’s in this same base right now, the base officials asked him to explain what happened in the Special Area, as far as I know, he’s with the base authorities right now." And Aurelia delivered the final shock.
Seris’s brain truly stopped working for a few seconds, she could not find any logical explanation.
She had killed Lian, not imagined that he was dead, not mistaken his pulse, and even the System had confirmed his death.
But he was alive? Healthy? Without even a single scratch?
All of Seris’s control over her expression completely disappeared, her eyes opened wide, her lips slightly parted.
"Hah?" she said in complete disbelief and only stared at Aurelia for several seconds.
One thought repeated in her mind again and again.
Lian was alive?

chapters.title: Chapter 398: Not So Happy
paragraphs: The white transfer light swallowed everything for a few seconds.

There was no sound of battle left, no smell of blood from the Giants’ Graveyard and no suffocating pressure of the four Ancient Cindari, only that complete whiteness that separated the surviving bodies from a world that was falling apart.
A moment later, the light disappeared.
Dozens of bodies appeared almost at the same time in front of the huge rift of Base Number 9.
Some of them fell to the ground immediately.
Some were not even conscious enough to understand where they were and a few others could only stay on their feet for a few more seconds by leaning on their broken weapons.
Among them, Lian was also lying on the ground.
From a few meters away, his condition looked terrible.
His clothes were almost completely covered in dried blood.
The cloth over his chest, where Seris’s sword had passed through his heart, was completely torn open and a large dark bloodstain covered much of his upper body.
But there was no wound under those clothes, the skin on his chest was smooth and his ribs were fine.
His heart was beating at a completely normal rhythm and mana was moving through his paths without the smallest problem.
Two healers almost ran toward him at the same time after seeing his blood-covered clothes and one of them knelt beside Lian and placed two fingers on his neck.
A few seconds later, he frowned.
"Wait..." the healer said with confusion and changed the position of his fingers again.
The second healer, who was taking out a checking tool, quickly looked at him.
"What happened?" he asked with concern.
The first healer did not answer.
He removed his hand from Lian’s neck and this time held his palm a few centimeters above his chest, a faint ring of mana appeared and passed from Lian’s head to his feet.
A small status panel appeared in front of him and the man stared at the results for a few moments.
Then he scanned him again.
The second healer became impatient.
"What happened?" he asked more firmly this time.
"Nothing." the first healer answered with a frown.
For a moment, the second man thought he had heard wrong.
"What do you mean, nothing?" he asked in disbelief and pointed at Lian’s clothes that were almost covered in blood.
"Just what I said, he has no injuries." the first healer said in a way that even he could not believe his own answer.
"Then where did all this blood come from?"
"I don’t know."
And at that exact moment, Lian’s eyes opened.
The first thing he felt was air, real air, without the smell of the Titan’s decay, without ash and without the presence of Black Silence.
For a moment he only breathed, then the shouts of the healers, the running soldiers and the emergency alarms entered his ears.
He had really returned, he had finally returned to the Ruined Realm with his own body.
Lian slowly raised his head.
The healer who was kneeling beside him almost took a step back.
"You’re conscious?" the man asked in surprise.
The young Vorhelm did not answer immediately, he placed his palm on the ground and slowly sat up.
His clothes were stuck to his skin and almost his entire body smelled like blood, but he felt no physical pain.
His eyes briefly moved toward his own hands.
They were fine and even the small scars from his previous injuries had disappeared.
The extra life had not only started his heart again, it had completely rebuilt his body.
Lian was still checking his body when his eyes moved to the right and stopped on someone.
Darian.
His older brother was standing several dozen meters away.
His armor was broken and covered in blood in several places, but compared to the other survivors, his condition was relatively good.
He was probably the healthiest person to return from the Graveyard after Lian.
Darian also saw him at that exact moment and his expression changed for less than a second.
It was so small that if Lian had not heard his words a few minutes earlier, he might not have noticed it at all.
Darian’s usual smile disappeared for a moment and his eyes opened slightly wider, a short flash of pure shock appeared in his eyes.

He was truly surprised, not just surprised but even shocked and stunned ... how? How was he alive? How was this bastard still alive? He was sure he was dead! He should have been dead, his heart had been pierced! So how was he still alive?
Then everything disappeared and he did not let even the smallest sign of emotion show, and the same relaxed smile appeared on his face again.
"Thanks for your help, it’s true that I couldn’t control my body but I saw everything." Lian smiled and spoke in a way that only he could hear.
"It was my duty to protect our world from that disaster." Darian said with a completely honest expression.
"Another reason I was able to survive was because of your help, so I should thank you."
"I’m glad you’re alive, at least I don’t have to be the one to take the news of your death home."
For anyone else, the sentence was just something a brother would say, but Lian still had the voice of that same man in his mind.
I never thought you’d kill yourself without me even needing to get my hands dirty.

"It’s true that, like other brothers and sisters, we don’t really know each other, but I’m glad I saw you, I hope we can see each other again before you leave this base." Lian said calmly with a sarcastic tone.
"Of course." Darian answered casually.
Then the shout of one of the healers made his gaze move away from Lian.

But Lian was sure about one thing, Darian’s shock had been real, he had not expected him to stand up again and the fact that he was alive had clearly caused disbelief and disappointment in him, as if his goal had failed.
Even so, he still showed nothing, for now it was better for Darian to continue believing that nobody had heard his words.
Lian looked away from his brother and checked the area around him.
Rindo was a few meters away among the healers, Cassian was there as well, Liana was sitting on the ground and Selina was almost unconscious from exhaustion.
Seraphina had completely lost consciousness.
Aren was standing in pain between several officers and healers, looking around in confusion.
Seris was also being carried away on a stretcher.
But something was missing, he looked around one more time and then his expression became serious.
One.
There was no sign of the giant ant.
Lian’s eyes narrowed slightly and he immediately opened his system panel.
[Hive Link]
[Status: Active.]
The slight pressure in his chest became a little weaker, the skill had not disappeared and to make sure, he opened the next panel.
[Colony:]
[Member: One.]
[Status: Alive.]
Lian stared at the last line for a few seconds, it was alive, at least that part was solved and he did not need to worry about the life of the only member of his colony.
But why had it not been transferred with them? Even Aren had been transferred even though he was an Awakener and was not from their world.
But why had the member of his colony not been transferred?
He focused his attention on the connection and a new panel appeared.
[Distance from Network Member: Outside the World Boundary.]
[Direct Connection: Impossible.]
[Interworld Path: Not Detected.]
Lian frowned.
So One had remained in that world.
The transfer had probably only returned the main participants of the mission and the humans recognized by the system.
One was neither of those, he was a native creature that had become connected to Lian through the S-Rank innate talent, Mother of the Colony.
He checked more options to see if he could find a way to summon him or something similar.
His S-Rank talent also had other innate abilities that had not been unlocked yet and unlocking them required him to complete the First Evolution.
Maybe if he completed his evolution, he could find a way to bring One to this world.
"So I found another reason." Lian quietly said under his breath.
His evolution was no longer only for himself, if his guess was correct, it was also the only way to bring his giant ant to this world.
His condition was not good the last time he had seen him.
No matter how fast the transfer had happened and no matter how slowly time passed there, he did not want to leave him alone for too long.
"Sir, we need to go." the healer beside Lian said seriously.
"I’m fine and I don’t need treatment." Lian answered as he slowly stood up.
The healer stared at him for a few seconds and then looked at his clothes, the torn chest and dried blood from his neck to his waist.
The man let out a short sigh.
"With respect, what you’re wearing right now is almost completely made of blood." he said dryly.
Lian looked at himself.
"This is old blood, I didn’t have any clothes to change into, so it became like this." Lian calmly explained.
The healer was silent for a moment and then his face tightened.
"That doesn’t make me feel better at all."
"You might have internal injuries that the first check did not find. Your mana paths or soul could be damaged, even if we find nothing, you at least need a full check."
Lian looked at the others for a moment.
The healers were already quickly taking Seris, Seraphina and several others toward the medical section.
There was no point in arguing anymore.
"Fine."
"Thank you." the healer almost breathed in relief.
In the end, he was forced to spend almost an entire day in the medical section of Base Number 9.

I never thought you’d kill yourself without me even needing to get my hands dirty.

"It’s true that, like other brothers and sisters, we don’t really know each other, but I’m glad I saw you, I hope we can see each other again before you leave this base." Lian said calmly with a sarcastic tone.
"Of course." Darian answered casually.
Then the shout of one of the healers made his gaze move away from Lian.

But Lian was sure about one thing, Darian’s shock had been real, he had not expected him to stand up again and the fact that he was alive had clearly caused disbelief and disappointment in him, as if his goal had failed.
Even so, he still showed nothing, for now it was better for Darian to continue believing that nobody had heard his words.
Lian looked away from his brother and checked the area around him.
Rindo was a few meters away among the healers, Cassian was there as well, Liana was sitting on the ground and Selina was almost unconscious from exhaustion.
Seraphina had completely lost consciousness.
Aren was standing in pain between several officers and healers, looking around in confusion.
Seris was also being carried away on a stretcher.
But something was missing, he looked around one more time and then his expression became serious.
One.
There was no sign of the giant ant.
Lian’s eyes narrowed slightly and he immediately opened his system panel.
[Hive Link]
[Status: Active.]
The slight pressure in his chest became a little weaker, the skill had not disappeared and to make sure, he opened the next panel.
[Colony:]
[Member: One.]
[Status: Alive.]
Lian stared at the last line for a few seconds, it was alive, at least that part was solved and he did not need to worry about the life of the only member of his colony.
But why had it not been transferred with them?
Even Aren had been transferred even though he was an Awakener and was not from their world.
But why had the member of his colony not been transferred?
He focused his attention on the connection and a new panel appeared.
[Distance from Network Member: Outside the World Boundary.]
[Direct Connection: Impossible.]
[Interworld Path: Not Detected.]
Lian frowned.
So One had remained in that world.
The transfer had probably only returned the main participants of the mission and the humans recognized by the system.
One was neither of those, he was a native creature that had become connected to Lian through the S-Rank innate talent, Mother of the Colony.
He checked more options to see if he could find a way to summon him or something similar.
His S-Rank talent also had other innate abilities that had not been unlocked yet and unlocking them required him to complete the First Evolution.
Maybe if he completed his evolution, he could find a way to bring One to this world.
"So I found another reason." Lian quietly said under his breath.
His evolution was no longer only for himself, if his guess was correct, it was also the only way to bring his giant ant to this world.
His condition was not good the last time he had seen him.
No matter how fast the transfer had happened and no matter how slowly time passed there, he did not want to leave him alone for too long.
"Sir, we need to go." the healer beside Lian said seriously.
"I’m fine and I don’t need treatment." Lian answered as he slowly stood up.
The healer stared at him for a few seconds and then looked at his clothes, the torn chest and dried blood from his neck to his waist.
The man let out a short sigh.
"With respect, what you’re wearing right now is almost completely made of blood." he said dryly.
Lian looked at himself.
"This is old blood, I didn’t have any clothes to change into, so it became like this." Lian calmly explained.
The healer was silent for a moment and then his face tightened.
"That doesn’t make me feel better at all."
"You might have internal injuries that the first check did not find.
Your mana paths or soul could be damaged, even if we find nothing, you at least need a full check."
Lian looked at the others for a moment.
The healers were already quickly taking Seris, Seraphina and several others toward the medical section.
There was no point in arguing anymore.
"Fine."
"Thank you." the healer almost breathed in relief.
In the end, he was forced to spend almost an entire day in the medical section of Base Number 9.

chapters.title: Chapter 399: First Evolution I
paragraphs: Every test they performed only made the healers more confused.
All of Lian’s organs and body parts were working normally without any problem or damage.
There were not even any healed fractures to be seen.
The mana pathways throughout his body were also stable and his soul showed no clear damage.
The third healer stared at the screen in front of him for several minutes after checking the results.
"Is there a problem?" Lian asked while sitting on the bed.
"No, and that’s exactly the problem, not only are you not injured, some of your body stats are even higher than the normal level." the healer answered with a strange expression.
The effect of the Extra Life had probably restored his body to a completely perfect condition.
After the healers also confirmed that he was completely healthy, they told him that he could leave whenever he wanted.
But before leaving, Lian slept for almost twelve hours, not because of physical tiredness, after all, his body did not have that kind of tiredness anymore.
The main reason was that after a long time, his mind finally had no immediate threat to follow.
He had been trapped inside his own body for several days.
His identity had been slowly eaten away.
He had died.
He had come back to life.
He had fought against a catastrophe inside a spiritual space.
And in the end, he had swallowed that same catastrophe inside something he still did not even know what it was.
The Heart of the Ruined Realm.
And through all of this, the last thing he had heard before returning to life was the indirect confession of his own brother that he had come to kill him.
Even his mind needed to shut down for a few hours.
The next morning, while he was getting ready to leave, two people entered his room.
Both were wearing dark formal clothes and each of them had the silver symbol of the World Awakened Federation on their chest.
One was a man around forty years old with short gray hair and the other was a younger woman holding a floating tablet.
The man stepped forward a few steps.
"Lian Vorhelm?"
"Yes, that’s me." Lian answered calmly.
"There are some questions you need to answer."
He raised an eyebrow.
"Don’t worry, we only have a few basic questions."
"Ask."
Both of them sat on the chairs around the bed, before asking detailed questions, they asked him to give a general summary of his experiences inside the Special Area.
Lian thought for a moment and after deciding what he wanted to say, he gave them a general summary without going into details.
His journey through the Giant Forest, Glassthorn and finally Emberroot and the important experiences they had there.
It was clear that the first and second ones were not important to them and their attention was actually on the third forest.
"When was your first encounter with the Cindari?"
"Do you confirm the existence of an organized native civilization?"
"How many cities did you see, approximately?"
"What exactly was the Forgotten Tree?"
All the questions being asked were clearly based on information they had gotten from the other Awakened who had already woken up.
And they had probably heard Lian’s name several times in their statements and decided to come and question him directly, and their questions confirmed this.
He answered as much as necessary, most of the answers were things that Rindo, Cassian and the other members of their group already knew and there was no reason to hide them.
When the questions reached the final days, the female officer raised her eyes from the tablet.
"What was your role in the end of the Quest?"
"It’s complicated." Lian answered simply.
The two officers looked at each other for a moment.
The woman opened her mouth, but the man slightly raised his hand.
"About the final events...the base officials prefer to speak with you personally."

The young Vorhelm understood a lot from that sentence, they did not have the right to ask the next questions, they probably did not even have the access level needed to know the full details about Black Silence.
"The person who returned with you is clearly a native of the Ruined Realm, and there are a few other things, parts of the reports have been sent directly to the command level."
"If you can give us some time within the next two days, the base officials have some more detailed questions, we will tell you the exact time."
"No problem." Lian answered, he had not forgotten Aren.
He planned to go and check on his condition today and make sure they were not hurting him, even though he was a native of the Ruined Realm, he had helped them a lot.
But that man had also suffered many injuries and was currently under treatment, and his interrogation would not begin until the treatment process was finished.
So there was no reason to worry.
"Thank you for your cooperation." both officers thanked him and then both of them left the room.
After they left, the first thing he did was look at his own clothes.
The blood-covered clothes were lying on the chair, dry and torn, the chest area was almost completely unusable.
"I don’t think this can be used anymore." Lian muttered.
He opened his storage space.
Fortunately, he had brought several extra sets of clothes with him before entering the Special Area.
At that time, he had only prepared for a long journey.
He did not know that the extra clothes would be useful after dying and coming back to life.
He took out dark pants, a simple black shirt and a pair of comfortable shoes and a few minutes later, he stood in front of the mirror.
Everything looked perfect and complete and then he also left the medical center.
He had more important things to deal with, for example, his first evolution.
As soon as he left the medical building, he stopped for a few seconds.
Base #9 had changed, just from its size it was clear that it had become several times larger than what he had seen the last time, many buildings that had not existed before had been built.
Official branch buildings of the Federation and organizations and institutions related to Awakened, and many guilds had also opened office branches here.
Lian slowly walked through the street and the first thing he noticed was that the population had also increased.
Awakened could be seen almost everywhere, groups returning from hunting and groups checking their equipment.
Mercenaries who were discussing contract prices beside the mission offices and young people who were excitedly comparing their new weapons.
He stopped in front of the huge floating screen in the main square of the base.
The map of the explored part of the Ruined Realm was displayed on it.
For a few seconds, he only looked at the colored lines.
Nine months ago, the human area was much smaller and was around one hundred kilometers and could barely reach one thousand.
Now the map had expanded to a huge distance in several directions.
A number in the corner of the screen caught his attention.
[Stabilized radius from Base #9: 8,907 kilometers.]
Lian raised an eyebrow.
More than eight thousand kilometers and almost nine thousand kilometers.
Below it, there was more information.
[Permanent observation points: 97]
[Active intermediate forts: 31]
[Registered hunting areas: 309]
[Confirmed high-risk areas: 21]
[Stabilized trade routes: 17]
He stared at the map for a moment, the progress was much greater than he had expected.
In nine months, humans had taken territory through large-scale expansion, built roads, created intermediate bases and classified hunting areas.
Even a complete economy around the Ruined Realm was starting to form.
"Nine months really isn’t a short time." he quietly said to himself, and there was another point that he noticed when his eyes fell on the recruitment requests for groups.
And to make sure, he looked at all the other screens that could provide information about this subject.
The subject was the average level of Awakened around his age.
His eyes narrowed slightly, nine months ago many young Awakened had just reached level ten.
Level ten was still considered an important boundary and now?
Level twenty-something seemed almost normal for serious young groups and most groups wanted members with at least level 20.
While the last time he had left this place and entered that rift, most young groups at best wanted members around level 10.
Many people around his age had already completed their first evolution.
And this made him feel another reality, he was behind.

Of course, not in the sense that he had become weaker, but time outside had moved forward without him and many people of his generation had reached level twenty-something and started their evolution paths.
While Lian was still level twenty and behind his first evolution, of course, none of them had been forced to swallow an entire catastrophe to evolve.
This was not a small difference.
"What about Kain?" the face of his best friend appeared in his mind.
The last time he had seen Kain, everything had been completely different and he had probably completed his first evolution by now too.
Maybe he had gained several new skills, maybe he was even one of the most famous young Awakened in Base #3 now.
And with his talent, it was not even unlikely that he was close to his second evolution, and if this was true, the distance between them had become very large.
"I don’t know if he went to get my armor for me or not, considering how expensive it probably was, probably not."
Another thought suddenly came to his mind.
The armor.
Before entering the Special Area, he had ordered the creation of an Ancient Rank armor.
At that time, they had said that making it would take some time, but this time was only supposed to be one month and nine months was definitely more than enough for the armor to be completed.
If the creator had not sold it or given it to someone else, which he naturally would not do, it should be completely ready.
Then he slightly shook his head, he had many things to do, he even had a large number of monster corpses to sell.
But all of these things had to wait until at least tomorrow, he had something more important to do today.
About half an hour later, he reached the more luxurious area of the base.
And there he saw a building he knew very well, the same inn where he had rented a room for the night nine months ago, before entering the Special Area.
But even that had changed and the previous building had been expanded and two new floors had been added to it.
The entrance had become larger and the outside area was now a parking area for vehicles made for Awakened and several high-level guards were standing beside the entrance.
Lian entered.

The inside also looked more crowded and more expensive, ordinary travelers were almost nowhere to be seen and most customers were members of large unions, professional Awakened or people whose equipment showed that they made a lot of money from hunting.
He walked toward the counter.
"Welcome, how can I help you?" the employee asked politely.
"I want a good room, the best one if possible." Lian answered.
"For how many nights?"
"For now, two nights."
The woman showed him the price and he saw the number and slightly raised an eyebrow, the price was almost twice what it had been nine months ago.
"The city has become expensive."
The employee laughed.
"Everything has become more expensive, but the hunters’ income has also increased." and then she answered jokingly.
Lian paid the cost and the room key was given to him in the form of a small token.
"Fifth floor, room 512."
He nodded and not long after, he reached his room and closed the door.
The room really looked luxurious and comfortable, he closed the window and then without hesitation slowly sat on the large bed.
Outside, evening was slowly settling over Base #9.
But his attention was no longer on the city, all his attention was on the evolution and on thinking about how he could move forward and what was waiting for him after swallowing Black Silence.
"It’s time."
The blue system panel appeared in front of him.
[Name: Lian Vorhelm]
[Race: Human]
[Class: Monster]
[Level: 20]
[First Evolution is available]
[Quest rewards are available]
His eyes stayed on the last line for a moment, the Quest rewards should be the same rewards that had been given for destroying Black Silence and the Titan.
But he put it aside for now, he could look at them later too.
The next panel opened.
[First Evolution Quest]
[Condition: Swallow one of the five Calamities.]
[Status: Completed.]
[Swallowed Calamity: Black Silence.]
[First Evolution is available.]
Lian stared at the message, finally, after all that trouble, he was truly ready.
[Stored levels: 3]
[Reward levels will be applied after completing the evolution.]
[Would you like to begin the First Evolution?]
[Yes / No]
Without hesitation, he chose the "Yes" option.
[Confirmed.]
[First Evolution is beginning.]
And the light swallowed the entire room.

chapters.title: Chapter 400: First Evolution II
paragraphs: [First Evolution has begun.]
Lian stared at the message in front of his eyes for several seconds while sitting on the edge of the bed.
He expected something to happen immediately; pain, a burst of mana, a change or something like that but nothing happened and the room remained silent.
"That’s it?".
One second passed.
Two seconds.
Then suddenly ...
Thump.
Lian suddenly sat up straight.
His heartbeat was so heavy that he could not only feel it inside his chest, but the dull sound of it also spread through the room.
His eyes narrowed.
Thump.
The second heartbeat was even heavier and pain came with it.
He breathed out hard and pressed his hand against the edge of the bed, something deep inside his bones had started to move; not breaking, but changing.
[Biological reconstruction has begun.]
[Secondary body template selected: Fallen Monster.]
The quiet but continuous sound of bones moving came from inside his body.
His spine slowly stretched.
His vertebrae became denser and stronger, and the bones in his shoulders slowly expanded to the sides.
His ribcage also became slightly larger, as if his body was being redesigned to handle a pressure that a normal human body should never have to handle.
Lian clenched his teeth, the pain was bearable.
After what he had endured in the spiritual space against Black Silence, this was not even close to the worst thing he had experienced.
But it was strange, he could feel every single change.
His muscle tissues began to rebuild.
It was not that his muscles became extremely large; instead, the visible difference was not that great, but every muscle fiber became thicker, denser and several times more efficient.
The power of his contractions increased, his connective tissues became stronger, and his tendons and joints were rebuilt so his body could produce more force without breaking under that force.
Lian closed his right fist, even this simple movement felt different from before.
He felt that if he wanted, he could release much more force from the same muscle he had possessed only a few minutes ago.
"So it wasn’t just the numbers on the panel." He looked at his hand with more interest.
The evolution was changing his body itself.
The process continued for several minutes and he clearly felt his legs become slightly longer.
His arms also became slightly longer.
His shoulders became wider and even when he stood up from the bed, he noticed that his angle of view of the room had changed slightly.
It seemed that a few centimeters had been added to his body, not enough to turn him into a completely different person but enough for him to notice it himself.
His weight had also increased.
Much more than what a few centimeters of extra height and a small amount of muscle should have caused.
The wooden floor of the room made a quiet sound when he took a step.
He looked down, the density of his bones was no longer like the bones of a normal human and his muscles were the same.
The system immediately confirmed this.
[Race remains unchanged.]
[Race: Human.]
[Secondary biological structure has synchronized with the Fallen Monster.]
Lian looked at the message for several seconds, so he was still human, his race had not changed but what was now under his human skin could no longer be considered completely human.
The biological structure of his body was no longer the structure a human had, his appearance was still the same, but everything under it now belonged to a monster.
"Interesting, but why did the race remain the same when the biological structure changed?". Lian said quietly and thought for a moment.
If the biological structure changed then the race should change too, unless humans viewed races differently from how the system viewed races.
Then another pressure formed inside his body, in the center of his mana network.
At first the pressure was only a small point, then it turned into something like an empty space.
A "chamber".
It was as if his body was creating a space that was meant to hold something very special.
Mana was pulled toward that point for several seconds.
He frowned for a moment but before he could react, the flow stopped again.
[Monster Core Chamber has been formed.]
[The holder is now capable of forming Monster Cores.]
[Monster Cores: 0]
Lian stared at the new section.
A core.
Monsters had cores, those cores were both a source of power and an important part of their biological and mana structure and their main source of power and energy.
As far as he knew, the cores of powerful monsters also had different abilities, but to be sure he would have to look into this more carefully and research it later.
And now his body also had the ability to form them.
Then the temperature of the room suddenly dropped.
At first he did not even notice and it took several seconds for his eyes to move toward the window, a thin layer of ice had formed in the corner of the glass.
Then it slowly spread and Lian’s breath became white when he breathed out.
But he did not feel any cold himself, not even a little, and white ice started moving from under his feet across the floor of the room.
At first it was only a few centimeters.
Then one meter.
Two meters.
Within a few moments, a large part of the floor was covered by a thin layer of ice.
He looked down, he had not activated any skill yet but the ice was spreading everywhere.
"Is this also part of the evolution?"
There was no answer but the change was not over yet and at the deepest point of his existence, the Ruined Heart beat once.
Thump.
Lian immediately felt it, this heartbeat was different from the physical heart in his body and for a fraction of a second, the inside of the Ruined Heart appeared in his mind.
Five slots.
Four empty slots.
And on the fifth slot, the form of Black Silence and the purple aura around the statue became visible for a moment and then disappeared.
[Unknown factor has interfered with the evolution process.]
[Mutated evolution path stabilized.]
He kept his eyes on the message for several seconds.
"Ruined Heart."
Again.
Every time something unusual happened in his structure, this unknown thing was somewhere inside it.
But once again there was no explanation and it was still unclear why the sudden change had happened.
A few seconds later, all the pain from the changes in his body stopped almost at the same time.
Lian took a calm breath, as if it was finally over and the next moment the system also confirmed it.
[First Evolution completed successfully.]
A very faint smile appeared on his face.
"Finally."
But before he could even check the condition of his own body, the first panel appeared.
Then the second.
The third.
Ten.
Twenty.
And suddenly hundreds of messages opened in front of his eyes.
"Damn... calm down!".
The system seemed to notice his anger and closed all the extra panels and notifications.
"Alright, now one by one."
The first group of messages was related to his level.
[Stored levels are being applied.]
[Level 20 → Level 21.]
[Level 21 → Level 22.]
[Level 22 → Level 23.]
[300 Stat Points.]
[Main Quest reward synchronized.]
[Stat Points: 550.]
He had gained 250 points from the Quest and another 300 points from the three stored levels.
"So now I get 100 stats for every level up." He smiled, compared to the previous number he received for each level up, this was a tenfold increase.
In a way, just through level ups, he could gain around 2,000 stat points by reaching level 40, which was the next level cap.
But these 2,000 stat points were not enough to reach the next maximum stat limit, because the next limit was 10,000 stats.
Of course, this limit was for other classes and especially five-star classes, considering that his limits were different from others, he might need much more stats to reach his next cap.
Lian immediately decided to look at the next messages before worrying about it.
A new status panel opened in front of him.

"That’s it?".
One second passed.
Two seconds.
Then suddenly ...
Thump.
Lian suddenly sat up straight.
His heartbeat was so heavy that he could not only feel it inside his chest, but the dull sound of it also spread through the room.
His eyes narrowed.
Thump.
The second heartbeat was even heavier and pain came with it.
He breathed out hard and pressed his hand against the edge of the bed, something deep inside his bones had started to move; not breaking, but changing.
[Biological reconstruction has begun.]
[Secondary body template selected: Fallen Monster.]
The quiet but continuous sound of bones moving came from inside his body.
His spine slowly stretched.
His vertebrae became denser and stronger, and the bones in his shoulders slowly expanded to the sides.
His ribcage also became slightly larger, as if his body was being redesigned to handle a pressure that a normal human body should never have to handle.
Lian clenched his teeth, the pain was bearable.
After what he had endured in the spiritual space against Black Silence, this was not even close to the worst thing he had experienced.
But it was strange, he could feel every single change.
His muscle tissues began to rebuild.
It was not that his muscles became extremely large; instead, the visible difference was not that great, but every muscle fiber became thicker, denser and several times more efficient.
The power of his contractions increased, his connective tissues became stronger, and his tendons and joints were rebuilt so his body could produce more force without breaking under that force.
Lian closed his right fist, even this simple movement felt different from before.
He felt that if he wanted, he could release much more force from the same muscle he had possessed only a few minutes ago.
"So it wasn’t just the numbers on the panel." He looked at his hand with more interest.
The evolution was changing his body itself.

His arms also became slightly longer.
His shoulders became wider and even when he stood up from the bed, he noticed that his angle of view of the room had changed slightly.
It seemed that a few centimeters had been added to his body, not enough to turn him into a completely different person but enough for him to notice it himself.
His weight had also increased.
Much more than what a few centimeters of extra height and a small amount of muscle should have caused.
